providers.description: Kallyope, Inc. is a New York City clinical-stage biotechnology company, founded in 2015 by Columbia University scientists Charles Zuker, Tom Maniatis and Richard Axel, that translates the biology of the gut-brain axis into medicines. It launched with a $44M Series A and has since raised a $66M Series B, a $112M Series C and a $236M Series D co-led by Mubadala Investment Company and The Column Group, with backers including Bill Gates, Lux Capital, Polaris Partners, Casdin Capital and Alexandria Real Estate Equities. Its proprietary Klarity platform integrates single-cell sequencing, pathway circuit mapping, optogenetics and chemogenetics, proprietary human genetics, mouse and human organoid systems, and small-molecule and peptide chemistry to map the neural circuits underlying migraine and metabolism; lead candidate elismetrep, a TRPM8 blocker, is in Phase 3 development for acute migraine. Kallyope publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDKs, CLI, status page or public GitHub organization, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, MCP or A2A agent-card surface was found on any host. Enrichment probing did find one real, anonymous, read-only REST surface: kallyope.com runs WordPress and exposes the WordPress REST API publicly at https://kallyope.com/wp-json, carrying the company news feed, site pages, media library and a first-party "document" content type of scientific posters, presentations and publications classified by the custom program, event, content-type and document-type taxonomies.

providers.name: Parse Biosciences
providers.description: Parse Biosciences is a Seattle-based life-sciences company that makes Evercode, a split-pool combinatorial barcoding chemistry for single cell and single nuclei RNA sequencing that runs on standard lab equipment rather than a dedicated microfluidics instrument. Its product line spans Evercode WT Mini, WT, WT Mega and WT Penta whole transcriptome kits, Evercode TCR and BCR immune profiling, Evercode Fixation, Evercode WT FFPE, Gene Select and CRISPR Detect, alongside a GigaLab sequencing service for 10M+ cell projects. Data analysis is delivered through Trailmaker, a cloud application that takes Evercode FASTQ files through a pipeline and into interactive downstream analysis. Parse publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract; Trailmaker is an end-user web application whose backend is authenticated with AWS Cognito and undocumented outside the product.

providers.name: Virgo
providers.description: Virgo builds AI foundation models for gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy, targeting gut-mediated diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer. Its flagship model, EndoDINO, was trained on the largest known endoscopy dataset (130,037 videos / ~3.5 billion frames), and EndoML is the GI-specific tooling environment for building clinical and research workflows on top of it. Virgo Cloud provides video capture and management for endoscopy procedures, while Virgo Trials accelerates clinical trials with automatic data capture, endoscopic scoring, placebo-response prediction, subgroup identification, and AI biomarker discovery. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bluejay Therapeutics
providers.description: Bluejay Therapeutics, Inc. was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Redwood City, California, developing treatments for viral hepatitis and liver disease. Its lead asset, brelovitug (BJT-778), is an investigational monoclonal antibody targeting the surface antigen shared by the hepatitis D and hepatitis B viruses; it received U.S. FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation for chronic hepatitis delta and reported a 100% virologic response at week 48 in its Phase 2 monotherapy study before entering the AZURE-2 global Phase 3 trial. The company also advanced a proprietary TLR9 agonist (cavrotolimod), a liver-targeted HBV transcript inhibitor (BJT-628) and a liver-targeted fatty acid synthase inhibitor (BJT-188) toward a combination regimen aimed at functional cure of chronic hepatitis B. Mirum Pharmaceuticals agreed to acquire Bluejay Therapeutics in December 2025 and completed the acquisition on 26 January 2026; the corporate site now serves a single acquisition notice redirecting readers to mirumpharma.com. Bluejay Therapeutics never ran a developer program — no product API, no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDKs, no GitHub organisation and no package-registry presence. The only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the WordPress REST content API behind bluejaytx.com, catalogued here. That surface is notable for outliving the web site it belongs to: the marketing page tree was deleted in the teardown, but the REST API and the post archive still serve all 35 press releases and publication notices from 2021 through 2025 with full text.

providers.name: Tempus AI
providers.description: Tempus AI (NASDAQ: TEM) is a precision medicine company that has built one of the world's largest libraries of de-identified clinical and molecular data, paired with an operating system to make that data accessible for diagnostics and research, starting with cancer. Its products span genomic profiling (xT / xR), AI-enabled clinical tools (Hub, One, Next), the Lens real-world data and agentic AI platform for life sciences, cardiology and radiology AI (ECG-AI, Pixel), and a consumer health app (Olivia). Tempus does not currently publish a self-serve, documented public developer API; integrations are delivered through enterprise and EHR channels (HL7 / FHIR, e.g. Epic) under partner agreements.

providers.name: Unlearn.AI
providers.description: Unlearn.AI provides an AI-powered platform that streamlines clinical trial development using digital twins of patients and advanced data analytics. Its TrialPioneer workspace spans trial planning and simulation (Scout literature search, Hindsight data exploration, SimLab scenario modeling), advanced trial monitoring with anomaly detection, and digital-twin control-arm forecasting that reduces control arm sizes and shortens enrollment. Backed by Insight Partners; no public developer API surface is published.

providers.name: Faro
providers.description: Faro Health is an AI platform for clinical development that helps biopharma and clinical research teams design and execute better studies. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Diego, California, Faro provides study design optimization, automated protocol document authoring, and clinical workflow automation, digitizing and structuring trial protocols so teams can accelerate development without compromising scientific rigor, patient safety, or patient-centricity. Faro is backed by investors including General Catalyst.

providers.name: Leal Health (fka TrialJectory)
providers.description: Leal Health (formerly TrialJectory) is an AI-powered, patient-first decision-support platform that matches cancer patients to advanced treatments and clinical trials. Its patented natural language processing engine reads inclusion/exclusion eligibility criteria and connects to ClinicalTrials.gov so patients, caregivers, and oncologists can self-screen against every recruiting oncology trial in roughly two minutes. For pharma, biotech, and CRO customers, the Patient Match Optimizer SaaS dashboard delivers de-identified, aggregate real-time datasets on patient barriers, motivators, geography, and competitive landscape to shorten enrollment timelines and improve minority representation in trials. The company was founded as TrialJectory by Tzvia Bader (CEO), Avital Gaziel, Guy Gildor, and Noam Geva, later rebranded to Leal Health, and lists a Clifton, New Jersey mailing address. Leal Health operates no public developer program: a live platform API host exists at api.leal.health, but every path behind the root returns HTTP 401 and no OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation is published.

providers.name: nference
providers.description: nference is a healthcare-AI company that builds an agentic intelligence layer for clinical research and drug development. Its nSights platform aggregates and analyzes de-identified multimodal patient data at massive scale — 1.4 billion+ clinical notes, 10 billion+ radiology images, 20 million+ digitized pathology whole-slide images, 12 million+ ECG waveforms, and 100 million+ echocardiogram videos — extracting 30,000+ clinical biomarkers to help life-sciences and health-system partners design patient cohorts, explore patient journeys, annotate data for model development, and run advanced data-science workflows across cardiology, oncology, immunology, rare diseases, neurology, infectious diseases, and nephrology. nference spun out the venture companies Anumana (ECG-based biomarker discovery) and Pramana (digital pathology). The company operates as an enterprise B2B platform with no public self-serve API; it is profiled here for its security, compliance, and governance posture. Backed by Matrix Partners.

providers.name: Pillar Biosciences
providers.description: Pillar Biosciences is a Natick, Massachusetts molecular diagnostics company, founded in 2014, that develops targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) solutions for precision oncology. Its proprietary SLIMamp (Stem-Loop Inhibition Mediated amplification) chemistry enables highly multiplexed, single-tube PCR library preparation from as little as 2.5 ng of DNA, and its oncoReveal panel portfolio covers solid tumour tissue, liquid biopsy, haematologic malignancy, BRCA/HRD/methylation and inherited disease testing, alongside an InheritReveal line and a VersaTile machine-learning panel-design platform. Sequencing data is processed by PiVAT (Pillar Variant Analysis Toolkit), a secondary-analysis pipeline available as a local install or a HIPAA-scoped cloud deployment, with optional OncoKB-powered tertiary reporting. Pillar ships both research-use-only kits and an IVD product line, and raised a $34.5M round led by Illumina in 2025. Pillar publishes no public API, SDK or developer program; PiVAT's integration surface is bioinformatics file formats (FASTQ, BAM, VCF, PDF) behind a customer login.

providers.name: Pluton Biosciences
providers.description: Pluton Biosciences is a microbial discovery company that uses a proprietary Discovery Platform - high-throughput soil microbiome screening combined with computational analysis - to find naturally occurring microbial consortia for agriculture and carbon sequestration. Its lead product is a Biological Nitrogen System: photosynthetic microbial consortia that operate at the soil surface to fix atmospheric nitrogen and mobilize phosphorus. Pluton is a research-and-product company, not an API company; it has no public developer portal. Partnership and licensing inquiries are handled directly.

providers.name: 10x Genomics
providers.description: 10x Genomics is a life sciences technology company building instruments, reagents, and software that resolve biology at single-cell and spatial resolution. Its Chromium platform delivers single-cell gene expression, immune profiling, and multiomic analysis; its Visium and Xenium platforms deliver spatial transcriptomics and in situ single-cell spatial biology. The company supports researchers with analysis software (Cell Ranger, Space Ranger, Xenium Onboard Analysis, Loupe Browser), a cloud analysis platform, and open datasets. 10x Genomics does not publish a general-purpose public REST developer API; its developer surface is command-line analysis pipelines, file-format tooling, and open-source repositories on GitHub.

providers.name: Evidation Health
providers.description: Evidation Health is a San Mateo, California digital health company, founded in 2012, that measures health in everyday life and runs permissioned real-world data research at scale. Its consumer app and platform — Achievement — rewards members for connecting wearables, apps and health records, and its enterprise Research & Engagement Platform gives life-sciences, payer, government and non-profit customers eConsent and onboarding, ePRO and survey capture, passive and active device monitoring, program analytics, and participant education. Evidation combines data from sources including Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin, Dexcom and EHR/claims records (via a partnership with 1upHealth's FHIR-based Patient Connect, and with HealthVerity), and has enabled 175+ virtual real-world studies and 70+ peer-reviewed publications. Evidation publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its programmatic surfaces are the member app backend and enterprise data deliveries, neither of which is publicly documented.

providers.name: Ultimagenomics
providers.description: Ultima Genomics develops high-throughput, low-cost DNA sequencing platforms built on a novel semiconductor-inspired architecture, aimed at driving the cost of a genome dramatically down to unlock population-scale genomics. Its systems support germline and somatic (oncology/MRD) sequencing, single-cell and spatial workflows, methylation/epigenomics, and proteomics, and integrate with an open ecosystem of third-party library-prep providers (10x Genomics, Olink). Rather than a public REST API, Ultima exposes its developer surface as open-source bioinformatics tooling and analysis pipelines: a large GitHub organization (Ultimagen) of UG-adapted variant callers and genomics utilities (GATK, Picard, STAR forks, ugbio-utils) and AWS HealthOmics WDL workflows for running cost-effective secondary analysis in the cloud.

providers.name: Rivia
providers.description: Rivia is a clinical trial intelligence platform based in Zurich, Switzerland that unifies fragmented clinical trial data from any vendor into a single, structured foundation for biotech and pharmaceutical companies. Its products include Rivia Core (data harmonization), Rivia Detect (AI agents that continuously identify and resolve data quality issues), and Rivia Spark (visual analytics with a conversational AI assistant for exploring trial data through natural language). The platform supports medical and clinical science, safety monitoring, clinical operations, and executive oversight use cases, promising go-live in under 20 days. Rivia raised a $15M Series A and is backed by investors including Earlybird and Speedinvest. The company is a sales-led enterprise platform with no public developer portal or API surface as of this profile; onboarding is via demo request.

providers.name: GT Medical Technologies
providers.description: GT Medical Technologies, Inc. is a Tempe, Arizona medical device company founded by brain tumor specialists to commercialize GammaTile, an FDA-cleared, bioabsorbable collagen implant embedded with Cesium-131 radiation seeds. Surgeons place the tiles directly into the resection cavity at the time of brain tumor removal, delivering immediate, targeted radiation without the weeks-long healing delay conventional external beam radiotherapy requires. The company sells a physical, prescription-only implant to hospitals and neurosurgical centers through a direct sales force and a Salesforce-based ordering portal; it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Infera
providers.description: Infera is an AI-native laboratory automation platform (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) that converts plain-English descriptions of experiments into validated, instrument-ready runs across the lab instruments a team already owns. It compiles protocols into vendor-specific scripts for liquid handlers, plate readers, mass spectrometers, thermocyclers and centrifuges (Opentrons, Hamilton, Tecan and others), limits AI to initial drafts while keeping downstream steps deterministic and fully checkable, supports both automated and manual bench procedures, and maintains an end-to-end audit trail of protocols and runs. Founded in San Francisco by Troy Zhang and Chloe Sow.

providers.name: Axsome Therapeutics
providers.description: Axsome Therapeutics (NASDAQ: AXSM) is a biopharmaceutical company developing and delivering novel therapies for the management of central nervous system (CNS) disorders. Headquartered at One World Trade Center, New York, Axsome markets three FDA-approved products — Auvelity (dextromethorphan-bupropion) for major depressive disorder, Sunosi (solriamfetol) for excessive daytime sleepiness in narcolepsy and obstructive sleep apnea, and Symbravo (meloxicam-rizatriptan) for the acute treatment of migraine — and is advancing a pipeline including AXS-05 for Alzheimer's disease agitation and smoking cessation, AXS-12 (reboxetine) for narcolepsy, and AXS-14 (esreboxetine) for fibromyalgia. Axsome operates a corporate website and product / HCP microsites but does not expose a public developer API surface; this profile catalogs corporate, product, regulatory, and investor touchpoints rather than programmatic interfaces.

providers.name: Dragonfly Therapeutics
providers.description: Dragonfly Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Waltham, Massachusetts, founded in 2016 by Tyler Jacks, Bill Haney and David Raulet to develop natural killer (NK) cell-based immunotherapies. Its proprietary TriNKET (Tri-specific NK cell Engager Therapy) and cytokine engager platforms produce molecules that bind both a tumor or disease antigen and an NK cell activating receptor, recruiting innate and adaptive immunity against cancer, autoimmune disease, fibrosis and neuro-inflammation. Lead clinical candidate DF1001 targets HER2 in advanced solid tumors, and the platform is licensed under multi-target collaborations with AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, Merck and Gilead. Dragonfly is a therapeutics developer rather than a software company: it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable API contract. The only agent-readable surfaces on its own host are the llms.txt and Model Context Protocol endpoint automatically provisioned by its Wix website platform.

providers.name: Lantern
providers.description: Lantern (legal entity Employer Direct Healthcare, LLC dba Lantern Specialty Care) is a US specialty care platform that connects members with high-quality, lower-cost care for surgery, cancer and infusion therapy — the complex, high-cost episodes that account for roughly half of healthcare spending. Founded in 2011 as SurgeryPlus and later expanded into cancer and infusion care, Lantern sells to employers, public-sector employers, labor union trusts, health plans and benefits consultants, pairing a hand-selected "Network of Excellence" of specialists with dedicated care teams that navigate a member end to end through a treatment journey. Lantern is backed by Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass Lantern publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable specification, SDKs or discovery surface — this profile captures its public company, trust and security posture only.

providers.name: Spiber
providers.description: Spiber Inc. is a Japanese biotechnology and advanced-materials company founded in 2007 and headquartered in Tsuruoka, Yamagata Prefecture, Japan. Spiber develops Brewed Protein materials — structural proteins produced by precision fermentation of plant-derived sugars using engineered microbes, then spun into fibers, resins, and films as animal-free, petroleum-free alternatives to silk, wool, cashmere, leather, and synthetic polymers. The company operates fermentation plants in Japan, Thailand, and the United States and supplies apparel, outdoor, automotive, and consumer brands, alongside a research program in synthetic biology, polymer science, and life-cycle assessment. Spiber is a materials manufacturer rather than a software vendor and publishes no developer program, developer portal, SDKs, or product API; the only machine-readable HTTP surface it serves is the read-only WordPress REST content API behind its corporate website.

providers.name: CaaMTech
providers.description: CaaMTech is a pharmaceutical drug discovery company in Issaquah, Washington, founded by Dr. Andrew Chadeayne, engineering next-generation psychedelic-inspired small-molecule therapeutics for mental health conditions. It synthesizes and characterizes novel tryptamines, screens natural and synthetic compounds for safety and efficacy, publishes fundamental crystallographic and pharmacological research, and builds a patent portfolio around the results. CaaMTech operates no developer program and publishes no product API; the only machine-readable surface on caam.tech is the standard WordPress REST API that serves the company site, which does make its research updates, pages and media programmatically readable without credentials, alongside an authenticated WordPress MCP adapter endpoint.

providers.name: Syneos Health
providers.description: Syneos Health is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Syneos Health API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Viome
providers.description: Viome (Viome Life Sciences) is a health technology company founded in 2016 by Naveen Jain that uses metatranscriptomic RNA sequencing — a technique originally developed for biodefense at Los Alamos National Laboratory — combined with artificial intelligence to measure active gene expression across the gut microbiome, oral microbiome, and human cells. From at-home stool, saliva, and finger-prick blood samples the company produces over 50 health scores across eight categories (BioAge, Gut Health, Oral Health, Energy, Inflammaging, Mood/Memory/Focus, Immunity, and Heart and Metabolic Health), personalized food recommendations across more than 370 foods, and custom-blended precision supplements and biotics. Products include the Full Body Intelligence, Gut Intelligence, and Oral Health Intelligence tests plus the CancerDetect saliva screening test for oral and throat cancer. Viome operates in over 100 countries, publishes peer-reviewed research in NPJ Genomic Medicine, iScience, and Microbiome, and runs a Life Sciences research division. Viome publishes no public developer API or machine-readable API contract; its consumer app at my.viome.com is served by an undocumented private backend, and the only agent-facing artifact the company publishes is a curated llms.txt.

providers.name: Blackrock Neurotech
providers.description: Blackrock Neurotech is a Salt Lake City, Utah based neurotechnology company that designs and manufactures implantable brain-computer interface (BCI) systems and the research instrumentation around them. Its platform pairs Utah Array microelectrode arrays and the next-generation Neuralace interface with the NeuroPort, Cerebus and CerePlex Direct neural signal processors, the CereStim stimulation system, and the Central software suite for acquisition, visualization and offline spike sorting. The company reports more than 19 years of human clinical study, 1,000+ research institutions served and 2,000+ published studies using its hardware. Blackrock does not publish a public web API: its programmatic surface is a set of device and file-format libraries distributed as downloads and GitHub source (cbSDK C++ API, cbMEX MATLAB API, CereStim API, brPY/brpylib Python data loader, and the NPMK MATLAB toolkit). Enrichment probing on 2026-08-02 found no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, MCP, agent card, llms.txt or /.well-known/ discovery surface on any Blackrock host.

providers.name: Field Medical
providers.description: Field Medical, Inc. is a Carlsbad, California clinical-stage cardiac electrophysiology company founded in 2022 by Dr. Steven Mickelsen to build a second-generation pulsed field ablation (PFA) platform. Its FieldForce Ablation System pairs a focal catheter design with proprietary FieldBending energy and is positioned as the first PFA system purpose-built for ventricular arrhythmia ablation, with atrial fibrillation applications in development. The company holds FDA Breakthrough Device Designation and a place in the FDA TAP Pilot Program for its VT indication, has published first-in-human VCAS data in Circulation, and has raised roughly $75M across Series A and Series B. Field Medical is a medical device manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public REST/GraphQL API and no SDKs. Its only machine-readable public surface is the llms.txt and anonymous site MCP endpoint that its Wix-hosted corporate website serves.

providers.name: Sable Bio
providers.description: Sable Bio is a London-based drug-safety intelligence company building an AI-augmented platform, Sable Target Intelligence, that helps toxicologists, informaticians, and drug discovery scientists assess and mitigate target safety risk earlier in the drug development process. The platform aggregates and quantifies clinical, genetic, experimental, and literature evidence into a unified Target Safety Intelligence surface so safety teams can systematically prioritize and de-risk drug targets faster than traditional manual review. The company is headquartered in East London (Runway East Aldgate) and is backed by Episode One, Seedcamp, and MMC Ventures. Sable Bio was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass it operates a public marketing and product site with a Vanta-hosted trust center but does not yet publish a developer-facing API, documentation, or data-access surface.

providers.name: Picnicai
providers.description: PicnicHealth (PicnicAI; legally Mission Health Labs, Inc.) is a San Francisco health-data company and Y Combinator alum (S14, founded 2014) that turns patients' fragmented medical records into structured, research-ready real-world datasets. Its consumer product gives patients a unified timeline of care across every provider, while PicnicResearch supplies de-identified, ontology-mapped (RxNorm, SNOMED, LOINC, ICD) real-world data to biopharma via AI extraction plus human clinical curation. The primary developer surface is a first-party R package distributed through PicnicHealth's own Posit/RStudio Package Manager for importing and visualizing research cohorts.

providers.name: Radical Health
providers.description: Radical Health is a Khosla Ventures-backed healthcare AI company that produces personalized, expert-reviewed cancer treatment reports for patients in the United States. Its platform ingests a patient's medical records and synthesizes oncology research, clinical trials, and prior patient outcomes into a tailored report within days, drawing on 5.3 million research papers, 11.8 million patient journeys, 20,000 treatment options, and 48,800+ active US clinical trials. The service pairs an always-on AI nurse navigator ("Alice") with human oncology oversight from institutions including UCLA, Johns Hopkins, Stanford, and Kaiser Permanente, and connects to 70,000+ US healthcare institutions (Epic, Kaiser, Ascension, HCA, Medicare) for records access. Reports are informational and educational only, not medical advice. Radical Health is HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II certified and operates as a consumer subscription product ($110/month with a 7-day free trial); it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: BillionToOne
providers.description: BillionToOne is a molecular diagnostics company using proprietary single-molecule Quantitative Counting Template (QCT) technology to detect disease at the DNA level from cell-free DNA. Its Unity prenatal screening suite (Unity Complete, Unity Confirm, and Unity fetal antigen tests) delivers non-invasive prenatal testing from maternal blood at nine weeks, and its Northstar oncology line (Northstar Select and Northstar Response) provides liquid-biopsy therapy selection and real-time treatment-response monitoring. BillionToOne integrates with electronic medical records through a collaboration with Epic and delivers results through its provider and patient portals. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global, Norwest Venture Partners, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Power
providers.description: Power (withpower.com) is a clinical-trial search and matching platform that helps patients find and enroll in research studies. It maintains a database of tens of thousands of active clinical trials searchable by condition, location, and drug type, and connects patients, providers, research coordinators, and trial sponsors. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Anthemis and CRV; no public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: TMRW Life Sciences *
providers.description: TMRW Life Sciences is a medical technology company that builds the world's first and only FDA-cleared automated platform for the safe management and storage of frozen eggs and embryos used in IVF and fertility treatment. Its cryo-storage hardware combines robotic specimen handling with digital tracking, chain-of-custody monitoring, and real-time visibility for fertility clinics and their patients, replacing manual, paper-based handling of irreplaceable reproductive tissue. Deployed at clinic networks including CCRM Fertility, Pinnacle Fertility, RFC, and IVIRMA North America. TMRW is a private company backed by GV (Google Ventures). It publishes a Security & Trust program (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27018) but does not expose a public developer portal, API, or specification surface.

providers.name: OncoC4
providers.description: OncoC4, Inc. is a privately held, late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Rockville, Maryland, founded in 2020, with subsidiaries in Nanjing, Guangzhou and Beijing, China, and Brisbane, Australia. The company discovers and develops novel biologics for the treatment of cancer, working across immune checkpoints including CTLA-4, CD24, PD-1/VEGF and the Siglec family, with monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates and CAR T-cell therapies. Its lead clinical candidate is gotistobart (BNT316/ONC-392), a next-generation anti-CTLA-4 antibody co-developed and commercialized with BioNTech under a strategic collaboration announced in March 2023. OncoC4 publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or developer documentation; its corporate website runs on the Umbraco CMS, which serves a default OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 discovery document and JWKS for CMS member authentication.

providers.name: Foresight Diagnostics
providers.description: Foresight Diagnostics is a CLIA-certified, CAP-accredited cancer diagnostics company founded in 2020 in Boulder, Colorado by Stanford physicians and scientists, and since February 2026 a wholly owned subsidiary of Natera. Its Foresight CLARITY minimal residual disease (MRD) platform is a liquid-biopsy test powered by proprietary PhasED-Seq phased-variant sequencing and bioinformatics, detecting circulating tumor DNA at an analytical sensitivity below one part per million across lymphoma, lung and other solid tumors. The company sells laboratory testing services to biopharma sponsors, academic researchers and clinicians rather than software: it operates a central laboratory and publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: sophiagenetics
providers.description: SOPHiA GENETICS (NASDAQ SOPH) is a healthcare technology company democratizing data-driven medicine through its cloud-based SOPHiA DDM Platform, which analyzes genomic, radiomic, and multimodal data to support clinicians and researchers across oncology, hereditary disorders, rare diseases, and precision medicine. The platform spans SOPHiA DDM for Genomics, Multimodal, and Radiomics, plus Alamut Visual Plus for variant interpretation and the OncoPortal knowledge base. The product is delivered as a login-gated SaaS platform; no public developer API or portal is currently published.

providers.name: Octave Bioscience
providers.description: Octave Bioscience is a precision neurology company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, that develops blood-based multi-protein biomarker tests for chronic neurological disease. Its commercially available Octave Multiple Sclerosis Disease Activity (MSDA) Test measures a panel of serum proteins to produce a quantitative disease activity score used alongside clinical and imaging assessment, and is available across the United States through a strategic collaboration with Quest Diagnostics. The company is also developing a Multiple Sclerosis Disease Progression (MSDP) test and a Parkinson's disease biomarker assay supported by a Michael J. Fox Foundation grant. Octave publishes a public trust center documenting HITRUST, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, HIPAA and GDPR posture, but operates no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Seer
providers.description: Seer, Inc. (NASDAQ: SEER) is a Redwood City, California life-sciences company pioneering proteomics, the large-scale study of proteins. Its Proteograph Product Suite pairs engineered nanoparticles with automated sample preparation and mass spectrometry to profile tens of thousands of proteins across biological samples at scale, and its cloud-based Proteograph Analysis System (PAS) software processes and interprets the resulting proteomic data for pharmaceutical, biopharma, and academic research. Seer exposes no public developer API; its software surface is the login-gated PAS platform delivered to customers of the Proteograph suite.

providers.name: Tilda Research
providers.description: Tilda Research deploys AI Teammates that perform the operational work of clinical trials for sponsors, CROs, and research sites — automating study workflows, data capture, trial monitoring, and regulatory compliance. Founded by Ram Yalamanchili and backed by 8VC, the company operates the Tilda Sense clinical-research platform (sense.tilda.bio) and advertises SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance via a Vanta-hosted trust center, but publishes no public developer program or API documentation.

providers.name: Neurelis
providers.description: Neurelis, Inc. is a privately held San Diego neuroscience and specialty pharmaceutical company founded in 2007 that licenses, develops and commercializes therapies for epilepsy, psychiatry and other central nervous system disorders with high unmet need. Its lead commercial product is VALTOCO (diazepam nasal spray), an FDA-approved acute treatment for intermittent, stereotypic episodes of frequent seizure activity (seizure clusters) in adult and pediatric patients two years of age and older, built on Intravail transmucosal absorption-enhancement technology acquired with Aegis Therapeutics. Neurelis also holds the ProTek and Hydrogel drug-delivery platforms, licenses Intravail to partners such as ARS Pharmaceuticals and Dr. Reddy's/Upsher-Smith, and is advancing the NRL-1049 and NRL-1004 pipeline programs. Neurelis publishes no developer program, no public API and no machine-readable API contract; its only agent-facing machine-readable surface is a set of llms.txt documents served on its corporate, product and patient-support properties.

providers.name: Francis Medical
providers.description: Francis Medical is a privately held medical device company headquartered in Maple Grove, Minnesota, founded in 2018 by Michael Hoey and named for his father, who died of prostate cancer in 1991. It develops the Vanquish Water Vapor Ablation System, a transurethral outpatient platform that ablates targeted prostate tissue using the thermal energy stored in sterile water vapor delivered in short bursts through a catheter, with the aim of treating localized disease while avoiding the incontinence and sexual dysfunction associated with radical prostatectomy and radiation. The company received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation in 2023 and 510(k) clearance for prostate tissue ablation in December 2025, and it is running the VAPOR 1 and VAPOR 2 clinical studies alongside a long-term registry; it has signalled intent to extend the same water vapor platform to bladder and kidney cancer. Francis Medical has raised roughly $160 million to date, including an $80 million Series C in January 2025 co-led by Solas BioVentures and Arboretum Ventures, with earlier participation from Coloplast. It is led by president and CEO Mike Kujak. Francis Medical publishes a physician locator, an electronic instructions-for-use (eIFU) library and a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy for its devices and embedded software, but operates no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Seed Health
providers.description: Seed Health is a microbiome science company founded in 2017 by Ara Katz and Raja Dhir, headquartered in Los Angeles County, California. It develops and sells clinically studied probiotic, prebiotic and synbiotic consumer products — most notably the DS-01 Daily Synbiotic, the PDS-08 Pediatric Daily Synbiotic and the VS-01 Vaginal Synbiotic — direct to consumers via a subscription commerce site at seed.com, alongside SeedLabs, its environmental and applied-microbiology research arm. Seed publishes a substantial public science, editorial (Cultured) and help-center surface, and maintains a small public GitHub organization, but it operates no public developer program: there is no developer portal, no published API reference, no OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI or MCP contract, and its internal storefront API paths are explicitly disallowed in robots.txt. Its practitioner program is fulfilled through Fullscript and email rather than through any integration surface.

providers.name: Digbi Health
providers.description: Digbi Health is a digital therapeutics company delivering a precision-biology virtual clinic for food-related and inflammatory illnesses — obesity, cardiometabolic disease, type 2 diabetes, digestive disorders (IBS, GERD), MSK chronic pain, PCOS, sleep and mental health. Its FoodRx program combines host-genetics and gut-microbiome testing with app-based coaching, precision nutrition, and pre/probiotic therapies, delivered to members through health plans and employers. Digbi Health is backed by Accel. The company operates a consumer-facing storefront and member app rather than a public developer API; this profile captures the public web, agent, and security surfaces observable at digbihealth.com.

providers.name: Edison Scientific
providers.description: Edison Scientific is an AI research company building Kosmos, an autonomous "AI Scientist" for R&D teams in drug discovery and biopharma. Kosmos reads scientific literature, analyzes experimental data, generates and tests hypotheses, and executes research workflows autonomously, collaborating with scientists through tools like Slack and Teams. The model-agnostic platform spans the drug development lifecycle from target identification through clinical development and filing, learning from proprietary organizational and scientific data. Edison Labs publishes open science research including the PaperQA line of multimodal deep research agents. The company is backed by Spark Capital and maintains an enterprise Trust Center with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture. No public developer API is published at this time.

providers.name: SolveBio
providers.description: SolveBio is a platform for biomedical and genomic datasets that lets developers query, harmonize, and automate bioinformatics workflows over curated reference data through a REST API and first-party client libraries (Python, JavaScript, Ruby, and R). SolveBio has been rebranded to QuartzBio, a Precision for Medicine company: the solvebio.com website now redirects to quartz.bio, the legacy API is served as the QuartzBio EDP REST API on per-customer instance hosts, and the SolveBio SDKs are being deprecated in favor of the quartzbio packages (Python client end of maintenance 2026-03-31). Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched from its public GitHub organization and package registries.

providers.name: Amgen
providers.description: Amgen is committed to unlocking the potential of biology for patients suffering from serious illnesses by discovering, developing, manufacturing and delivering innovative human therapeutics. As a pioneer in biotechnology since 1980, Amgen uses living cells to make biologic medicines addressing cardiovascular metabolic conditions, oncology, inflammation, rare diseases, and bone health, operating in approximately 100 countries worldwide.

providers.name: DeepScribe
providers.description: DeepScribe is a San Francisco, California ambient AI medical scribe company that automates clinical documentation and coding for specialty healthcare providers. Founded in 2017 (incorporated 2019) by Matthew Ko, Kairui Zeng, and Akilesh Bapu, DeepScribe captures the natural conversation between clinician and patient and produces structured clinical notes inside the provider's existing EHR workflow. The platform is HIPAA-compliant and is deployed across more than 1,500 healthcare organizations, with reported traction of 8 million+ visits captured and a 99.92% note-satisfaction rating. Core products include the AI Medical Scribe (ambient documentation), SmartPrep (pre-visit intelligence), AI Coding (E/M, ICD-10, and HCC automation), Customization Studio (provider-specific note personalization), and DeepScribe Assist (point-of-care insights). DeepScribe ships bi-directional EHR integrations with Epic, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, AdvancedMD, drchrono, ModMed, Flatiron (OncoEMR), Ontada (iKnowMed Generation 2), and Objective Medical Systems, with a focused practice in oncology, cardiology, gastroenterology, neurology, orthopedics, urology, and value-based care. The company partners with AWS, Anthropic, Deloitte, and Panda Health for infrastructure, model, and go-to-market support. DeepScribe is sold as enterprise SaaS through a contact-sales motion; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release, and authentication into the clinician workspace happens through canvas.deepscribe.ai.

providers.name: Auxilius
providers.description: Auxilius is R&D finance automation software for biopharmaceutical companies, purpose-built to manage clinical trial finances. The platform automates clinical expense accruals and financial close with built-in audit controls, tracks investigator grant spend by mapping patient-visit data to site contracts, and models and re-forecasts study spend as trial conditions change. It integrates with clinical (Medrio, Veeva), financial (Oracle NetSuite, Workday, SAP, QuickBooks), procurement (Coupa, Bill.com), and planning (Planful, Anaplan) systems, delivering variance analysis, automated reconciliation, and audit-ready role-based approval workflows. Auxilius is SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 compliant and is used by 100+ biopharma companies. It is backed by Bain Capital Ventures. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Culture Biosciences
providers.description: Culture Biosciences is a South San Francisco TechBio company that builds cloud-connected bioreactor systems and bioprocess development services for cell culture. Its platform pairs automated single-use bioreactors (250mL bench-scale and 5L, plus the Stratyx mobile bioreactor) with Console, a cloud-native software product for real-time monitoring, experiment management, data analytics, and remote collaboration. Through its Nexxys services group the company runs clone/strain/construct screening, process characterization, process development, and bioprocess modeling and simulation for customers working on synthetic biology, protein therapeutics, and viral vectors. Culture Biosciences lets teams outsource and scale bioreactor experiments without scaling their own lab infrastructure. Backed by DCVC, Northpond Ventures, Synthesis Capital, S32, and Cultivian Sandbox Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; the company operates the Console cloud platform but does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Tasso
providers.description: Tasso, Inc. designs painless, needle-free blood collection devices and an end-to-end logistics platform for decentralized and at-home blood sampling. Its product line includes Tasso+ for capillary whole-blood collection, the Tasso-M20/Mini for dried blood microsampling, and the tile-T20 for liquid serum and plasma, enabling remote specimen collection for clinical trials, patient screening, diagnostics, and research. Tasso pairs the hardware with kitting, shipping, and sample-return logistics and is cited in over 100 peer-reviewed publications. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Fidocure
providers.description: FidoCure is a translational precision-medicine service for canine cancer, developed by One Health Company and backed by a16z. It combines next-generation genomic sequencing of a dog's tumor at a CLIA-certified (human-grade) lab with tumor profiling and an AI-driven data platform to identify cancer-driving mutations, then recommends personalized targeted therapeutics that veterinarians can prescribe. FidoCure has guided treatment for thousands of dogs across roughly 1,350 clinics and maintains the largest proprietary canine cancer dataset, underpinning peer-reviewed research with Stanford, the Broad Institute, Tufts, and the University of Georgia. FidoCure operates as a veterinarian-facing clinical service rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its public identity, portal, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nectar
providers.description: Nectar (Nectar Life Sciences) is a hybrid, vertically-integrated allergy care platform combining at-home testing with in-person clinical care. Patients can self-test for dozens of indoor and outdoor environmental allergens using mail-in home kits, then receive personalized treatment including sublingual immunotherapy (allergy drops), prescription nasal sprays, rescue inhalers, and allergy shots. Its flagship Nectar Allergy Center in New York City treats adults and children for environmental allergies, asthma, food allergies, and eczema, alongside virtual telehealth appointments. Nectar is a consumer healthcare provider with no public developer API surface; it was backed by Obvious Ventures, Juxtapose, and Harmony Partners.

providers.name: Atrandi
providers.description: Atrandi Biosciences (founded 2016 in Lithuania as Droplet Genomics) is a life-sciences tools company building droplet-microfluidic platforms and its patented Semi-Permeable Capsule (SPC) technology for single-cell analysis. SPCs isolate individual cells while letting reagents diffuse freely, enabling complex multi-step single-cell genomics, multiomics, and microbial whole-genome sequencing workflows. Atrandi ships instruments (Flux, Onyx, Styx), application kits, and consumables used by 200+ research groups worldwide. The company is a wet-lab instrumentation and consumables vendor and publishes no public developer API; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and enriched with verified public identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Flatiron Health
providers.description: Flatiron Health is a healthcare technology company focused on oncology, combining real-world data from millions of cancer patients with software and AI to support life sciences research and clinical care. Its platforms include OncoEMR and OncoCloud for oncology practices, Flatiron Vessel (clinical research EDC, formerly Protocol First) and Clinical Pipe for clinical trials, and real-world evidence products for life sciences. Flatiron data has informed thousands of peer-reviewed publications and regulatory submissions. The company is part of Roche.

providers.name: Photys Therapeutics
providers.description: Photys Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Waltham, Massachusetts advancing proximity-based, targeted protein modulation medicines across three heterobifunctional modalities: PROTAC-based protein degradation (lead program PHT-776/HPB-143, an oral IRAK4 degrader that entered Phase I in August 2026 for autoimmune and inflammatory disease), PHICS (Phosphorylation-Inducing Chimeric Small molecules, partnered with Novo Nordisk since December 2024 for cardiometabolic disease), and tPRIME for restoring protective proteins such as p53 Y220C in oncology. Founded in 2022 out of Amit Choudhary's lab at the Broad Institute and Brigham and Women's Hospital with a $75M Series A led by MPM Capital and Longwood Fund. Photys operates no developer program and publishes no OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, WSDL or gRPC contract; its only machine-readable, agent-facing surface is the platform-provided Wix Site MCP endpoint served from its own host at www.photys.com/_api/mcp, which answers anonymously with nine tools over site content and business details.

providers.name: Ataraxis
providers.description: Ataraxis AI is a precision-medicine company building clinical AI foundation models that make disease predictable, beginning with oncology. Founded in 2022 by Jan Witowski, MD, PhD, and Krzysztof Geras, PhD (both formerly of NYU), Ataraxis trains multi-modal AI on hundreds of millions of pathology images to assess disease aggressiveness and predict cancer recurrence, treatment response, and survival. Its first product, Ataraxis Breast, is an AI-native, clinically validated prognostic and predictive test suite for breast cancer (Recurrence Risk, Chemotherapy Benefit, and Neoadjuvant Response) delivering same-day results without exhausting physical tissue. The company is backed by Obvious Ventures, AIX Ventures, and Giant Ventures, and advised by Turing Award winner Yann LeCun. Ataraxis operates a clinician portal rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Dyno Therapeutics
providers.description: Dyno Therapeutics is an AI-driven biotechnology company in Watertown, Massachusetts that combines machine learning with high-throughput in vivo experimentation to engineer adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors for gene therapy. Its CapsidMap platform designs novel AAV capsids optimized for tissue targeting, immune evasion, manufacturability, and payload packaging, advanced through partnerships with pharmaceutical companies. Dyno also open-sources protein-design tooling for the research community, including the dyno-phi CLI for its Phi protein-design platform and the Psi-1 de novo binder-design model.

providers.name: Citruslabs
providers.description: Citruslabs is a clinical research organization (CRO) that designs and runs clinical trials, consumer perception studies, and randomized controlled trials for consumer health brands across supplements, skincare, pet health, food and beverage, longevity, and women's health. It handles IRB approval, protocol design, participant recruitment, decentralized data collection, and statistical analysis, then turns results into regulator-reviewed, marketing-ready product claims for retailers, advertising, and packaging. Studies range from DIY consumer perception studies to full randomized controlled trials, typically completing in four to sixteen weeks.

providers.name: Five Lives
providers.description: Five Lives is a health-technology company building evidence-based digital tools for dementia prevention and brain health for adults aged 50 and over. Founded by former Peak brain-training leaders Xavier Louis (CEO) and Sylvain Piquet (COO), the fully remote company operates two consumer mobile apps: Five Lives Brain Health, a prevention app available since 2021 with cognitive tests, brain games, and lifestyle tracking across five pillars (nutrition, sleep, physical activity, mood and social connection, and mental stimulation); and Five Lives Care, an evidence-based memory and autonomy programme for people aged 60+ launched in January 2026 and developed with leading memory centres in the UK and France. Its work draws on the FINGER study and the Lancet Commission's modifiable dementia risk factors, with research partners including the University of Oxford, Trinity College Dublin, the FINGER Brain Health Institute, Dementias Platform UK, and the Gerontopole d'Ile de France. Backed by Speedinvest. Five Lives does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Lindus Health
providers.description: Lindus Health is a next-generation contract research organization (CRO) that runs clinical trials end to end for biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors. It pairs Citrus, an AI-assisted trial operating system connecting patient identification through final data capture, with centralized patient identification and enrollment (AI-powered EHR querying, digital pre-screening, centralized patient support), flexible site models spanning site-based, hybrid and fully virtual delivery, and integrated clinical services from protocol design through database lock. Its platform surface covers EDC, eSource, ePRO/eCOA, eConsent and CTMS. The company operates across the US, UK and Europe with APAC partnerships, employs over 160 staff, and works in cardiometabolic, respiratory, psychiatry, women's health and dermatology. Commercial engagements are performance-based with milestone pricing. Lindus Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal or API documentation; its public technical footprint is two open-source CDISC clinical-data repositories.

providers.name: Paradigm Health
providers.description: Paradigm Health is an AI-native clinical trial platform connecting biopharma sponsors with a research-ready provider network spanning roughly 2,100 care locations across the United States. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, the company operates infrastructure implemented at healthcare provider organizations to make clinical research part of routine care. Its Study Conduct platform captures data directly from electronic health records and other structured and unstructured sources, algorithmically evaluates FDA-defined data points in real time, and transmits the critical safety and efficacy signals needed for regulatory determinations to trial sponsors and the FDA. Paradigm serves both trial sponsors (protocol optimization, feasibility and site selection, patient identification and enrollment, data collection and delivery, post-approval evidence) and research sites. The company acquired Flatiron Health's Clinical Research business, announced a research collaboration with the U.S. FDA, and is backed by ARCH Venture Partners, General Catalyst, and GV. Paradigm currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its identity, legal, and published security/compliance surface.

providers.name: Q Bio
providers.description: Q Bio is a Redwood City, California health-technology company offering the Q Exam and the Q Bio Health Dashboard, sold directly at its clinic and through enterprise partners. The Q Exam is a comprehensive preventive-health assessment that combines whole-body non-contrast MRI, 120+ blood biomarkers, analysis of 163 risk-relevant genes, wearable data, medical history, and board-certified physician review into a single longitudinal health baseline. Imaging is quantified by Constellation, the company's FDA-cleared AI image-analysis software that segments organs and measures anatomy, and results are stored in the Q Bio Health Dashboard for year-over-year comparison. Q Bio is a portfolio company of a16z. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Enzo Biochem
providers.description: Enzo Biochem, Inc. (operating as Enzo Life Sciences) is a life sciences company specializing in labeling and detection technologies for biomedical research and drug development. Trading under the tagline "Scientists Enabling Scientists," Enzo develops and manufactures research reagents and assays including AMPIVIEW RNA probes for in-situ hybridization and FISH, antibodies, ELISA immunoassays, immunohistochemistry (IHC) products, and CELLESTIAL cell-based assays. Its biopharma arm provides drug discovery services, target identification and validation, assay development, in vitro toxicology, and GMP manufacturing. Products are sold through an online catalog and account portal at enzo.com rather than a public developer API. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub company lead and enriched with the identity, website, and domain-security posture that could be verified from public sources.

providers.name: Inductive Bio
providers.description: Inductive Bio is an AI-powered virtual lab for small molecule drug discovery, based in New York and founded in 2022 by Josh Haimson and Ben Birnbaum (both formerly of Flatiron Health). The company pairs medicinal chemists with machine learning to run millions of in silico ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Toxicity) experiments, surface the strongest compound hypotheses, and accelerate the path to development candidates. Its Beacon-1 models took first place in both the 2025 Polaris/ASAP and 2026 OpenADMET/ExpansionRx blind ADMET competitions, and are delivered through the Compass software platform (with the Indy AI chemistry assistant) and an Embedded Experts services offering. Inductive Bio operates a pre-competitive ADMET data consortium, is SOC 2 compliant, and is backed by a16z, Lux Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Obvious Ventures, Character, and S32. Compass is enterprise/partner software; it exposes an API to partner teams but publishes no public, self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK.

providers.name: OneHealthCompany
providers.description: The One Health Company is a Palo Alto veterinary precision-oncology company, best known for its FidoCure platform, that brings human-grade precision cancer medicine to dogs. FidoCure sequences a dog's tumor with next-generation DNA sequencing, matches the cancer-driving mutations to targeted therapies, and gives veterinarians an individualized treatment plan grounded in the world's largest proprietary canine cancer dataset (billions of data points across a network of more than 1,300 veterinary clinics). The company was founded in 2015 by Christina Lopes and Ben Lewis on the "One Health" thesis that treating cancer in companion dogs also advances real-world evidence for human oncology. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z bio), Y Combinator, Polaris Partners, Borealis Ventures, Lerer Hippeau and Tau Ventures. As of this profile the company exposes a consumer and veterinarian web experience (including a veterinarian login portal) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic surface.

providers.name: Science
providers.description: Science Corporation is a clinical-stage medical technology company founded in 2021 by Max Hodak and headquartered in Alameda, California, with offices in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina and Paris, France. Science develops brain-computer interface (BCI) and neural-engineering technologies to restore vision, cognition, and mobility, including the PRIMA retinal implant for patients with macular degeneration, the Biohybrid neural interface, and the Vessel perfusion platform. Through its Foundry division Science also offers MEMS production and neural-engineering services to external partners. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Science publishes no public web API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Cooler Heads
providers.description: Cooler Heads Care, Inc. is a San Diego medical device company founded in 2018 by Kate Dilligan that makes Amma, an FDA-cleared Portable Scalp Cooling System (PSCS) used to reduce chemotherapy-induced hair loss. Amma circulates chilled fluid through a fitted cap to constrict scalp blood vessels and limit chemotherapy delivery to hair follicles, and is designed to be portable enough that patients can keep cooling outside the infusion chair. The company sells to infusion centers and oncology practices and publishes patient, provider, reimbursement and training material on its own site. It ships no developer API, SDK or public API documentation; its only machine-readable public surface is the Wix-platform site MCP endpoint and llms.txt served from its own host.

providers.name: Svastia
providers.description: Svastia (Svastia Genetics Inc.) is a precision-genomics and oncology data company that bundles clinical research products with cutting-edge bioinformatics to accelerate precision cancer therapy. It offers DNA/RNA sequencing, exome and gene-panel assays, immune (B/T-cell) repertoire sequencing, cell-based drug-efficacy screening, therapeutic-antibody development toolkits, and siRNA design, together with biomarker analytics (Tumor Mutational Burden, Microsatellite Instability) and clinical reporting based on ACMG/ASCO guidelines. Svastia serves hospitals, diagnostics labs, researchers, and CROs, and runs a bespoke clinical/genetic data-collection service across a hospital network, with HL7-FHIR data exchange between EHR and Clinical Trial Management Systems. Products are delivered through a login-gated web portal; the company does not publish a public developer API. Backed by 500 Global; offices in San Francisco (USA) and Cambridge (UK).

providers.name: Delve Bio
providers.description: Delve Bio is a genomic diagnostics company commercializing clinical metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for infectious disease diagnosis. Its flagship test, Delve Detect, analyzes all nucleic acids in a single cerebrospinal fluid sample to simultaneously detect bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites, screening against a curated database of more than 68,000 pathogen species to diagnose meningitis and encephalitis with results in roughly 48 hours. The company is the exclusive licensee of the University of California San Francisco (UCSF) mNGS technology developed at the Center for Next-Gen Precision Diagnostics, founded by Charles Chiu, Joe DeRisi, Michael Wilson, Pardis Sabeti, and Matthew Meyerson, and backed by investors including GV. Delve Bio operates as a CAP/CLIA-certified clinical laboratory serving labs and clinicians; it exposes no public developer API surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a gv portfolio lead.

providers.name: Biostate AI
providers.description: Biostate AI is a Houston-based precision-health biotechnology company combining proprietary wet-lab chemistry with generative AI to make RNA and DNA sequencing dramatically cheaper and more accessible. Its BIRT (Barcode-Integrated Reverse Transcription) plus PERD (Probes for Excess RNA Depletion) platform delivers Total RNA sequencing from around $60 per sample, and its N-Act and RNAstate AI models turn omics data into clinical insights for autoimmune, cardiovascular, and cancer diagnostics. The company operates a cloud data lake for AI-ready omics data and runs research partnerships across the U.S., India, and China. As of this profile Biostate publishes a marketing and publications site plus open research model repositories on GitHub, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK client library, or developer portal.

providers.name: Vedanta Biosciences
providers.description: Vedanta Biosciences is a late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered at 19 Blackstone Street in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded by PureTech Health together with a group of scientific co-founders who pioneered the modern understanding of cross-talk between the human microbiome and the immune system. The company develops a potential new category of oral Live Biotherapeutic Products built from rationally defined consortia of human commensal bacteria grown from pure clonal cell banks rather than donor-derived stool, and it maintains technical expertise in the manufacture of live organisms. Its lead program, VE303, is an eight-strain defined bacterial consortium in the global Phase 3 RESTORATiVE303 registrational study for the prevention of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, following Phase 2 results showing a greater than 80% reduction in the odds of CDI recurrence versus placebo; VE202 is in development for inflammatory bowel disease and VE707 for prevention of multidrug-resistant organism infections. Vedanta has raised a $68 million Series D and a $106.5 million financing, and its programs are supported by non-dilutive awards from BARDA and CARB-X. Vedanta is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it runs a WordPress marketing and corporate site, publishes no developer portal, no SDKs, no GitHub organization and no machine-readable API contract, and an August 2026 probe of vedantabio.com found no OpenAPI, no /llms.txt, no MCP endpoint, no A2A agent card and an empty /.well-known/ discovery surface.

providers.name: Diagonal Therapeutics
providers.description: Diagonal Therapeutics is a Watertown, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2022 by CEO Alex Lugovskoy in partnership with Atlas Venture, developing "clustering" agonist antibodies that switch broken signaling pathways back on rather than inhibiting them. Its DIAGONAL product engine pairs computational epitope filtering with experimental screening — generating roughly 200,000 candidate antibody sequences per target, clustering them by predicted shape, binning by receptor complementarity and assembling multispecific antibodies from those bins — to make agonist antibody discovery tractable. The lead program, DIAG723, is a first-in-class ALK1:BMPRII clustering agonist antibody that restores ALK1 signaling; it holds US FDA and EMA orphan drug designation for hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) and entered the Phase 1/2 DIAMOND trial (NCT07623525), with a first patient dosed in July 2026, alongside preclinical work in pulmonary arterial hypertension. The pipeline extends into hematology, hepatology, nephrology and cardiovascular disease. The company has raised roughly USD 255 million across a USD 128 million Series A (April 2024, co-led by BVF Partners and Atlas Venture) and an oversubscribed USD 125 million Series B (January 2026, co-led by Sanofi Ventures and Janus Henderson Investors). Diagonal is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: it operates a Next.js marketing site backed by a Sanity CMS, and publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Vertex Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Vertex Pharmaceuticals is a global biotechnology company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, focused on scientific innovation to create transformative medicines for people with serious diseases. The company specializes in cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, beta thalassemia, APOL1-mediated kidney disease, pain, and other serious conditions. Vertex is committed to responsible sharing of clinical trial data with qualified researchers through formal data request processes.

providers.name: Boston Heart Diagnostics (Eurofins Scientific)
providers.description: Boston Heart Diagnostics is a specialty cardiovascular diagnostics laboratory, part of Eurofins Scientific, that has been improving patient outcomes since 2007 through a combination of integrated diagnostics, advanced lipid and metabolic testing, genetic risk evaluation, personalized reporting, and a scientifically designed nutrition and lifestyle program. It serves clinicians and patients through a provider portal and a patient portal (mybostonheart.com) rather than a public developer API; there is no published developer portal, OpenAPI, or programmatic surface at this time. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the identity and security-posture fields below are captured from the provider's public web presence.

providers.name: Enable
providers.description: Enable Medicine is a healthcare and life-sciences data company that licenses an integrated, AI-ready index of clinical, spatial, cellular, and molecular data. Its research platform helps biopharma companies, academic institutions, and healthcare providers run spatial-biology analysis — spatial proteomics, cell phenotyping, tumor-microenvironment characterization, immune profiling, and biomarker identification — across 20+ disease areas over harmonized datasets spanning 10M+ patients and 125M+ cells. The platform is delivered through a login-gated web application at app.enablemedicine.com; no public developer API is currently documented. Backed by initialized-capital, insight-partners, lightspeed-venture-partners, menlo-ventures, norwest-venture-partners, and sierra-ventures.

providers.name: Genome Medical
providers.description: Genome Medical is a telehealth-enabled genetic services provider offering expert genetic counseling, test selection and ordering support, results interpretation, and clinical trial matching for individuals with rare and hereditary conditions. It partners with health systems, life sciences organizations, and genetic testing labs to scale genetic care, reduce diagnostic backlogs, and accelerate diagnoses through a proprietary clinical platform and patient portal. Genome Medical does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Inductive
providers.description: Inductive Bio is a New York-based AI drug discovery company building a virtual lab for small molecule optimization. It pairs medicinal chemists with AI to run millions of in silico ADMET experiments before synthesis. Its Beacon-1 models — trained on a pre-competitive, anonymized data consortium spanning thousands of drug programs — won consecutive first-place finishes in the 2025 Polaris/ASAP and 2026 OpenADMET blind ADMET prediction competitions, beating 370+ submissions including entries from Merck and NVIDIA. Products include the Compass software platform (accessible via API), the Indy AI chemistry assistant, the ADME-One high-throughput profiling service, and Embedded Experts. Founded in 2023 by Josh Haimson and Ben Birnbaum (both formerly Flatiron Health); SOC 2 compliant; backed by Obvious Ventures, a16z Bio+Health, Lux Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Character, and S32.

providers.name: TandemAI
providers.description: TandemAI is an integrated drug discovery contract research organization (CRO) that combines proprietary AI and physics-based computational methods with in-house high-performance computing and extensive wet-lab operations to accelerate pharmaceutical research. Its cloud-enabled, data-centric, browser-based platform, TandemViz, spans hit finding, hit-to-lead and lead optimization, digital assays and workflows, medicinal chemistry and synthesis, biological assays, and a peptide platform. TandemAI is offered as an FTE-based service model that bundles wet-lab services with complimentary access to its AI and computational tools, or as a stand-alone SaaS software license. The company merged with Perpetual Medicines and is backed by Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Verisian
providers.description: Verisian is an AI infrastructure platform for clinical trials, giving pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs the information infrastructure required to deploy AI across their experts and processes. The platform provides full study traceability and automates statistical programming workflows: automating the validation of SDTM and ADaM analysis datasets (turning time-consuming QC double-programming into value-generating QA oversight), and generating complete define-XML files and draft reviewer's guides that are guaranteed consistent with the underlying analysis, so teams are submission-ready in hours. Verisian is cloud native, compatible with any statistical computing environment (SCE), storage, or compute, and integrates through simple file transfer with no complex API integration required. It serves statistical programmers, statisticians, data managers, medical writers, clinicians, and regulatory teams across in-house and CRO-outsourced operating models; Bayer is a named customer. There is no public developer API surface — the product is an enterprise application (app.verisian.com) accessed after sales onboarding.

providers.name: Briya
providers.description: Briya builds AIRE (AI Research Environment), a privacy-first AI platform for healthcare and clinical research that lets researchers analyze real-world medical data without writing code. AIRE trains AI models on real-world data and provides domain-specific agents for literature review, hypothesis testing, population and cohort analysis, study design, and manuscript-ready output with built-in validation. Data is accessed across multiple sources without centralizing it into a warehouse, with a compliance posture aimed at HIPAA, GDPR, and FDA/EMA regulatory standards. Briya serves emerging biotech, life sciences organizations, academic institutions, and healthcare systems, with offices in New York, Nashville, and Tel Aviv. The company is backed by Insight Partners. This API Evangelist profile is an enrichment pass on a portfolio lead; Briya publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Enjamb Labs
providers.description: Enjamb Labs builds an AI-agent platform for pharmaceutical drug development. Its browser-based "integrated research environment" runs specialized agents across the full R&D lifecycle -- clinical evidence synthesis, trial design and statistical programming, and regulatory submission preparation -- while connecting to the systems pharma teams already use (Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, SAS) so no data migration is required. The workspace bundles Word/Excel/PowerPoint editors, Python and R compute environments, and 100+ scientific integrations, and emphasizes auditability, traceability, and human review, keeping each output attached to its sources, files, code, and decisions. Backed by Y Combinator and Founders, Inc., Enjamb reports early usage across major pharmaceutical companies including Johnson & Johnson, Merck, AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, and Sanofi.

providers.name: Ionis Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Ionis Pharmaceuticals is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Ionis Pharmaceuticals API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Arima Genomics
providers.description: Arima Genomics is a San Diego based cancer diagnostics company built on Hi-C sequencing and 3D genome science. Founded in 2015 to study how DNA is organized in three dimensions, the company now develops clinical tests and technology platforms that detect cancer-driving structural alterations — noncanonical fusions, enhancer hijacking, extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) and complex rearrangements — from routine FFPE tumor tissue that conventional DNA and RNA profiling can leave unresolved. Its surface spans research products (Arima-HiC+, Arima High Coverage HiC, Promoter and Custom Capture HiC, HiC FFPE, Arima CiFi), lab services including Single Cell Methyl-3C and multi-omics, the Aventa FusionPlus and Aventa Lymphoma clinical tests, and biopharma partnership programs. Arima publishes open-source bioinformatics pipelines on GitHub (Arima-HiC mapping pipeline, Arima-CHiC, Arima-SV-Pipeline) but operates no public web API, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Asimov
providers.description: Asimov is a synthetic biology company building an integrated platform for the intelligent design of living systems. Its Edge Systems (CHO for biologics, LV for cell therapies, AAV for gene therapies, and RNA for RNA medicines) combine engineered mammalian host cells, a library of more than 1,000 validated genetic parts, and cloud-based genetic design software so biopharma partners can design and manufacture advanced therapeutics at higher titers and on faster timelines. Backed by a16z, DCVC, Wing Venture Capital, and Y Combinator. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Clear Labs
providers.description: Clear Labs builds automated next-generation sequencing (NGS) platforms that combine laboratory robotics, cloud software, and bioinformatics to deliver genomic data and actionable insights. Its product lines span oncology research (Clear Dx), infectious-disease and microbial genomics (Clear Ix), and food-safety pathogen testing (Clear Safety) for organisms such as Listeria and Salmonella. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, Menlo Ventures, and Wing Venture Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Clear Labs publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation as of this profile; the record captures company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Converge Bio
providers.description: Converge Bio is a generative-AI platform for life sciences that accelerates drug development across discovery, molecular design, and manufacturing. It trains Bio-LLM foundation models directly on biological languages (DNA, RNA, and protein sequences) and delivers them through the Converge Computational Lab, whose applications include ConvergeAB (AI antibody design across IgG/VHH/bispecific formats), ConvergeGEO (protein gene-expression optimization across CHO/HEK293/E. coli and other cell systems), ConvergeCELL (virtual cell simulation for target and biomarker discovery), and a Patent Extractor for mining antibody sequences. The platform is delivered to biotech and pharmaceutical customers under a Request Access engagement model; there is no public developer API, SDK, or self-serve documentation surface today. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners ($25M Series A, January 2026); founded 2023.

providers.name: Matterworks
providers.description: Matterworks is a Boston-based life-sciences AI company building foundation models for biochemical omics. Its Large Spectral Model is trained on billions of small-molecule, lipid, peptide, and protein mass-spectrometry spectra across millions of biological contexts, and its Pyxis platform turns raw omics data into quantitative, untargeted biochemical annotations and predictions used for asset and target discovery, mode-of-action elucidation, and life-science R&D pipeline decisions. Matterworks positions biochemical omics as explaining orders of magnitude more biological variation than sequence data alone. The product is accessed through the Pyxis web application (app.matterworks.ai, Auth0 sign-in); no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface is published at this time.

providers.name: Outpost Bio
providers.description: Outpost Bio builds frontier AI foundation models for the human microbiome. Its "lab-in-the-loop" platform pairs high-throughput wet-lab experiments with machine learning in a continuous cycle to predict how drugs and ingredients interact with microbial ecosystems, helping de-risk drug and ingredient R&D decisions around metabolism, toxicity, and efficacy.
