Its engineered biologics bind two complexed targets simultaneously to increase tumor specificity, driving internalization of the antibody-receptor complex and its cytotoxic payload, with the goal of expanding the therapeutic window for hard-to-treat cancers such as colorectal, lung, and head-and-neck squamous cell carcinomas. The company raised an oversubscribed $137M Series B in 2026 (co-led by Frazier Life Sciences and Novartis Venture Fund, with DCVC Bio, OrbiMed, and others) and is advancing its bispecific ADC programs toward clinical development. Sidewinder is a biopharma research company and publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Trace Neuroscience
providers.description: Trace Neuroscience, Inc. is a biotechnology company developing genetic medicines for neurodegenerative diseases. Its lead investigational medicine, TRCN-1023, is designed to restore the function of the UNC13A protein, which is disrupted in most people living with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The company sponsors the FUNCtion ALS Phase 1/2 trial (NCT07674667) evaluating TRCN-1023 delivered by intrathecal injection. Trace Neuroscience is backed by GV and does not currently publish a public developer portal or APIs.

providers.name: Valar Labs
providers.description: Valar Labs is an AI oncology company building diagnostics that interpret solid tumors from routine pathology slides to predict cancer treatment response. Its proprietary CHAI (Computational Histology Artificial Intelligence) platform analyzes digitized H&E-stained slides — trained on 500,000+ pathologist annotations of tumors and their microenvironment — to help physicians and patients make evidence-based therapy decisions. Products include Vesta Bladder (predicting BCG response in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer), Vesta Prostate, and Vitara Pancreas ChemoPredict (guiding first-line chemotherapy selection in advanced pancreatic cancer). Founded at the intersection of AI and oncology and backed by a16z and DCVC, Valar Labs delivers results within days without requiring additional tissue. The company operates a physician ordering portal at portal.valarlabs.com and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API specification as of this profile.

providers.name: Actio Biosciences
providers.description: Actio Biosciences is a San Diego-based clinical-stage biotechnology company developing precision medicines that translate insights from Mendelian (single-gene) genetics into treatments for both rare and common diseases. Its pipeline targets genetically defined conditions including KCNT1-related epilepsy and TRPV4-related Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2C (CMT2C), following a strategy of expanding from rare indications into more prevalent diseases that share the same underlying biology. The company is backed by Canaan Partners. Actio publishes no developer or API surface; this profile captures its public identity and corporate web properties.

providers.name: BioCytics
providers.description: BioCytics, Inc. is a privately held biotechnology company in Huntersville, North Carolina, founded in 2005 by John Powderly, MD, CPI, and clinically incubated by the co-located Carolina BioOncology Institute cancer research clinic. Its name means "applications of living cells": the company runs a Human Applications Laboratory (HAL), a patient-driven and industry-driven BioBank, and a BioInformatics group, and sells cGMP cell-therapy manufacturing (CDMO), early-phase CRO services, clinical lab diagnostics and translational analytical services alongside its own autologous adaptive immune cell therapy (AAICT) pipeline for solid tumors. Its BioDICE platform — BioCytics Digitally Integrated Clinical Enterprise — is an internal EMR / EDC-CDM / lab-documentation / CTMS suite whose product page names openEHR, HL7, FHIR, OMOP and SMART-on-FHIR as the data standards it works with, and openEHR International lists BioCytics as a Bronze industry partner. None of that is exposed: BioCytics publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind, and biocytics.com is a 26-page WordPress site whose only machine-readable surface is the CMS's own unadvertised /wp-json/ index.

providers.name: Curebase
providers.description: Curebase is a San Francisco-based clinical trials technology company (founded 2017) that provides a modern, AI-native eClinical platform for sponsors, CROs, biotechs, MedTech companies, and research sites. The platform unifies the full trial lifecycle in one system: ePRO/eCOA (electronic patient-reported and clinical outcome assessments), eConsent (digital informed consent), EDC (electronic data capture), patient recruitment and screening, participant engagement and retention tooling, and site management. Curebase also ships Sitebase, a free eClinical suite for research sites, and Hope, a conversational AI voice agent. It supports decentralized and hybrid trial models natively. Curebase is a private, venture-backed company (Series B led by Industry Ventures; investors include GGV Capital, Acrew, Gilead, and others). It is SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR compliant. Curebase does not publish a public developer API or API documentation; integration is handled through enterprise engagements.

providers.name: Gandeeva
providers.description: Gandeeva Therapeutics is a Vancouver, Canada-based precision-medicine and drug-discovery company that combines cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) with artificial intelligence and machine learning to visualize druggable transient protein-protein interactions at atomic resolution and design first-in-class molecular glues and engineered antibodies. Its structure-guided platform spans target prediction and validation (SPOTLIGHT), hit identification across virtual and fragment libraries (HYPERFOCUS), and cryo-EM-driven lead optimization (CRYO-CADD), with an oncology-focused pipeline of proximity-inducing small molecules. The company raised a $40M Series A and has run cryo-EM research collaborations with partners including Moderna and Zymeworks. Gandeeva is a private biotechnology company and does not publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/portfolio record.

providers.name: Kula Bio
providers.description: Kula Bio is an agricultural biotechnology company headquartered in Natick, Massachusetts that manufactures Kula-N, a nitrogen-fixing microbial biofertilizer built on the bacterium Xanthobacter autotrophicus. The company's process, originating in Dr. Dan Nocera's research, "supercharges" the microbe with renewable energy so it fixes atmospheric nitrogen at the root zone, letting growers replace a portion of synthetic nitrogen while cutting the greenhouse-gas footprint of the applied product. Kula Bio sells a liquid formulation and, since February 2026, a Soluble Powder (SP) line, serving produce and row-crop growers through agronomic distribution rather than through software. It raised a $50M Series A led by Lowercarbon Capital and was named to TIME's list of America's Top GreenTech Companies of 2026. Kula Bio publishes no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind; this profile records that measured absence alongside its verified public corporate surface.

providers.name: Plantible Foods
providers.description: Plantible Foods is a business-to-business food-ingredient company founded in 2018 by Dutch entrepreneurs Tony and Maurits, with its first commercial production facility in Schleicher County, Texas. The company cultivates lemna (duckweed) in controlled, automated aquafarms and uses a proprietary water-based extraction process to isolate RuBisCO, sold as Rubi Protein — roughly 85% protein by weight with a PDCAAS of 1.0 — alongside Lemna Leaf Greens and application-specific systems such as RubiWhisk and RubiPrime. It sells to food manufacturers and ingredient companies rather than consumers, and in February 2026 became the first company to receive an FDA "no questions" GRAS letter for isolated RuBisCO protein in food. Investors include RA Capital, Nourish Ventures, Chipotle, Kellogg's and CJ Group. Plantible is an agricultural manufacturing business: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind, and plantiblefoods.com is a Webflow marketing site with no developer surface.

providers.name: Conformal Medical
providers.description: Conformal Medical, Inc. is a Nashua, New Hampshire medical device company developing the CLAAS (Conformal Left Atrial Appendage Seal) and next-generation CLAAS AcuFORM left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) systems, foam-based implants intended to seal the left atrial appendage and reduce stroke risk in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation without requiring pre-procedure CT sizing. The company runs the CONFORM pivotal IDE trial and the GLACE study, and publishes a public marketing site segmented for patients, physicians and company/investor audiences. W. L. Gore & Associates completed its acquisition of Conformal Medical on 2026-02-19. Conformal Medical is a regulated medical device manufacturer, not a software vendor: it operates no developer program, publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or machine-readable specification, and its only software artifacts are clinical-trial companion mobile apps for enrolled sites.

providers.name: Roche
providers.description: F. Hoffmann-La Roche is a Swiss multinational healthcare company with two divisions: Roche Pharma and Roche Diagnostics. Roche does not publish a general public developer API but exposes interoperability through the navify diagnostics platform, the cobas infinity laboratory software, and an open-source GitHub presence focused on data-science tooling such as pyreadstat, foxops, and OligoGym.

providers.name: Stroma Medical
providers.description: Strōma Medical Corporation is a clinical-stage medical device company headquartered in Irvine, California, developing the Strōma Laser System — a patented laser technology that permanently changes eye color by removing the thin layer of brown pigment on the anterior surface of the iris, revealing the underlying amber, hazel, grey, blue or green color beneath. The in-office procedure uses only topical anesthetic, takes under a minute per eye per treatment, and reveals its result over three to four weeks. Strōma licenses the system to refractive surgeons and LASIK-certified ophthalmologists rather than selling to consumers directly. The device is investigational and is not available for sale or use in the United States, and the company filed a voluntary Chapter 11, Subchapter V case in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware. Strōma publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable API contract of any kind; its public web presence is a six-page WordPress marketing site.

providers.name: Accent Therapeutics
providers.description: Accent Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company pioneering a new class of small-molecule precision cancer therapies that target critical intracellular dependencies spanning multiple types of cancer. Its pipeline is led by ATX-295, a novel KIF18A inhibitor in clinical development, with data presented at AACR and ASCO. Backed by GV, Accent focuses on precision oncology drug discovery and development. The company does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its corporate and web identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aerska
providers.description: Aerska is a biotechnology company developing RNA interference (RNAi) medicines to treat, delay, and prevent diseases of the brain and central nervous system. The company pairs next-generation RNAi therapeutics with receptor-mediated "brain shuttle" delivery technology engineered to cross the blood-brain barrier and silence disease-causing genes in the CNS. Founded in 2025 by Jack O'Meara, Stuart Milstein, and Dave Hardwicke, Aerska is headquartered in Dublin, Ireland with research operations in London. It emerged from stealth in 2026 having raised a Series A round led by the EQT Dementia Fund and age1, with additional backing from Speedinvest and Backed. Aerska is a pre-clinical drug-discovery company and does not currently publish a public developer API or platform.

providers.name: AIRNA
providers.description: AIRNA Corporation is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing precision RNA editing therapeutics based on ADAR (adenosine deaminase acting on RNA), a naturally occurring human protein the company redirects to convert adenosine to inosine at a targeted RNA site — changing protein function without permanently altering DNA. Its oligonucleotide medicines are designed for durable, reversible and repeatable dosing. The lead program, AIR-001, targets alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD), alongside cardiometabolic RNA editing programs spanning rare genetic disorders and common conditions. Founded by scientific pioneers of ADAR editing, AIRNA operates from Cambridge, Massachusetts and Tübingen, Germany (AIRNA Bio Germany GmbH). AIRNA publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; therapeutics, not software, are the product.

providers.name: AminoChain
providers.description: AminoChain operates a transparent, decentralized research ecosystem for patient-centric biomedical research. Its Specimen Center helps researchers discover and access legacy biospecimens through decentralized specimen discovery and collaboration, while its Donor Platform enables prospective participant registries and manages participant involvement in studies. The platform emphasizes privacy-preserving re-engagement, cryptographic tracking of biospecimens, auditable consent, and benefit-sharing models that return value to patients and donors. Backed by a16z. AminoChain currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: antengene
providers.description: Antengene Corporation is a commercial-stage, R&D-driven global biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing first-in-class and best-in-class therapies for the treatment of hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. Headquartered in Shanghai with a global footprint across the Asia Pacific region and beyond, Antengene's marketed product XPOVIO (selinexor) and a pipeline of oncology assets such as the Claudin 18.2 antibody-drug conjugate ATG-022 and the CD73 inhibitor ATG-037 target unmet needs in cancer care. Antengene operates in the life sciences sector and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and captured in the API Evangelist network for company intelligence and enrichment.

providers.name: Asher Biotherapeutics
providers.description: Asher Biotherapeutics (Asher Bio) is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2019 and headquartered at 650 Gateway Blvd. in South San Francisco, California. The company develops cis-targeted immunotherapies — engineered biologics that simultaneously engage an immunomodulatory receptor and a cell-type-specific target on the same immune cell, so a cytokine is only activated on the intended cell population rather than acting indiscriminately across immune subsets. Its lead candidate, etakafusp alfa (AB248), is a cis-targeted IL-2 directed at CD8+ effector T cells and is in Phase 1a/1b clinical development in cancer, alongside earlier-stage programs AB821 and AB359 and a cis-targeted cytokine augmentation program for cell therapies. Asher Bio is a therapeutics developer, not a software or platform company: it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Basking Biosciences
providers.description: Basking Biosciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Research Triangle, North Carolina (with operations in Mitchelton, Queensland, Australia) developing novel therapies for life-threatening blood clots. Its lead program BB-031 is an investigational RNA aptamer that targets von Willebrand Factor (vWF) to deliver a rapid-onset, targeted, and reversible thrombolytic for acute ischemic stroke, paired with BB-025, a direct-acting reversal agent designed to rapidly neutralize BB-031. The company is running the RAISE Phase 2 clinical trial and is backed by Insight Partners. Surfaced as a VC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Bitterroot Bio
providers.description: Bitterroot Bio is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Palo Alto, California, pioneering the emerging field of cardio-immunology — the interplay between the immune system and cardiovascular disease. Its lead program, BRB-002, is a novel investigational immunomodulating protein therapy that targets CD47 to treat atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) by acting on atherosclerotic plaque through the immunomodulation of macrophages, an approach distinct from current standards of care. Founded in 2021, the company is advancing BRB-002 through its MATADOR Phase 2a proof-of-concept study. Bitterroot Bio is a therapeutics developer and publishes no public developer API or programmatic surface; this profile captures its public web identity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cellares
providers.description: Cellares is an Integrated Development and Manufacturing Organization (IDMO) for cell therapies, operating a global network of automated "Smart Factories." Its FDA-recognized Cell Shuttle platform delivers high-throughput, end-to-end, cGMP industrial-scale cell therapy manufacturing, and its Cell Q platform automates quality-control testing of cell therapy products. Smart Factories operate in South San Francisco (CA), Bridgewater (NJ), Leiden (Netherlands), and Kashiwa (Japan). Cellares was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and profiled in the API Evangelist network; as a cell therapy manufacturing organization it publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Circular Genomics
providers.description: Circular Genomics is a San Diego, California precision-neurology diagnostics company that uses brain-derived circular RNA (circRNA) as a class of stable, blood-based biomarkers for psychiatric and neurological disease. Spun out of the University of New Mexico in 2021 and now resident at Lilly Gateway Labs in San Diego, the company builds CircPath, a proprietary molecular-intelligence platform that discovers, validates and translates circRNA signals into biological insight, and productizes it as research and clinical assays: Discover 1600+ (whole-transcriptome circRNA sequencing across 1,600+ brain-derived circRNAs with pathway-level analysis), AD Predict and AD Detect for Alzheimer's disease, and MindLight, an SSRI antidepressant response test for major depressive disorder. Test ordering and results delivery for licensed healthcare providers run through a login-gated provider portal at mindlight.circulargenomics.com, which is a white-labeled CrelioHealth laboratory information system rather than a first-party developer surface. Circular Genomics publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or developer documentation of any kind.

providers.name: Cour Pharmaceuticals Development
providers.description: COUR Pharmaceuticals Development Co., Inc. (COUR Pharma) is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in the Chicago area (Northbrook/Skokie, Illinois), spun out of research at Northwestern University. COUR develops antigen-specific immune tolerance therapies built on its proprietary COUR Nanoparticle (CNP) platform: biodegradable polymer nanoparticles of roughly 500 nm carrying about 1% disease-specific antigen, which mimic apoptotic bodies so that antigen-presenting cells in the liver and spleen re-recognize the antigen as self, deleting pathogenic T cells and expanding regulatory T cells. Active clinical programs include CNP-103 for Type 1 Diabetes and CNP-106 for Myasthenia Gravis, with earlier work in Primary Biliary Cholangitis and Celiac Disease. COUR is a therapeutics developer, not a software or platform company: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Creyon Bio
providers.description: Creyon Bio (branded Creyon) is a San Diego drug-development company operating an AI-powered nucleic acid engineering platform, NucleIQ, that designs oligonucleotide and RNA therapies with tissue- and cell-specific delivery. Creyon uses aptamer-based delivery, lipid nanoparticles, and transferrin-receptor aptamers to cross the blood-brain barrier, targeting immunology, central nervous system (CNS), and neuromuscular indications including late-onset Pompe disease. The company is a venture-backed portfolio company of DCVC and currently advances three wholly-owned programs. This profile is a company/identity record in the API Evangelist network; Creyon publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: DiscGenics
providers.description: DiscGenics is a privately held, late-stage clinical biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, developing allogeneic, cell-based regenerative biologic therapies for degenerative diseases of the spine. Its lead candidate, IDCT (rebonuputemcel), is a single-injection allogeneic discogenic progenitor cell therapy for symptomatic mild-to-moderate lumbar degenerative disc disease, manufactured under cGMP from donated adult human intervertebral disc tissue and granted FDA Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) and Fast Track designations. The company is running a US Phase III program (the PIVOT and CONFIRM studies) alongside a clinical study in Japan. DiscGenics is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Electra Therapeutics
providers.description: Electra Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company in South San Francisco, California, founded in 2018 and pioneering first-in-class antibody therapies directed at signal regulatory proteins (SIRP) for immunological diseases and cancer. Its lead candidate, ELA026 (ipsoprubart), is a monoclonal antibody targeting SIRP-alpha/beta1/gamma on myeloid cells and T lymphocytes to selectively deplete the pathological immune cells that drive the cytokine storm in secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH); it is in the pivotal SURPASS Phase 2/3 study. A second SIRP-targeted program, ELA822, is directed at activated T lymphocytes for immunology and inflammation indications. The company has raised roughly $267M from investors including OrbiMed, Nextech Invest, EQT Life Sciences and Westlake Village BioPartners. Electra publishes a corporate website, pipeline, publications, clinical-trial and news pages, but no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Erasca
providers.description: Erasca is a clinical-stage precision oncology company (NASDAQ: ERAS) headquartered in San Diego, California, whose name is its mission: to erase cancer. The company is singularly focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing therapies for RAS- and MAPK pathway-driven cancers. RAS is the most frequently mutated oncogene and the MAPK pathway one of the most frequently altered signaling pathways in cancer, together accounting for roughly five million newly diagnosed patients globally each year. Erasca pursues three complementary therapeutic strategies intended to comprehensively shut down the RAS/MAPK pathway by targeting multiple nodes and cooperative mechanisms in parallel. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio-linked lead; as a therapeutics company Erasca publishes a corporate and investor web presence rather than a developer API surface, so this record captures verified company identity, legal, and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Evergreen Theragnostics
providers.description: Evergreen Theragnostics is a Springfield, New Jersey radiopharmaceutical company founded in 2019 that operates a cGMP contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) for therapeutic and diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals, alongside its own clinical pipeline of theragnostic pairs including the OCTEVY PET diagnostic imaging agent for neuroendocrine tumors. Its 14,000 square foot Springfield facility carries seven commercial-scale production suites, sterility lines, quality control and packaging space serving radioligand therapy developers. Lantheus Holdings completed its acquisition of the company on April 1, 2025, and Evergreen now operates as part of Lantheus. The company sells manufacturing services and drug products, not software: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Karius
providers.description: Karius is an infectious disease diagnostics company that applies clinical metagenomics and machine learning to microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) circulating in the bloodstream, detecting pathogens that conventional culture-based testing misses. Its CLIA-certified and CAP-accredited laboratory runs the Karius Spectrum blood test, which screens a single blood draw for more than 1,000 bacteria, fungi, DNA viruses, and parasites, and the Karius Focus BAL test, which detects more than 500 pathogens in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid for lung infections. Results are returned to clinicians managing complex, immunocompromised, and difficult-to-diagnose patients.

providers.name: LENZ Therapeutics
providers.description: LENZ Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: LENZ) is a commercial-stage ophthalmic pharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, focused on the commercialization of VIZZ (aceclidine ophthalmic solution) 1.44% — the first and only FDA-approved aceclidine-based eye drop for the treatment of presbyopia. LENZ commercializes VIZZ in the United States and establishes international licensing partnerships to provide access globally. The company publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable API description of any kind; its public surface is a ten-page WordPress marketing site, a VIZZ product site, and an investor-relations portal carrying SEC filings and a press-release RSS feed.

providers.name: Mariana Oncology
providers.description: Mariana Oncology, a Novartis company, is a Watertown, Massachusetts biotechnology company developing precision radioligand therapies (RLTs) — targeted radiopharmaceuticals that deliver alpha- and beta-emitting radioisotopes selectively to tumor cells while sparing healthy tissue. Its pipeline pursues solid-tumor targets including DLL3-expressing small cell lung cancer (MC-339), alongside breast and prostate programs, and it operates a Radioligand Therapy Innovation Center of Excellence for radiochemistry, isotope handling and clinical supply. Founded in 2020 and acquired by Novartis in May 2024, Mariana Oncology is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable interface of any kind.

providers.name: PAQ Therapeutics
providers.description: PAQ Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at 100 Summit Drive, Burlington, Massachusetts, developing targeted protein degradation (TPD) medicines for KRAS-driven cancers. Rather than inhibiting the KRAS oncoprotein, PAQ's autophagy-based degrader chemistry recruits the cell's own natural degradation machinery to remove the protein outright, an approach the company applies to the KRAS mutations found in roughly a quarter of human tumors, most notably lung, colorectal and pancreatic cancer. Its lead program, PT0511, is a pan-KRAS degrader that dosed its first patient in a Phase 1 trial in January 2026. The company was co-founded by Nan Ji (Chief Executive Officer) and Huaixiang Hao (Head of Research), with Andrew Krivoshik as Chief Medical Officer. PAQ Therapeutics is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it operates a four-page corporate WordPress site and publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Parabilis Medicines
providers.description: Parabilis Medicines (formerly FogPharma) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing a new class of ultra-tunable alpha-helical peptide therapeutics called Helicons to reach intracellular protein targets long considered undruggable. Its AI- and physics-based discovery platform underpins a pipeline led by zolucatetide, a candidate targeting the beta-catenin / TCF interaction in the Wnt signaling pathway across multiple cancers. Backed by more than $500M from leading life sciences investors and public since its June 2026 IPO (Nasdaq: PBLS), the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and GV. It publishes a public marketing and investor web presence and a science/data tech blog, but exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Protagonist Therapeutics
providers.description: Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Newark, California and founded in 2006. It discovers and develops peptide-based new chemical entities using a proprietary peptide discovery and engineering platform, targeting rare and prevalent diseases with significant unmet medical need. Lead programs include rusfertide, a hepcidin mimetic in Phase 3 for polycythemia vera, and icotrokinra (PN-235), an oral IL-23 receptor antagonist partnered with Johnson & Johnson. The company is publicly traded (Nasdaq: PTGX) following its 2016 IPO. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or agent surface.

providers.name: Qlaris Bio
providers.description: Qlaris Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing first-in-class therapies for ophthalmic diseases, with a mission to preserve vision and prevent blindness. Its lead candidate, QLS-111, uses a novel mechanism of action to lower intraocular pressure by targeting the distal outflow pathway, and is being evaluated for primary open-angle glaucoma, ocular hypertension, and elevated IOP associated with conditions such as Sturge-Weber Syndrome. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a clinical-stage drug developer, Qlaris Bio publishes a corporate website but no public developer, API, or product integration surface.

providers.name: Rezo Therapeutics
providers.description: Rezo Therapeutics is a San Francisco (Mission Bay) biopharmaceutical company spun out of the Quantitative Biosciences Institute (QBI) at UCSF, co-founded by Nevan Krogan, that is building a disease-agnostic network-biology drug discovery platform. Its "sequence to systems to drugs" approach integrates proteomics, human genetics, structural biology, medicinal chemistry, bioinformatics and machine learning to construct comprehensive maps of molecular disease networks and identify novel, druggable targets for precision therapeutics, with an initial focus on oncology. The company launched in November 2022 with a $78M Series A led by SR One, a16z Bio + Health and Norwest Venture Partners, and appointed Derek Hicks as chief executive officer in August 2025. Rezo is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: its computational platform is internal R&D tooling, and the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Sail Biomedicines
providers.description: Sail Biomedicines is a Cambridge, Massachusetts preclinical biotechnology company created in October 2023 by Flagship Pioneering through the merger of Laronde and Senda Biosciences, and it is the company this profile's legacy `laronde` slug refers to. Sail combines Laronde's Endless RNA (eRNA) platform — synthetic circular RNA engineered to be translated persistently inside the body — with Senda's programmable lipid and natural nanoparticle delivery chemistry, and layers generative AI on the combined dataset to design what the company calls fully programmable medicines. Its lead effort is in vivo CAR-T for autoimmune disease: instructing a patient's own T cells to reprogram themselves inside the body rather than extracting, engineering and reinfusing them, an approach Sail markets as "immune reset". In July 2026 Johnson & Johnson committed $785 million up front (including a $465 million equity investment) plus up to $140 million in milestones and took an exclusive option to acquire the company for a further $2.58 billion. Sail sells therapeutics, not software: it publishes no API, no SDK, no machine-readable specification and no developer documentation, and it operates no public source-code organization.

providers.name: Spero Therapeutics
providers.description: Spero Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing innovative medicines for immune-mediated and infectious diseases. Its pipeline includes SP001, a third-generation anti-CD40L antibody targeting IgG4-related disease, alongside earlier programs in antibacterial and rare-disease therapeutics. Spero was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network. As a life-sciences drug developer, Spero publishes a corporate and investor-relations web presence but no public developer API, developer portal, or technical integration surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Switch Therapeutics
providers.description: Switch Therapeutics is a precision neuroscience biotechnology company founded in 2020 and based in San Francisco, California, developing biomarker-gated genetic medicines for central nervous system (CNS) diseases with high unmet need. Its Conditionally Activated siRNA (CASi) platform combines properties of single- and double-stranded RNAs in one molecule to enable efficient self-delivery, potent and durable gene knockdown, and cell-type/cell-state selectivity. Its lead development candidate is CASi-APOE, a liver-sparing APOE RNAi therapy. The company is backed by CRV and Insight Partners and is a therapeutics developer with no public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Touchlight
providers.description: Touchlight is a UK-based cell-free DNA manufacturer, founded in 2007 and headquartered in Hampton, London, that produces synthetic DNA enzymatically rather than by bacterial fermentation. Its doggybone DNA (dbDNA) platform — along with mbDNA and z-dbDNA — is a cell-free, plasmid-free DNA vector used as starting material for mRNA, viral vector (AAV, lentivirus), non-viral gene therapy, gene editing and DNA vaccine programs, manufactured at what the company describes as the first GMP-licensed facility for fully cell-free enzymatic DNA. Touchlight sells physical DNA material — off-the-shelf catalogue constructs and custom RUO-to-GMP manufacturing — and operates no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Triveni Bio
providers.description: Triveni Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing first-in-class antibody therapeutics for immunological and inflammatory (I&I) disorders, built on a genetics-informed approach to target discovery combined with advanced antibody engineering. Its lead program TRIV-509 is a dual-specific monoclonal antibody against kallikreins 5 and 7 (KLK5/7) for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, addressing barrier dysfunction, inflammation and itch; TRIV-573 is a half-life-extended, second-generation bispecific that pairs the KLK5/7 mechanism with anti-interleukin-13 (IL-13) and entered Phase 1 in 2026. The pipeline also includes an antibody inhibitor of trypsin 1 and 2 for hereditary pancreatitis driven by PRSS1 mutations. The company launched with a $92M Series A, raised a $115M Series B, and closed a $65M Series C in June 2026, and was named a Fierce 15 biotech of 2025. Triveni Bio is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Zencore Biologics
providers.description: Zencore Biologics (zgbiotech.com) is a one-stop biologics CDMO (contract development and manufacturing organization) technology service platform serving pharmaceutical clients globally. Its services span large-molecule biologics development and production, antibody-drug conjugates (ADC), cell culture media, analytical and quality testing, and regulatory registration support. Surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming; this profile is a corporate/biotech entity with no public developer API surface (no OpenAPI, well-known, or event/webhook interfaces were found).

providers.name: Aardvark Therapeutics
providers.description: Aardvark Therapeutics, Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed (AARD) clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel small-molecule therapies designed to inhibit hunger and treat metabolic disease. Its lead candidate, ARD-101, is an oral, gut-restricted agonist of bitter taste receptors (TAS2Rs) on the luminal side of the intestine, which triggers the release of satiety hormones to suppress hunger signaling; it has been evaluated for hyperphagia associated with Prader-Willi Syndrome, including the Phase 3 HERO trial, as well as in obesity and hypothalamic obesity. The company operates purely as a drug-development organization: its public web presence consists of science, programs, team, news and investor-relations material, and it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Ablative Solutions
providers.description: Ablative Solutions, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage medical device company founded in 2011 and headquartered in Kalamazoo, Michigan, with offices in San Jose, California. It develops the Peregrine System, a percutaneous catheter platform that performs chemical renal denervation by infusing dehydrated alcohol into the perivascular space around the renal arteries to deactivate surrounding sympathetic nerves, as a treatment for systemic and uncontrolled hypertension. The Peregrine System Infusion Catheter holds FDA 510(k) clearance for infusion of diagnostic and therapeutic agents into the perivascular area of the peripheral vasculature; the Peregrine System Kit remains an investigational product under clinical study in the United States and has received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation for drug-resistant hypertension. The company is certified to ISO 13485. Ablative Solutions publishes a small corporate and clinical-information website only; it operates no developer program, public API, documentation portal, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Amicus Therapeutics
providers.description: Amicus Therapeutics is a global rare disease biotechnology company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing medicines for people living with genetically defined conditions. Founded in 2002 and headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey, Amicus markets two approved therapies: Galafold (migalastat) — the first and only oral therapy for adults with Fabry disease who have an amenable GLA variant, approved by the European Commission in May 2016 — and the two-component Pombiliti (cipaglucosidase alfa-atga) + Opfolda (miglustat) enzyme replacement / stabilizer combination for adults with late-onset Pompe disease. Amicus operates wholly owned subsidiaries in Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, Spain, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc. agreed to acquire Amicus in December 2025 for $4.8 billion; the acquisition completed on April 27, 2026 and Amicus now operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of BioMarin, having previously traded on NASDAQ under the ticker FOLD. The company maintains no publicly documented commercial developer APIs, SDKs, or GitHub organization; its digital surface is composed of corporate, product, patient-support, and clinical-trial websites.

providers.name: Atlas5D
providers.description: Atlas5D is a healthcare technology company that develops an Ambient Measurement System (AMS) for assessing health and wellness through motion in any environment. Its passive, privacy-preserving sensor platform recognizes specific individuals, characterizes and quantifies their movement, and interprets daily routines to predict trends and assess risk of adverse events such as falls, without wearables, without transmitting video, and without storing images. Atlas5D serves individuals monitoring aging loved ones, assisted-living and other institutional care settings, and healthcare and clinical-trial teams that need clinical-grade, real-world evidence of patient movement wherever people live. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Calviri
providers.description: Calviri is a Phoenix, Arizona biotechnology company, founded in 2017, that develops multi-cancer diagnostic tests and therapeutic and preventative cancer vaccines for dogs and people. Its science rests on RNA-Error Derived Neoantigens (REDNs) — abnormal proteins thrown off by the error-prone RNA processing of tumor cells — which Calviri builds as peptides on semiconductor chips and then queries against an individual's blood for antibody responses, using those antibodies as sensitive biomarkers of cancer. Its lead product, StageOne Plus, is a canine multi-cancer blood test designed to detect stage 1 disease before signs appear, alongside a pipeline of canine and human therapeutic and preventative vaccines and a preventative-vaccine trial (VACCS) that enrolled 800+ dogs. Calviri is a life-sciences company with no developer program, no product API and no developer portal; the only machine-readable surface on calviri.com is the Wix-platform-generated llms.txt and the anonymous site MCP endpoint it advertises.

providers.name: Ensoma
providers.description: Ensoma is a privately held, clinical-stage genomic medicines company developing in vivo hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) engineering. Its platform pairs an off-the-shelf in vivo delivery system built on high-capacity virus-like particles that preferentially bind HSCs with a gene engineering toolkit spanning base editing and high-efficiency gene integration, carrying payloads of roughly 35 kilobases so that changes from single-base edits through multi-gene insertions can be made without ex vivo cell collection, manipulation, or transplant conditioning. The company is pursuing programs across genetic disease, immune disorders, and oncology, including EN-374 for X-linked chronic granulomatous disease, and is backed by 5AM Ventures, F-Prime Capital, RTW Investments, Alexandria Venture Investments, Cormorant Asset Management, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. Enrichment found no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, OpenAPI/GraphQL/AsyncAPI contract, MCP server, or agent card — this is a therapeutics R&D company, not an API provider. Its only public machine-readable output is open-source computational genomics and sequencing-pipeline code published under its GitHub organization.

providers.name: HotSpot Therapeutics
providers.description: HotSpot Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, pioneering allosteric drug discovery by targeting "natural hotspots" — the regulatory on/off switches on proteins. Its Smart Allostery platform combines AI-driven mining of large, diverse structural and biological data sets with a tailored pharmacology toolkit and bespoke medicinal chemistry to design first-in-class oral small molecules, and has been applied across E3 ligases, kinases and transcription factors. The company has raised roughly $190M across Series A, B and C financings and advanced its lead candidate HST-1011, an oral allosteric CBL-B inhibitor, into first-in-human dosing for cancer, alongside programs in autoimmune disease. HotSpot sells medicines and research collaborations, not software: it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Totus Medicines
providers.description: Totus Medicines is a biopharmaceutical company developing precision oral medicines against historically "undruggable" disease targets. The company's OmniDEL discovery platform screens targets in their normal cellular environment to identify potent, selective covalent small molecules, drawing on precedents like penicillin and AZT. Totus is advancing a pipeline focused on oncology and immunology & inflammation (I&I), including TOS-358, a covalent PI3Ka inhibitor, and a first-in-class covalent IRF5 inhibitor in clinical development. Headquartered in Emeryville, California, Totus was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and profiled in the API Evangelist network. As a clinical-stage drug-discovery company, Totus publishes no public developer API surface; this profile captures its corporate identity, web properties, and security posture.

providers.name: Breezebio
providers.description: BreezeBio (formerly GenEdit) is a South San Francisco genetic-medicine company developing precision-delivered nucleic acid therapies for autoimmune disease and oncology. Its proprietary NanoGalaxy platform uses non-lipid, hydrophilic polymer nanoparticles of tunable size, charge, and composition to selectively deliver DNA, RNA, and ribonucleoprotein payloads to specific tissues and cell types beyond the liver — including immune cells and targets in the heart, lung, and central nervous system. The company is advancing an internal therapeutic pipeline led by BRZ-101, which aims to restore immune tolerance in type 1 diabetes, and in February 2026 closed a $60M Series B backed by DCVC Bio, Sequoia Capital, and other investors. BreezeBio is a research-stage biopharmaceutical company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile tracks its corporate and identity surface within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Dewpoint Therapeutics
providers.description: Dewpoint Therapeutics is a biotechnology company applying the emerging science of biomolecular condensates to drug discovery. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, with an additional research site in Dresden, Germany, Dewpoint has built an AI-powered, end-to-end platform (ERSA, powered by ERSAi) spanning target discovery, condensate-modulating (c-mod) drug discovery, optimization, and development. Its pipeline targets previously undruggable diseases across oncology, neurodegeneration, cardiopulmonary, and virology, with collaborations including Bayer, Novo Nordisk, Evotec, and Chemify. Dewpoint is a General Catalyst portfolio company; it operates internal research platforms and the open CD-CODE condensate knowledge platform (condensates.com), but does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Frontier Medicines
providers.description: Frontier Medicines is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company pioneering the discovery and development of small-molecule covalent drugs against disease-causing proteins long considered undruggable. Its proprietary Frontier Platform pairs chemoproteomics with artificial intelligence and machine learning and a proprietary Druggability Atlas that maps thousands of novel covalent binding opportunities across the human proteome. Lead precision oncology candidates include FMC-376 (KRAS G12C), FMC-220 (a p53 Y220C reactivator), and FMC-242 (PI3Kalpha-RAS). Founded in 2018 with offices in Boston, Massachusetts and South San Francisco, California, the company is backed by DCVC and other life-science investors. Frontier Medicines was added to the API Evangelist network as a DCVC portfolio company; it publishes no public API or developer surface, so this profile captures company identity only.

providers.name: Generation Lab
providers.description: Generation Lab is a longevity science company founded in 2023 by Alina Su, UC Berkeley bioengineer Dr. Irina Conboy, and Michael Suswal, and backed by an $11M seed round led by Accel (Accel's first longevity bet). Its flagship SystemAge test measures biological age across roughly 460 biomarkers spanning 19 to 21 physiological systems and organs from an at-home, needle-free blood collection, returning a personalized aging report and science-backed action plan that ranges from lifestyle and supplement guidance to clinical interventions. The test is distributed through 300+ clinic partners across 18 countries and via a patient/provider portal. Generation Lab publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its public web, product, and legal surfaces.

providers.name: Latent Labs
providers.description: Latent Labs is a London- and San Francisco-based frontier AI lab founded in 2023 by Dr. Simon Kohl, a former senior research scientist on DeepMind's Nobel Prize-winning AlphaFold 2 and co-lead of DeepMind's protein design team. The company builds generative AI foundation models to make biology programmable, with the goal of enabling biotech and pharmaceutical partners to computationally generate and optimize therapeutic molecules. Latent Labs emerged from stealth in February 2025 with $50M in total funding ($40M Series A co-led by Radical Ventures and Sofinnova Partners, plus 8VC, Kindred Capital, Pillar VC, Flying Fish, Isomer, and angel investors including Jeff Dean, Aidan Gomez, and Mati Staniszewski). The company's proprietary model family includes Latent-X (atom-level de novo protein binder design for macrocycles and mini-binders), Latent-X2 (drug-like antibodies with low ex vivo immunogenicity), and Latent-Y (described as the first lab-validated agent for drug design). Models are accessed through the Latent Labs Platform (platform.latentlabs.com) — a no-code web application with a free tier and daily credits — and, for Latent-X2, via API for commercial partners. There is no public OpenAPI spec, SDK, or open-source release at this time; programmatic access is gated through partnerships@latentlabs.com and wet-lab validation is performed in-house at the company's San Francisco facility.

providers.name: Procyrion
providers.description: Procyrion, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage medical device company headquartered in Houston, Texas, developing Aortix, a catheter-deployed percutaneous mechanical circulatory support (pMCS) pump. Aortix is placed in the descending thoracic aorta and uses fluid entrainment to unload the heart and increase perfusion to the kidneys, targeting acute decompensated heart failure with diuretic resistance, prevention of acute kidney injury during cardiac surgery, cardiac unloading to limit myocardial infarct size, and longer-term chronic heart failure therapy. The device is under investigation in the DRAIN-HF pivotal IDE trial and is limited by federal law to investigational use; it is not approved for sale in any geography. Procyrion is a medical hardware and clinical company - it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Roivant
providers.description: Roivant Sciences Ltd. (Nasdaq: ROIV) is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical holding company that accelerates the development and commercialization of medicines through its distinctive "Vant" model, a network of nimble, focused subsidiary companies such as Immunovant, Priovant, and Pulmovant. Founded in 2014, Roivant advances a pipeline spanning immunology, dermatology, and other therapeutic areas, and has delivered multiple FDA approvals and Phase 3 trial successes. Roivant is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; it operates a corporate and investor web presence but publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Thyme Care
providers.description: Thyme Care is a value-based oncology care-navigation and support company that partners with health plans, providers, and employers to guide people through a cancer diagnosis and treatment. Its virtual oncology care team and navigators help members access care, coordinate with treating physicians, manage symptoms and side effects, understand costs, and improve outcomes across the cancer journey. Thyme Care delivers this through partner programs (Thyme Care Connect, Thyme Care Signal, Thyme Box, and Enhanced Supportive Care) rather than a public developer platform. As of this enrichment pass, no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or /.well-known API-discovery surface were found for Thyme Care; it is profiled here as a company, not an API provider.

providers.name: Unchained Labs
providers.description: Unchained Labs is a life-science tools company that designs, manufactures, and sells analytical instruments, automation, and consumables for biologics, gene therapy, cell therapy, nanoparticle, exosome, and genomics research. Its product line includes plate-based systems for protein characterization, concentration and quantification (Lunatic and Stunner), protein stability and formulation (Uncle), automated buffer exchange and sample prep (Big Tuna, Little Big Tuna), viscosity measurement, and lipid-nanoparticle synthesis and analysis. The company serves biopharma R&D, process development, and QC labs. Unchained Labs is primarily a hardware, reagent, and lab-software vendor; as of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, REST/GraphQL surface, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and enriched with verified company identity and link properties from its public website.

providers.name: Zag Bio
providers.description: Zag Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing thymus-targeted therapies for autoimmune diseases. The company engineers bifunctional antibodies that deliver self-antigens to antigen-presenting cells in the thymus, harnessing the body's natural process of central immune tolerance so developing immune cells learn to recognize, tolerate, and protect the body's own tissues. Its pipeline includes ZAG-101, a candidate for Type 1 Diabetes. Founded and incubated by Polaris Partners, Zag Bio launched publicly in October 2025 with an $80M Series A. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company; as a therapeutics developer it publishes no public API or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Alamar Biosciences
providers.description: Alamar Biosciences is a privately held life sciences company headquartered in Fremont, California, building precision proteomics tools aimed at the earliest detection of disease. Its NULISA (NUcleic acid Linked Immuno-Sandwich Assay) chemistry and Attobody reagents, run on the ARGO and ARGO HT automated immunoassay systems, deliver attomolar-sensitivity, high-multiplex protein measurement for biomarker discovery, translational research, neurodegeneration and immuno-oncology panels. Alamar publishes no public web API. Its developer-facing surface is open source rather than service based: the first-party NULISAseqR R package (GPL-3) for importing, normalizing, quality-controlling and analyzing NULISAseq XML output, documented at nulisaseqr.alamarbio.com, alongside the NULISA Analysis Software (NAS) that ships with the instruments.

providers.name: Create
providers.description: CREATE Medicines is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company developing in vivo CAR (chimeric antigen receptor) cell therapies using mRNA lipid-nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) delivery. Its platform reprograms immune cells, including T cells, NK cells, and myeloid cells, directly inside the body rather than extracting and engineering them ex vivo, with clinical and preclinical programs spanning oncology, autoimmune disease, and fibrosis. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. The enrichment pipeline found no developer or API surface; this is a clinical-stage therapeutics company, not a software or platform provider, so no API artifacts were produced (none is the correct, non-fabricated result).

providers.name: MPIRIQ
providers.description: MPIRIQ (MPiriQ Science Technologies GmbH) is a Munich-based healthcare software company that automates clinical documentation for medical practices and study centers. Its AI platform structures patient data directly inside existing EMR/PMS systems, runs quality and billing validation checks in the background, and connects real-world care data to clinical research through decentralized, GDPR-compliant pseudonymization. The platform helps practices participate in clinical trials via automated indication screening and patient recruitment, giving physicians time back while opening a research revenue stream. Founded in 2024 and backed by HV Capital and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Nature's Fynd
providers.description: Nature's Fynd is the consumer food brand of The Fynder Group, a fermentation biotechnology company that grows a complete protein (Fy Protein) from an extremophile fungus originally discovered in the geothermal springs of Yellowstone National Park. The Fynder Group operates as the central R&D, fermentation, and scaled-manufacturing hub behind Fynder Ingredients (specialty food and beverage ingredients), FynderBio (oral biopharmaceuticals), and Hydefy (bio-based performance materials). Nature's Fynd sells meat- and dairy-alternative consumer foods made from Fy Protein. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Rondo Therapeutics
providers.description: Rondo Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Hayward, California, developing immune-cell engaging bispecific antibodies designed to treat solid tumors by unleashing the immune system while maximizing efficacy and minimizing side effects. Founded in 2019 by Shelley Force Aldred and Nathan Trinklein, its pipeline includes RNDO-564 (Phase 1 for bladder cancer) plus programs targeting ovarian, endometrial, and renal cancers, backed by a Series A led by Canaan and Red Tree Venture Capital and a collaboration with Eli Lilly. Rondo publishes a corporate and pipeline website but exposes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API surface; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Santa Ana Bio
providers.description: Santa Ana Bio is a precision immunology company developing targeted therapies to stop autoimmune and inflammatory disease at the source. The company pairs a multi-omics discovery platform (integrating genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data) with a pipeline of bispecific and multi-specific antibody and antibody-drug-conjugate programs (SAB01, SAB05, SAB06) advancing toward IND submissions across 2026-2027. Backed by a16z and GV, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. It publishes a corporate and careers website but no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Verana Health
providers.description: Verana Health is a healthcare real-world data (RWD) and analytics company that transforms de-identified electronic health records from more than 90 million patients across 50+ EHR systems into curated, disease-specific datasets for life sciences and clinical research. Its VeraQ population health data engine harmonizes, tokenizes, and links structured and unstructured EHR data, claims, and medical images using clinician-directed curation, natural language processing, and machine learning, delivering Qdata modules across ophthalmology, urology, and neurology. Verana partners with medical specialty societies (including the AAO IRIS Registry) to power trial design, site and patient identification, real-world evidence studies, and quality-measure reporting. The company is HIPAA-compliant and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of GV. No public developer API or developer portal is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Visolis
providers.description: Visolis is a biomanufacturing company that combines synthetic biology with chemical catalysis to convert plant biomass into MEV (mevalonic acid), a proprietary platform molecule used to make sustainable, bio-based alternatives to petroleum-derived chemicals and fuels. Its products include bio-isoprene for synthetic rubber (a partnership with Zeon), AroSAF 100% bio-based sustainable aviation fuel, and non-toxic bio-based industrial solvents (piloted with the U.S. Department of Defense). Headquartered in San Leandro, California and led by CEO Deepak Dugar, Visolis is a climate-tech company surfaced as a DCVC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Visolis publishes a corporate marketing site but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Generate Biomedicines
providers.description: Generate Biomedicines is a Somerville, Massachusetts therapeutics company pioneering Generative Biology, a machine-learning-driven approach to de novo protein design across antibodies, peptides, enzymes, and gene therapies. Founded out of Flagship Pioneering and chaired by Noubar Afeyan, the company trains generative models on the full compendium of natural protein structures and sequences plus proprietary wet-lab data to design novel protein therapeutics computationally rather than by trial-and-error discovery. Its open-source flagship is Chroma, a programmable diffusion-based generative model for joint protein structure and sequence design published in Nature 2023 ("Illuminating protein space with a programmable generative model", doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06728-8) and released on GitHub under Apache 2.0 with pretrained weights available under a custom Chroma Parameters License (free for academic and nonprofit use). Chroma uses equivariant graph neural networks, diffusion modeling, and conditional random fields to sample all-atom protein structures with sub-quadratic complexity, supporting conditional generation via composable Conditioner modules for symmetry, substructure, shape, and secondary-structure constraints. The internal Generate Platform iterates on a "generate, build, measure, learn" loop that pairs in-silico design with high-throughput protein synthesis and characterization; the company reports having generated, built, and tested more than 42,000 proteins. Generate Biomedicines has platform collaborations with Amgen (six programs, January 2022) and Novartis (multiple programs, September 2024) and a CAR T collaboration with Roswell Park. Its clinical pipeline is led by GB-0895, a long-acting anti-TSLP antibody for severe asthma now in Phase 3 (SOLAIRIA study) with a parallel Phase 1 in COPD, plus preclinical programs GB-4362 (anti-free-MMAE for ADC oncology safety) and GB-5267 (MUC16 armored CAR T for ovarian cancer). The company priced its initial public offering in February 2026. Revenue derives from drug development, partner collaborations, and (for Chroma) commercial weights licensing; there is no public developer REST/HTTPS API or SDK for the Generate Platform itself — Chroma is consumed as a Python library installed via pip with model weights downloaded from chroma-weights.generatebiomedicines.com after registering for an API key.

providers.name: Newlight Technologies
providers.description: Newlight Technologies, Inc. is a Huntington Beach, California biotechnology company founded in 2003 and incorporated in Delaware that produces AirCarbon, a PHB biomaterial made by naturally-occurring ocean microorganisms that consume air and greenhouse gas. The company operates a commercial-scale biomanufacturing plant and sells AirCarbon as resin to industrial partners and as finished goods under the Restore foodware and Covalent fashion-accessory brands, positioning the material as a carbon-negative, home-compostable, ocean-degradable replacement for petroleum plastic. Newlight is a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no API reference and no machine-readable contract. Its only agent-reachable surface is the Wix platform Site MCP endpoint that its marketing site advertises in its own llms.txt.

providers.name: Obsidian Therapeutics
providers.description: Obsidian Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing engineered cell and gene therapies built on its proprietary cytoDRiVE platform, which uses drug-responsive domains to regulate therapeutic protein function with an FDA-approved small molecule. Its lead program, OBX-115, is in Phase 2 trials for advanced melanoma. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a life-sciences company with no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Rallybio
providers.description: Rallybio Corporation (NASDAQ RLYB) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in New Haven, Connecticut, founded in 2018, developing and commercializing life-transforming therapies for patients with severe and rare diseases. Its pipeline spans maternal-fetal health, complement dysregulation, hematology, and metabolic disorders, led by RLYB116, a differentiated complement component 5 (C5) inhibitor, and RLYB332, a long-acting matriptase-2 (MTP-2) antibody for iron-overload disorders. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a pharmaceutical company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures corporate identity only.

providers.name: Adagio Therapeutics
providers.description: Adagio Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2020 to discover, develop, and commercialize antibody-based therapies for serious infectious diseases, with an initial focus on SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory viruses. Its lead programs centered on monoclonal antibody candidates engineered for high potency and broad, evolution-resistant neutralization. The company was renamed Invivyd, Inc. in 2023 (Nasdaq: IVVD) and now advances antibody medicines such as PEMGARDA and the VYD2311 candidate. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network. As a life-sciences therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures corporate identity and policy links only.

providers.name: Aera Therapeutics
providers.description: Aera Therapeutics is a genetic-medicines biotechnology company founded by a team of scientists, investors, and company builders to unlock the potential of genetic medicines through next-generation delivery technologies and precision payloads. Aera develops multiple proprietary delivery platforms — including Targeted Lipid Nanoparticles (tLNPs) and protein-nanoparticle systems — to broaden the application of genetic medicines across many disease areas, advancing a broad preclinical pipeline toward the clinic. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network. Aera is a therapeutics company and publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface; this profile captures its corporate identity and domain-security posture. Sector: life-sciences.

providers.name: ARTBIO
providers.description: ARTBIO is a clinical-stage radiopharmaceutical company developing a new class of targeted Alpha Radioligand Therapies (ARTs) built on the lead-212 (212Pb) isotope. Founded in 2021 out of research at the University of Oslo and Norway's Radium Hospital by Roy Larsen and Oyvind Bruland - the scientific co-founders behind Xofigo - the company pairs a differentiated oncology pipeline with its proprietary AlphaDirect isotope-production technology, a first-of-its-kind 212Pb isolation method intended to enable distributed manufacturing and reliable supply of alpha radioligand therapies. Its lead program AB001 (212Pb-NG001) is in first-in-human Phase 1 trials in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, with additional preclinical and discovery programs across breast, head and neck, lung, pancreatic and other solid tumors. ARTBIO operates from Cambridge, Massachusetts and Oslo, is backed by F-Prime Capital, Third Rock Ventures, Omega Funds, Sofinnova Partners, B Capital, ARE and QIA, and is privately held. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification - software is not its product.

providers.name: Arvinas
providers.description: Arvinas is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company (NASDAQ: ARVN) headquartered in New Haven, Connecticut, developing targeted protein degradation therapeutics using its proprietary PROTAC (proteolysis targeting chimera) Discovery Engine. PROTAC molecules are heterobifunctional protein degraders that harness the body's natural protein-disposal system to eliminate disease-causing proteins rather than merely inhibiting them, with a therapeutic focus on oncology and neurology. Arvinas developed the first FDA-approved PROTAC protein degrader, VEPPANU (vepdegestrant). The company was founded on research from Yale University and maintains research partnerships across the industry. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; Arvinas is a life-sciences company and does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Auron Therapeutics
providers.description: Auron Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Newton, Massachusetts, developing therapies that target cell-state plasticity to address the underlying causes of disease across oncology and inflammatory disease indications. The company built the AURIGIN platform, which integrates multi-omic profiling and computational biology to map how cells change states and identify those states that can be therapeutically targeted. Auron was founded by Dr. Katharine Yen with co-founders Dr. Ross Levine, Dr. Eytan Stein, and Dr. Matthew Vander Heiden, a team drawing on experience from Agios Pharmaceuticals and its FDA-approved IDH inhibitor programs. It is backed by investors including Apollo, Arkin Bio, Casdin Capital, and DCVC Bio. As a therapeutics company Auron publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its corporate and legal web presence only.

providers.name: Bright Peak Therapeutics
providers.description: Bright Peak Therapeutics AG is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2018 and co-located in Allschwil, Switzerland (Switzerland Innovation Park Basel Area) and San Diego / Del Mar, California. The company engineers next-generation multi-functional immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune disease, using a protein-engineering and site-specific chemical-conjugation platform to build multi-functional PD-1 inhibitors and cytokine immunoconjugates that combine novel and clinically validated mechanisms in a single molecule. Its lead program, BPT567, is a first-in-class PD1-IL18 immunoconjugate that entered a Phase 1/2a clinical trial. The company has raised a USD 90 million Series C led by Johnson & Johnson Innovation (JJDC) alongside Versant Ventures, RA Capital Management, Fidelity, Qatar Investment Authority, Invus, Venrock, KB Investment, Alexandria Venture Investments and Northleaf Capital Partners. Bright Peak is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it publishes a corporate marketing site and no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: CoRegen
providers.description: CoRegen, Inc. (CoRegen Science) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Houston, Texas developing adoptive cell therapies for aggressive solid tumors. Its platform, licensed exclusively from the O'Malley Lab at Baylor College of Medicine, uses CRISPR gene editing to knock out the SRC-3 steroid receptor coactivator gene in regulatory T (Treg) cells, reprogramming them from immunosuppressors into tumor-killing effectors. The lead program, CRG-150, received FDA IND clearance for a first-in-human Phase 1/2a trial in advanced solid tumors, and the underlying science won the 2023 Cozzarelli Prize. CoRegen is a therapeutics organization, not a software company: it publishes a nine-page marketing and science site (about, the science, preclinical studies, pipeline, publications, leadership, news, careers, contact) and no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Engrail
providers.description: Engrail Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2019 and focused on precision neuroscience. The company develops innovative, precision-targeted small-molecule therapeutics aimed at the molecular mechanisms and neural circuits underlying nervous system disorders, combining internal discovery with strategic partnerships. Its pipeline includes candidates ENX-102, ENX-104, ENX-203, and ENX-205 for patients with devastating and life-limiting neurological conditions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public developer/API surface.

providers.name: Enlaza Therapeutics
providers.description: Enlaza Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in La Jolla, California developing first-in-class covalent protein biologics for cancer and other serious diseases. Its proprietary War-Lock technology uses engineered unnatural amino acids to enable protein drugs — including antibody-drug conjugates and T-cell engagers — to bind their disease targets irreversibly, aiming for sustained target occupancy and a prolonged biologic effect with minimal systemic exposure across oncology and immuno-oncology applications. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a corporate website but no public developer API surface.

providers.name: HistoSonics
providers.description: HistoSonics is a medical device company commercializing histotripsy, a non-invasive, non-thermal and non-ionizing sonic beam therapy that uses focused ultrasound to form a controlled bubble cloud which mechanically destroys and liquefies targeted tissue at a sub-cellular level. Its robotically assisted Edison Histotripsy System received U.S. FDA marketing authorization through the De Novo Classification Request process in October 2023 for the non-invasive destruction of liver tumors, making it the first histotripsy platform authorized anywhere in the world, and has since added CE Mark authorization in Europe and an FDA submission covering kidney tumors. The underlying science originated with researchers at the University of Michigan, and the company maintains clinical partnerships with the University of Michigan and the University of Wisconsin. HistoSonics publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API specification; its public web surface is a marketing, clinical-evidence, physician-education and eIFU site rather than an API platform.

providers.name: insitro
providers.description: insitro is a machine-learning-driven drug discovery and development company founded in 2018 by Daphne Koller and headquartered in South San Francisco, California. It combines large-scale in vitro cellular data generated in its own automated labs with human clinical and genetic data to build predictive models of biology, aiming to bring better drugs faster to the patients most likely to benefit. Its therapeutic focus spans metabolism, oncology, and neuroscience, and its interdisciplinary teams pair life scientists, data scientists, and engineers. insitro operates no public developer API; it maintains open-source research and infrastructure tooling (such as the redun workflow engine) on its GitHub organization. Backed by a16z, GV, and the SoftBank Vision Fund.

providers.name: Neurona Therapeutics
providers.description: Neurona Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotherapeutics company in South San Francisco, California, developing allogeneic regenerative neural cell therapies that permanently integrate into neural circuits to treat chronic disorders of the nervous system. Founded on nearly two decades of stem cell research from the University of California, San Francisco, its lead candidate NRTX-1001 (rezanecel) is an inhibitory interneuron cell therapy delivered as a single, minimally invasive dose for drug-resistant mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, and is advancing through the NTE001 and NTE002 studies toward the Phase 3 EPIC trial. UCB completed its acquisition of Neurona on June 2, 2026. The company publishes no public API, developer program, SDK, or machine-readable specification; its public surface is corporate and clinical, not developer-facing.

providers.name: Ollin Bio
providers.description: Ollin Bio is a privately held biotechnology company developing novel therapeutics, organizing its work around defined therapeutic areas and a product pipeline of drug candidates in development. Backed by a16z, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead. As a research-stage therapeutics company, Ollin Bio publishes a marketing and corporate website but does not expose a public developer program, API, documentation, or SDKs at this time. This profile records the company's public identity and web properties; it will be re-enriched if a public API surface ever appears.

providers.name: Pelage Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Pelage Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing regenerative medicines for hair loss based on hair follicle stem cell biology discovered by UCLA researchers. Its lead candidate, PP405, is a topically-applied small molecule that reactivates dormant hair follicle stem cells via a metabolic switch to stimulate regrowth, targeting androgenetic alopecia, drug-induced alopecia, and telogen effluvium; it is non-hormonal, non-invasive, and in Phase 2 clinical trials. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). It publishes a corporate site and a clinical-trials site but no public developer, API, or technical surface.

providers.name: Prime Medicine
providers.description: Prime Medicine is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a new class of differentiated one-time curative genetic therapies built on Prime Editing, a versatile, precise, and efficient gene editing technology that can search and replace disease-causing genetic sequences at their precise location in the genome without causing double-strand DNA breaks. The company is advancing a pipeline of programs across a broad range of diseases and, per its public materials, believes Prime Editing could theoretically correct approximately 90% of known disease-causing genetic mutations. It is publicly traded and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures).
