This is a corporate/life-sciences profile: the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Prudentia Sciences
providers.description: Prudentia Sciences provides a scientific intelligence layer powering life-sciences dealmaking. The platform unifies fragmented pharmaceutical and biotech data sources, applies expert-developed evaluation frameworks, and applies AI trained on drug development so that pharma companies, biotech firms, investors, and deal teams can assess pharmaceutical assets faster and with more confidence during M&A and licensing transactions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). No public API or developer surface was found during enrichment; the company operates as a single-tenant, SOC 2-aligned SaaS platform.

providers.name: Ray Therapeutics
providers.description: Ray Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing optogenetic, gene-based medicines to restore vision in people with blinding degenerative retinal diseases. Its approach reprograms surviving retinal neurons to detect light and transmit visual signals to the brain, independent of the underlying gene mutation. Lead programs include RTX-015 (retinitis pigmentosa and other inherited retinal diseases, Phase 1/2) and RTX-021 (Stargardt disease and geographic atrophy, IND-enabling). The company is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. Ray Therapeutics operates as a therapeutics developer and does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: RayzeBio
providers.description: RayzeBio is a clinical-stage radiopharmaceutical therapeutics company headquartered at 5505 Morehouse Drive, Suite 300, San Diego, California, and since 2024 a wholly owned Bristol Myers Squibb company. It develops targeted radiopharmaceutical therapies (RPTs) built on the alpha-emitting isotope actinium-225, led by RYZ101 (225Ac-DOTATATE) against somatostatin receptor 2 (SSTR2)-expressing tumors including gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, extensive-stage small cell lung cancer and hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer, alongside earlier programs targeting glypican-3 (GPC3) in hepatocellular carcinoma and ACP3, plus paired diagnostic imaging agents such as [68Ga]Ga-RAYZ-8009. Its public web presence is a WordPress corporate marketing site covering discovery capabilities, radioisotope manufacturing, the pipeline, posters and presentations, leadership and careers; the company operates no developer program and publishes no API, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and is profiled here for network completeness rather than for an API surface.

providers.name: Revalia Bio
providers.description: Revalia Bio transforms donated, non-transplantable human organs and tissues into high-fidelity biological datasets, using AI to accelerate drug and device development. The company has built "The Human Data Stack" — infrastructure spanning data generation, ingestion, integration, interpretation, and delivery of decision-ready clinical insights for pharma, biotech, healthcare, and regulatory customers. Applications include safety signal detection, dose and target selection, patient selection, and mechanism-of-action studies. Founded by Greg Tietjen (CEO) and Jenna DiRito (COO), it generated first revenue in 2023 and raised seed funding in 2024. Backed by Sierra Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Revalia Bio publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or technical surface — it is a B2B research-services company, not a developer platform.

providers.name: Seaport Therapeutics
providers.description: Seaport Therapeutics is a Boston-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing new medicines for patients with depression, anxiety and other neuropsychiatric disorders. Its proprietary Glyph platform — licensed from the Porter Research Group at Monash University — applies lymphatic-targeting oral prodrug chemistry so that more medicine reaches the bloodstream and brain while bypassing first-pass liver metabolism and reducing side effects. The clinical pipeline includes GlyphAllo (SPT-300), an oral allopregnanolone prodrug in Phase 2 for major depressive disorder; GlyphAgo (SPT-320), an oral agomelatine prodrug in Phase 2 for generalized anxiety disorder; and Glyph2BLSD (SPT-348), a pre-clinical non-hallucinogenic 2-bromo-LSD neuroplastogen. Seaport publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification; its public web surface is a corporate WordPress site plus a hosted investor-relations subdomain.

providers.name: Secretome Therapeutics
providers.description: Secretome Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company (formerly NeoProgen, founded 2018) developing allogeneic, off-the-shelf regenerative therapies derived from neonatal cardiac progenitor cells (nCPCs). Its lead candidate STM-01, and the cell-free secretome STM-2, target heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and Duchenne muscular dystrophy associated cardiomyopathy, and are in Phase 1 clinical study. The company publishes a corporate and investor-relations website covering its science, pipeline, team, patient/expanded-access policy and press releases; it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Sionna Therapeutics
providers.description: Sionna Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: SION) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered at 21 Hickory Drive, Waltham, Massachusetts, working to revolutionize the treatment paradigm for cystic fibrosis (CF) by developing novel small molecules that normalize the function of the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) protein. Building on more than a decade of its co-founders' research, the company advances a pipeline of first-in-class stabilizers of CFTR's nucleotide-binding domain 1 (NBD1) — the domain that carries F508del, the most common CF-causing mutation — including SION-719 and SION-451, alongside a portfolio of complementary CFTR modulators such as SION-2222 (galicaftor) and SION-109 designed to work synergistically with the NBD1 stabilizers. Sionna operates purely as a drug-development organization: its public web presence is a nine-page WordPress marketing site covering science, pipeline, careers, contact and legal material, plus a hosted investor-relations portal. It publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Solu Therapeutics
providers.description: Solu Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, pioneering a novel class of antibody therapeutics that unlock cell-surface targets by combining small molecules with effector antibodies through proprietary linker technology. Its two platform technologies are CyTAC (Cytotoxicity Targeting Chimera), which links cell-surface targets to antibodies that kill pathogenic cells, and TicTAC (Therapeutic Index Control Targeting Chimera), which gives long-acting small-molecule agonists and antagonists antibody-like pharmacokinetics. Its lead program, STX-0712, is a CyTAC targeting the GPCR CCR2 in Phase 1 trials for chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, with additional oncology and immunology programs advancing. Solu is a portfolio company of the venture firm DCVC. The company operates as a drug-discovery and clinical-development organization and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or programmatic surface.

providers.name: Structure Therapeutics
providers.description: Structure Therapeutics (NASDAQ: GPCR) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in South San Francisco, California, developing novel oral small-molecule medicines for chronic diseases with significant unmet medical need. The company applies a structure-based drug discovery platform focused on G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) to design once-daily oral therapies, with lead programs centered on oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonists for obesity and metabolic disease. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Structure Therapeutics maintains a corporate and investor web presence, but no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Vera Therapeutics
providers.description: Vera Therapeutics is a clinical- and commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Brisbane, California, developing treatments for serious immunological and inflammatory diseases of the kidney. Its lead program, atacicept (marketed as TRUTAKNA), is a dual BAFF/APRIL inhibitor for IgA nephropathy (IgAN). Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, Vera Therapeutics publishes a corporate and patient-facing website (veratx.com) but exposes no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface. Sector: life-sciences.

providers.name: Vivid Vision
providers.description: Vivid Vision is a digital vision care company that builds VR- and software-based tools for diagnosing and treating binocular vision disorders. Its products include a vision training system for amblyopia (lazy eye), strabismus, and convergence insufficiency; Vivid Vision Perimetry (VVP), a VR-based visual field test used as an endpoint in ophthalmology clinical trials for geographic atrophy, AMD, and glaucoma; and EYEBAB VT therapeutic exercises for clinical settings. Founded in 2014, the platform has been used by more than 100,000 patients across 50+ countries through eye-care practices and clinics. Vivid Vision is backed by Uncork Capital. The company is a patient- and clinician-facing vision-care provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface at this time.

providers.name: Anto Biosciences
providers.description: Anto Biosciences is a frontier biology AI lab making the gut microbiome computable for the first time. It builds foundation models for microbial communities and quality-aware, goal-directed sparsification algorithms that filter noise from microbiome data to predict how the gut microbiome affects drug efficacy, toxicity, and safety across diverse populations (by geography, age, and diet). Applications include population-specific drug response prediction, identifying failure mechanisms at the microbial metabolic-pathway level, and molecule optimization for broader effectiveness. Backed by Y Combinator, the company is early stage and research-focused; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or a GitHub organization. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead and enriched with verified identity links only (no API artifacts, none published).

providers.name: Iterum Therapeutics
providers.description: Iterum Therapeutics plc is a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company headquartered in Dublin, Ireland, focused on developing novel anti-infective medications to treat multi-drug resistant (MDR) bacterial infections. Its lead product, ORLYNVAH (sulopenem), is described as the first oral and IV penem antibiotic targeting gram-negative resistant infections. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Iterum Therapeutics is a pharmaceutical/biotech company and does not operate a public developer API; as of March 2026 the company entered liquidation following a High Court order in Ireland.

providers.name: Oncimmune
providers.description: Oncimmune is a biotechnology company specializing in antibody and autoantibody biomarker discovery for precision medicine. Its proprietary ImmunoINSIGHTS platform screens against 9,000+ human antigens using Luminex xMAP bead-based multiplexed immunoassay technology, minimal sample volumes, high-throughput automated robotic workflows, and proprietary machine-learning algorithms to identify immune-system signatures across immuno-oncology, autoimmune disease, and infectious disease. Products include the ImmunoINSIGHTS 2K targeted panels, custom biomarker discovery services, and bioinformatics/data-science multiomics integration. Oncimmune was acquired by Alden Scientific in July 2025. The company operates as a research and discovery services provider and does not publish a public developer or API platform.

providers.name: Schrödinger
providers.description: Schrödinger is a New York-headquartered (NASDAQ: SDGR) computational science company that develops a physics-based and AI-driven molecular simulation platform used across drug discovery and materials science. Its flagship desktop modeling environment is Maestro (MS Maestro for materials science), which integrates a deep stack of computational tools — Glide (docking), FEP+ (free energy perturbation), Desmond (molecular dynamics), Jaguar (quantum chemistry), Prime (protein structure prediction), BioLuminate (biologics), LigPrep, QikProp, SiteMap, and WaterMap — together with the Schrödinger-maintained PyMOL visualization system. LiveDesign is the cloud-native enterprise design lab where chemists, biologists, and program teams collaborate on molecules, run computational workflows, and integrate experimental data; it exposes a snap-in API framework for connecting in-house and third-party tooling. The Schrödinger Python API (current release 2026-1) is the primary developer surface, providing programmatic access to molecular structures, Maestro automation, jobcontrol, Glide, FEP+, Desmond, Jaguar, MacroModel, Prime, BioLuminate, and LiveDesign integration (login, export, dataset and column management). Schrödinger also ships KNIME extensions, command-line drivers for every computational product, and maintains a meaningful open-source footprint on GitHub — including PyMOL, maeparser, coordgenlibs, sketcher, gpusimilarity, csmiles, and the fixed-data-table-2 React component. The business has two segments — software licensing to global pharma, biotech, and materials companies, and a co-developed and proprietary drug discovery pipeline. There is no public developer signup or self-serve REST API; access to the platform, Python API, and LiveDesign is gated through commercial licensing and the my.schrodinger.com customer portal.

providers.name: Inovia Bio
providers.description: Inovia Bio is a TechBio company delivering drug development strategy and evidence generation for biotech and pharmaceutical organizations, aiming to combine big-pharma impact with biotech speed. It pairs purpose-built platforms with advisory services to produce regulatory-grade evidence, covering clinical development planning and trial design, therapeutic product profiles (TPP), development, regulatory and commercial strategy, Integrated Evidence Plans (IEP/IEGP), Real World Evidence (RWE) for regulatory submissions, and clinical program rescue. Its Study Designer platform (diagity.inovia.bio) supports study design workflows. Inovia Bio is a Seedcamp portfolio company; no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation are published at this time.

providers.name: Inscripta
providers.description: Inscripta, Inc. was a Boulder, Colorado digital genome engineering company founded in 2015 that built the Onyx benchtop platform — an automated CRISPR instrument, consumables, assays and a cloud-based Inscripta Engineering Portal that let scientists design and track millions of precise single-cell genome edits in one experiment. It licensed the MAD7 nuclease, acquired Infinome Biosciences and Sestina Bio in 2023 to pivot toward sustainable biomanufacturing, and merged with Manus (Manus Bio) in April 2025 to form an end-to-end bioalternatives company. Inscripta publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification; its only public developer artifact is BioCantor, an MIT-licensed Python genome-annotation library on PyPI and GitHub. inscripta.com now serves a single merger landing page pointing at manusbio.com.

providers.name: Inquis Medical
providers.description: Inquis Medical is a privately funded medical device company founded in 2020 and headquartered at 1530 O'Brien Drive in Menlo Park, California, dedicated to advancing the treatment of venous thromboembolic disease (VTE). Its flagship product, the AVENTUS Precision Thrombectomy System, is a single-catheter mechanical thrombectomy platform that combines a directional intelligent tip with an integrated 5F navigation catheter and dilator, TrueClot proprietary tissue-sensing that gives the operator real-time feedback on what the catheter tip is engaging (wall latch, lollipops, clogs), and in-line filtration with autologous blood reinfusion that reduces blood loss without capital equipment. The AVENTUS Thrombectomy System received FDA 510(k) clearance for peripheral indications and, in June 2025, for the treatment of pulmonary embolism; the company also ships the AVENTUS Introducer Sheath and the AVENTUS Clot Management System. Inquis raised a $40 million Series B in 2024 and a $75 million Series C to scale commercial adoption. Inquis Medical is a clinical hardware company: it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API contract, and its public GitHub organization holds a single empty embedded-firmware repository.

providers.name: Pathos
providers.description: Pathos (Pathos AI, Inc.) is an AI-enabled, clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2022 by Eric Lefkofsky and Ryan Fukushima that applies artificial intelligence and large-scale multimodal patient data to oncology drug development. Its PathOS platform is organized around three engines — Scout (AI asset selection that matches an investigational therapy to the patient subgroup most likely to respond), Sprint (small autonomous clinical-execution pods that design and run biomarker-driven trials), and Foundry (the oncology foundation model built in partnership with Tempus and AstraZeneca) — trained against a stated corpus of more than 200 petabytes of multimodal clinical, molecular and imaging data linked to patient outcomes. The company raised a $365M Series D in May 2025 at roughly a $1.6B valuation, completed the acquisition of Rain Oncology, and is advancing a precision-oncology pipeline that includes a CBP/p300 inhibitor and a brain-penetrant PRMT5 inhibitor. Pathos sells partnership and co-development to pharma and biotech; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: PolyXLabs
providers.description: PolyXLabs is a Techstars-backed biotechnology and sustainable-materials company developing biodegradable plastic alternatives from lignocellulose-based biomass, including food waste such as spent coffee grounds. The company produces customized, toxin-free, microplastic-free polymers designed to be lightweight and durable as drop-in replacements for conventional plastics in consumer goods and packaging, with operations across the United States and Europe and headquarters in Martonvasar, Hungary. PolyXLabs currently publishes no public API or developer surface; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Prellis Biologics
providers.description: Prellis Biologics is a Berkeley, California biotechnology company that discovers fully human antibody therapeutics by combining wet-lab human immunology with machine learning. Its EXIS (Externalized Immune System) platform uses LNO lymph node organoids — 3D tissue printed with holographic two-photon photolithography — to recreate human lymph node biology in vitro, raise true human antibody responses across genetically diverse donors, and feed the resulting sequence and characterization data into generative AI models that predict and optimize candidates in an iterative lab loop. The company sells antibody discovery collaborations and licensed therapeutic programs to pharmaceutical partners rather than software, and publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Rgenix
providers.description: Rgenix, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded by scientists from The Rockefeller University to discover and develop first-in-class small molecules and biologics against previously undruggable drivers of cancer metastasis, using its proprietary RNA-DRIVEr target-discovery platform. Its programs include ompenaclid (RGX-202), an oral SLC6A8/creatine-transporter inhibitor in Phase 2 for RAS-mutant colorectal cancer, abequolixron (RGX-104), an oral LXR agonist in Phase 1b/2, and RGX-019-MMAE, a MERTK-targeting antibody-drug conjugate. The company changed its corporate name from Rgenix to Inspirna in September 2021 and operates from Long Island City, New York. It is a therapeutics developer with no public API, developer program, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Andes
providers.description: Andes (Andes Ag, Inc.) is a climate-technology and agricultural-biotechnology company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Alameda, California. Andes engineers and selects beneficial soil microorganisms that are applied alongside seed in commodity row-crop production — corn, soybean, wheat and canola — where they accelerate the natural conversion of atmospheric carbon dioxide into stable soil inorganic carbon (carbonate minerals), a process the company calls Microbial Carbon Mineralization. Andes sells the resulting durable carbon dioxide removal as verified credits to corporate buyers and Scope 3 programs, and pays participating growers through the Andes Carbon Program. The company published the first Microbial Carbon Mineralization methodology, developed with EcoEngineers under ISO 14064, and has run field trials with Bayer, Cargill, Corteva, Nutrien and Wilbur-Ellis. Andes has raised roughly $38M, including a Series A co-led by Leaps by Bayer and Cavallo Ventures, and its shares trade on private secondary venues including EquityZen and Nasdaq Private Market. Andes publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Infinitopes
providers.description: Infinitopes is an Oxford University spinout biotech company (founded 2021, based at the BioEscalator in Oxford, UK) developing off-the-shelf precision cancer vaccines aimed at preventing deaths from cancer metastases. Its proprietary Precision Immunomics platform identifies tumor-specific antigens by integrating immunopeptidomics, advanced laboratory methods, machine learning, and validated biological testing across cancer types, paired with engineered viral vectors that elicit protective CD8 T-cell responses. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Amplify Partners (also supported by Cancer Research UK). This is a digital-biology company profile; Infinitopes publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Insempra
providers.description: Insempra is a biotechnology company that produces sustainable, bio-based ingredients using precision fermentation. It develops alternatives to petrochemical and naturally-extracted ingredients for the beauty and personal care, food and nutrition, and fibers and performance materials industries. Products include a bio-based Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol fragrance ingredient, an Omega-7 biolipid, and Biomelanin (in development), produced from agricultural and forestry waste streams through circular manufacturing. Insempra is a portfolio company of EQT Ventures and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Kiko Labs
providers.description: Kiko Labs is a neuroscience-based early-learning company (a 500 Global portfolio company) that builds adaptive brain-training games for children ages 3-7. Its flagship product, Kiko's Thinking Time, is a voice-guided iOS app developed with Harvard and UC Berkeley neuroscientists with support from the US Department of Education and National Science Foundation. The program trains executive functions — working memory, inhibition, focus, and cognitive flexibility — through progressive games, and includes a parent and educator dashboard for tracking skill development. Kiko Labs is a consumer edtech company and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Seismic Therapeutic
providers.description: Seismic Therapeutic is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing transformative biologic medicines for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. The company pairs structural biology with machine learning through its proprietary IMPACT platform to design multi-functional antibodies and Immunoglobulin Sculpting (IgSc) enzymes across cell-mediated, allergic, and antibody-mediated immune diseases. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As a therapeutics R&D company it publishes no public developer or API surface at seismictx.com; this profile captures its corporate identity only.

providers.name: Alterome Therapeutics
providers.description: Alterome Therapeutics is a clinical-stage precision oncology company founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Diego, California, backed by Canaan Partners. The company designs alteration-specific cancer therapies using deep biology and chemistry expertise paired with an in-house computational chemistry platform ("The Kraken"), a custom CPU/GPU compute array for physics-based molecular simulation and drug design. Its clinical pipeline includes ALTA2618, a mutation-selective inhibitor for AKT1 E17K-driven cancers, and ALTA3263, an oral pan-KRAS ON-state inhibitor targeting more than 90% of KRAS mutations in cancer. Alterome was surfaced through the Canaan Partners portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Merida Biosciences
providers.description: Merida Biosciences is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company developing precision immunology therapies for autoimmune and allergic disorders. The company targets the pathogenic drivers of antibody-driven diseases with the goal of durable clinical responses while minimizing the side effects of current non-specific autoimmune treatments. Launched in 2025 with $121 million in funding and backed by GV, Merida operates as a preclinical therapeutics company with a science-and-pipeline website and no public developer, API, or technical product surface.

providers.name: ElevateBio
providers.description: ElevateBio is an advanced therapies technology company and contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) for cell and gene therapies, headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts. Through its BaseCamp cGMP manufacturing and process-development business and its centers of excellence, ElevateBio provides end-to-end capabilities spanning gene editing, viral vectors (AAV and lentivirus), mRNA and RNA therapeutics, induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), analytical and process development, and regulatory CMC support, helping partners advance genetic medicines from concept through commercialization. Surfaced as a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund and profiled in the API Evangelist network, ElevateBio operates as a science- and manufacturing-driven organization rather than a public API provider; this profile captures its identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Epic Bio
providers.description: Epic Bio (legally Epicrispr Biotechnologies, Inc.) is a clinical-stage genetic medicines company in South San Francisco, California, founded in 2018 by Stanford CRISPR pioneer Stanley Qi, Ph.D. It develops epigenetic editing therapies that modulate gene expression without cutting DNA, built on its proprietary Gene Expression Modulation System (GEMS) platform — a combination of ultracompact DNA-binding proteins (CasMINI, CasONYX), tailored guide RNAs, and a large library of transcriptional and epigenomic modulators. Its lead program EPI-321 is in first-in-human clinical study for facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD), with preclinical programs in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency and heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. The company is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes a corporate and scientific website but no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Experic
providers.description: Experic is a specialist powder-handling contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) founded in 2018, headquartered in Cranbury, New Jersey, with an EU clinical supply center in Ireland. The company provides process, analytical and formulation development, clinical and commercial cGMP manufacturing, dry powder inhalation (DPI) and capsule/powder dosing, autoinjector and pen assembly, and clinical trial packaging, labeling, storage and logistics. Experic is a physical-goods manufacturing and clinical supply services business; it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Geneos Therapeutics
providers.description: Geneos Therapeutics is a clinical-stage (Phase 2b) biotherapeutics company in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania developing DNA-based personalized immunotherapies for cancer (PICs). Its GT-EPIC neoantigen-targeting platform sequences a patient's tumor, identifies the targetable neoantigens, and encodes up to roughly 40 of them into a synthetic DNA plasmid drug product delivered intradermally alongside a plasmid-encoded IL-12 adjuvant and CELLECTRA electroporation. Geneos was spun out of Inovio Pharmaceuticals and licenses that immunotherapy platform exclusively; it has run clinical work in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and glioblastoma (GBM) and is advancing toward a Phase 2b HCC trial. Geneos is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Hongene Biotech
providers.description: Hongene Biotech Corporation is a nucleic acid contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) founded in 1998, with nearly 30 years of RNA-focused expertise. It offers vertically integrated services spanning oligonucleotide API manufacturing (from preclinical to commercial, GMP up to tonne scale), mRNA CDMO services (raw materials through enzymes and lipids to GMP manufacture and fill-finish), custom chemical synthesis of nucleic acid building blocks, and chemoenzymatic ligation for siRNA and sgRNA. Hongene supplies premium nucleic acid raw materials worldwide and runs an online store for direct-purchase reagents. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan and enriched from Hongene public web surfaces; the company publishes no developer API.

providers.name: Immunai
providers.description: Immunai is a New York-headquartered biotechnology company, founded in December 2018, that maps the human immune system at single-cell resolution and applies machine learning to drug discovery and development. Its central asset is AMICA (Annotated Multiomic Immune Cell Atlas), a cell-level immune knowledge base built from single-cell multiomics — RNA transcriptome, surface proteome, TCR/BCR repertoire and spatial transcriptomics — harmonized across thousands of public and proprietary studies covering hundreds of diseases and immune cell types, paired with an ImmunoDynamics Engine used for target discovery, preclinical evaluation and clinical trial optimization. Immunai works through partnerships with biopharmaceutical companies and research institutions rather than a self-serve product, and as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable specification or SDKs. Offices are in New York, Tel Aviv, Prague and Zurich; the company acquired Dropprint Genomics (2021) and Nebion (2021).

providers.name: Inari
providers.description: Inari Agriculture, Inc. — "The SEEDesign company" — is a Cambridge, Massachusetts agricultural biotechnology company founded by Flagship Pioneering in 2016, with additional sites in West Lafayette, Indiana and Ghent, Belgium. Its SEEDesign platform combines genomics, artificial intelligence and predictive design with a multiplex gene-editing toolbox to accelerate crop improvement in soybean, corn and wheat, targeting 10-20% yield gains alongside roughly 40% reductions in nitrogen and water use. Inari runs a partner-first, business-to-business model, licensing designed seed to independent seed companies and breeders rather than selling to farmers directly. Inari publishes an llms.txt at inari.com/llms.txt but operates no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract; its data platform (Databricks-based) is internal. Not to be confused with the unrelated medical-device company Inari Medical.

providers.name: Nervonik
providers.description: Nervonik, Inc. is a clinical-stage medical device company in Los Angeles, California, founded in 2020 by CEO Aydin Babakhani, developing miniaturized peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS) neuromodulation implants for chronic neuropathic pain in high-motion anatomy. Its platform pairs proprietary wireless power delivery and miniaturized implantable leads with integrated sensing circuitry that records evoked compound action potentials (ECAPs) and other biomarkers, enabling closed-loop, patient-specific stimulation as an opioid-free alternative to spinal cord stimulators and pharmacological therapy. The company completed a first-in-human feasibility study and closed an oversubscribed $52.5M Series B in April 2026 led by Amzak Health, after a $13M Series A in March 2025. Nervonik publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract; its public web surface is a WordPress marketing and investor-relations site.

providers.name: Pharmaron
providers.description: Pharmaron is a life-science contract research, development, and manufacturing organization (CRO/CDMO) providing R&D services across the full drug-discovery and development pipeline for the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industry. Its services span laboratory research, chemistry, biology, drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics, safety assessment, chemistry-manufacturing-and-controls (CMC), and clinical development for small molecules, biologics, and cell and gene therapies. Pharmaron operates globally with facilities in China, the US, and the UK and is publicly listed. It is a B2B partner to drug developers and does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: Vedana Therapeutics
providers.description: Vedana Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation medicines for migraine prevention. Founded by biotech investor Anurag Agarwal and antibody-development veteran Leon Garcia, the company emerged from stealth in June 2026 with a $46 million Series A co-led by Westlake BioPartners and Canaan Partners, with participation from Dawn Biopharma and Alexandria Venture Investments. Vedana is building a portfolio of long-acting, subcutaneously dosed monoclonal antibodies that go beyond CGRP by targeting PACAP (pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating peptide) and other CGRP-independent pathways, aiming to deliver complete and lasting relief for the majority of migraine patients who remain suboptimally controlled on current standard of care. Its preclinical pipeline includes VDN-0100 (anti-PACAP antibody, first-in-human planned 2027), VDN-0200 (PACAP x CGRP bispecific), and two undisclosed programs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Vedana is a therapeutics company and publishes no public API or developer surface; this record captures its corporate identity for discovery.

providers.name: Averna Therapeutics
providers.description: Averna Therapeutics is a genetic-medicine biotechnology company creating what it calls the last, great missing tool required to break through the most persistent barriers in genetic medicine. Backed by Insight Partners, the company was recognized as an Endpoints 11 Most Promising Biotech Company in 2025 and has presented at the 44th Annual J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference. As a therapeutics R&D company it does not currently publish any public developer program, API, SDK, or API documentation surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company identity record only.

providers.name: Bland Company
providers.description: The Bland Company is a London-based food-technology and biotechnology startup building functional plant proteins that replace eggs in food manufacturing. Its feedstock-agnostic process upcycles underused agricultural side streams into flavor-neutral, cost-stable proteins engineered to match animal-protein functionality — solubility, foaming, gelling, and emulsifying — for bakery, sauces, beverages, and snacks. The company raised a ~$2.7M pre-seed round led by Initialized Capital. It publishes no public developer API surface (no docs, SDKs, or GitHub); this profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company/portfolio lead.

providers.name: Twig
providers.description: Twig (twig.bio) is a UK biotechnology company using artificial intelligence and machine learning to design sustainable bioengineered ingredients — "AI defined ingredients that don't cost the earth." Its proprietary twig:tech platform pairs bio:drive, an AI/ML design engine that generates and scores novel microbe designs across pathway and enzyme selection, gene edits, and expression levels, with grow:bot, an automated high-throughput lab that builds and tests those designs and feeds every result back into the next design cycle. Twig aims to cultivate clean ingredients from bacteria via fermentation rather than extracting them from the ground or sea or producing them with fossil fuels. Twig is a Seedcamp portfolio company and is backed by additional early-stage investors. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC portfolio lead; Twig currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface — its api./app. subdomains resolve to internal infrastructure — so this pass captures company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: Windfall Bio
providers.description: Windfall Bio transforms methane emissions into organic fertilizer and carbon credits using proprietary non-GMO methane-eating microbes (methanotrophs). The company operates across agriculture, coal mining, oil & gas, and waste management, capturing methane at the source and converting it into a soil amendment while generating verifiable carbon credits. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the latest enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: LyGenesis
providers.description: LyGenesis is a Pittsburgh-based clinical-stage cell therapy company developing allogeneic regenerative therapies that use a patient's own lymph nodes as bioreactors to grow functioning ectopic organs. Its lead program transplants donor hepatocytes into upper-abdominal lymph nodes via endoscopic ultrasound to treat end-stage liver disease and is in a Phase 2a clinical trial; preclinical proof-of-concept programs target thymus (aging), kidney (end-stage renal disease) and pancreas (Type 1 diabetes). LyGenesis is a laboratory and clinical-research organization, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and this profile records that absence rather than any API surface.

providers.name: Bindbridge
providers.description: Bindbridge is an AI-driven molecular discovery company founded in 2025 and based in Cambridge, UK, developing next-generation crop protection through targeted protein degradation. Its BRIDGE platform uses AI to discover and design molecular glues and targeted protein degraders with novel modes of action against weeds and crop diseases, combining AI candidate generation, computational docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and free-energy binding calculations to accelerate agricultural R&D across herbicides, insecticides, and fungicides. The company raised $3.8M to help reduce billion-dollar crop losses and is backed by Speedinvest. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile; it publishes no public API or developer surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Elligo Health Research
providers.description: Elligo Health Research is a healthcare-enabling clinical research organization (CRO) that embeds clinical trials directly into real-world healthcare settings. Through its proprietary IntElligo Research Stack and System of Accelerated Research (SOAR) model, Elligo connects sponsors and CROs to known, diverse patient populations across 115+ hospitals and health systems, 200+ healthcare-based sites, and 100+ research-based sites. Services span site networks, patient access and recruitment, decentralized and hybrid trial solutions, site support and staffing, and concierge patient retention and travel logistics. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Elligo is tracked as a portfolio-lead in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Empirico
providers.description: Empirico is a biotechnology company that powers therapeutic discovery with human genetics and small interfering RNA (siRNA) medicines. Combining internal capabilities in human genetics and siRNA chemistry with partner expertise, the company identifies naturally occurring genetic variations associated with health benefits and develops precision oligonucleotide therapeutics for common diseases with significant unmet medical need. In October 2024 Empirico entered a licensing agreement with GSK worth up to $745 million for a clinical-stage oligonucleotide targeting respiratory disease (COPD). Empirico is backed by DCVC. It is a pharmaceutical R&D company and does not operate a public technology or API platform.

providers.name: Healx
providers.description: Healx is a Cambridge, UK clinical-stage biotechnology company that uses artificial intelligence to discover and develop new treatments for rare diseases. Its Healnet platform pairs generative AI with drug-discovery and rare-disease expertise to build a biomedical knowledge graph from public and proprietary sources - biomedical literature, disease and biochemical datasets, clinical trials and patents - and to identify novel uses for known compounds. Founded by David Brown and Tim Guilliams, Healx advances its own therapeutic pipeline (including its NF1 lead candidate HLX-1502) and partners with pharma companies such as Sanofi. Healx does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: KromaTiD
providers.description: KromaTiD (KROMASURE) is a Boulder, Colorado single-cell analysis life-science tools and services company founded in 2016, built around its proprietary directional Genomic Hybridization (dGH) platform. dGH probes only the parental strand of DNA, which lets it resolve orientation-specific structural variation — inversions, translocations, insertions and other complex rearrangements — cell by cell, at resolutions that next-generation sequencing and conventional FISH cannot reach. The company sells the KROMASURE platform and the dGH in-Site, dGH SCREEN, kBand and PinPoint product lines as kits and as lab services, aimed at cell and gene therapy developers who need insertional-mutagenesis risk assessment, genotoxicity profiling, edit optimization, starting-material and donor qualification, cell-line characterization and batch-release testing for CMC and FDA IND submissions. Its work has also been used by NASA for spaceflight radiation research. KromaTiD publishes no developer program, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract; its only authenticated surface is a Cognidox-backed customer document portal at my.kromatid.com.

providers.name: PrognomiQ
providers.description: PrognomiQ Inc. is a Redwood City, California multi-omics diagnostics company, spun out of Seer (NASDAQ: SEER) in 2020, that combines proteomic, genomic, transcriptomic and metabolomic measurement with machine learning to detect cancer and other complex diseases earlier from a blood draw. Its first commercial product, ProVue Lung, is a proteomics-based laboratory developed test (LDT) intended to aid early detection of lung cancer. PrognomiQ is a clinical laboratory and life sciences business rather than a software vendor: as of this profile it publishes a six-page corporate marketing site, a public GitHub organization holding forks of open-source data-engineering tooling, and no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Radionetics Oncology
providers.description: Radionetics Oncology is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing precision radiopharmaceutical treatments for cancer. The company designs small-molecule radioligands that target G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) to selectively deliver targeted radiation therapy to solid tumors, including breast and lung cancer, combining GPCR biology expertise with medicinal chemistry. Radionetics entered a strategic agreement with Eli Lilly in 2024. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public developer, API, or technical-integration surface at this time.

providers.name: VeriSIM Life
providers.description: VeriSIM Life is an AI-driven drug discovery and development company that applies mechanistic artificial intelligence and quantitative simulation to reduce the cost, time, and failure rate of translating drug candidates into clinical trials. Its BIOiSIM platform is a biosimulation decision engine that can screen large libraries of drug-like compounds and run simulation scenarios across species and dosing regimens, while AtlasGEN designs novel molecules and evaluates them for safety and efficacy. The company operates PulmoSIM Therapeutics as a subsidiary. VeriSIM Life exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; the platform is accessed through partnerships and demos. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Varda Space Industries
providers.description: Varda Space Industries is an American space manufacturing company founded in 2021 and headquartered in El Segundo, California. Varda designs, builds and flies the W-Series, a free-flying orbital production satellite paired with a hypersonic reentry capsule, so that materials can be processed in microgravity and returned to Earth. The company sells three lines of service: biopharmaceutical processing (small-molecule crystallization that gravity disrupts on Earth), a government hypersonic flight testbed that uses the capsule's Mach 25 reentry as a test article carrier, and general microgravity research flights. Varda is a hardware and manufacturing-services business rather than a software vendor: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification, and customer-facing technical interfaces are documented in a downloadable Payload User Guide PDF.

providers.name: Enko Chem
providers.description: Enko Chem, Inc. (Enko) is an agricultural life sciences company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Mystic, Connecticut, where it operates an 89,000 sq ft research lab and greenhouse campus. Enko discovers and develops next-generation crop protection chemistry — weed, disease, insect and soil-pest control — using its proprietary ENKOMPASS platform, which combines DNA-encoded library screening, structure-based design, artificial intelligence and machine learning to identify new modes of action and lead molecules faster and at lower cost than conventional agrochemical R&D. Enko works through partnerships with Syngenta, Bayer, Nufarm and the Gates Foundation Strategic Investment Fund rather than selling software, and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Formation Bio
providers.description: Formation Bio (formerly TrialSpark, founded 2016 in New York City) is a tech-driven, AI-native pharmaceutical company that aims to bring new treatments to patients faster and more efficiently. Rather than discovering drugs, Formation Bio in-licenses and acquires clinical-stage drug assets from pharma companies, universities, and biotech firms, then develops them using proprietary technology platforms, process automation, and large language models applied across the drug development lifecycle — patient recruitment, e-consent, data management, monitoring, and biostatistics. The company rebranded from TrialSpark to Formation Bio in 2023 as it moved from a pure clinical-trial software platform to combined platform-plus-asset ownership. It raised a $372M Series D in 2024 and announced a first-in-class AI collaboration with Sanofi and OpenAI. Formation Bio operates hybrid teams across New York City, Boston, the San Francisco Bay Area, and North Carolina's Research Triangle. It is a private company with no public developer API program; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Strand Therapeutics
providers.description: Strand Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, founded by biological engineers out of MIT — including Jacob Becraft (CEO), Tasuku Kitada (President, Head of R&D), Ron Weiss and Darrell J. Irvine — around what the company describes as the first mRNA programming language. Strand engineers programmable genetic medicines across three named platforms: SignalPath LNPs for tissue-selective delivery of mRNA payloads, SignalLock RNA which restricts expression to target tissues and deactivates it elsewhere, and SignalScript RNA for self-replicating and circular RNA constructs. Its clinical pipeline includes STX-001, STX-003 (systemic tumor delivery, entering the clinic in 2026) and STX-005 (in vivo CAR T), targeting solid tumors, blood cancers and autoimmune disease. Strand operates no developer program and publishes no API, SDK, webhook or machine-readable specification of any kind; its corporate site is a static Webflow property behind Cloudflare with no content API, no feed and no sitemap. It is catalogued here because it appears in the API Evangelist secondary-market harvest backlog, and this profile records the honest zero.

providers.name: TimeTrace Labs
providers.description: TimeTrace Labs is a London-based mathematics and artificial intelligence company building the measurement layer for healthcare, spun out of a decade of research at the University of Oxford and backed by Seedcamp and Fly Ventures. Its quantitative measurement platform separates signal from noise in multimodal physiological time-series (kinematics, EEG, ECG, actigraphy, glucose, voice), powering analytics for drug development, clinical trials, and public health that the company delivers to partners through secure APIs and a compliant analytics dashboard — though it publishes no public developer portal or API documentation yet.

providers.name: Agomab Therapeutics
providers.description: Agomab Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company (Nasdaq: AGMB) developing novel disease-modifying therapies for fibro-inflammatory diseases, with an initial focus on chronic fibrotic indications of high unmet medical need such as Crohn's disease and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Building on deep expertise in growth factor biology, Agomab advances a pipeline of small-molecule and antibody candidates targeting the pathways that drive tissue fibrosis and inflammation. Headquartered in Belgium with operations across Europe and the United States, the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a biopharmaceutical company it publishes a corporate and investor-relations web presence rather than a public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the network catalog.

providers.name: Alchemab Therapeutics
providers.description: Alchemab Therapeutics is a UK-based clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation antibody therapeutics for hard-to-treat diseases. Its "Adaptive Immunity" platform identifies naturally resilient individuals, such as long-term cancer survivors, and harnesses their protective antibodies, using artificial intelligence and deep learning to translate these natural immune responses into novel human-derived therapeutics across neurodegeneration, oncology, and other areas of high unmet need. Alchemab was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As a research-stage therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API program, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

providers.name: Alpine Bio
providers.description: Alpine Bio is a molecular-farming biotechnology company (formerly Nobell Foods and Alpine Roads), founded in 2016 and based in South San Francisco, California. It produces next-generation protein ingredients and bioactives from plants using advanced purification and molecular farming, having expressed more than 15 complex proteins including the world's first plant-derived casein, fractionated soy protein isolates, and activated iron-loaded lactoferrin. The company sells high-purity, clean-label ingredients to food and beverage formulators for applications such as protein shakes, bars, coffee creamers, iron supplements, yogurt, and clear protein sodas, and markets animal-free dairy products under the Nobell Foods brand. It is a portfolio company of a16z surfaced in the API Evangelist network; Alpine Bio publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Autobahn Therapeutics
providers.description: Autobahn Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in San Diego, California, developing regenerative medicines for central nervous system (CNS) disorders. The company pairs a proprietary brain-targeting chemistry platform - which creates orally administered small-molecule prodrugs designed to cross the blood-brain barrier - with validated human biology and biomarker-driven development strategies. Its pipeline includes elunetirom (its lead clinical program, being developed for indications such as bipolar depression), ABX-101 (a next-generation CNS-active S1P molecule), and ABX-003. Autobahn is backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners and Insight Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; the company does not currently publish a public developer API, so this record captures company identity and published web properties only.

providers.name: BreezeBio (formerly GenEdit)
providers.description: BreezeBio, Inc. (formerly GenEdit) is a clinical-stage genetic medicines company based in South San Francisco, California, solving the central delivery problem of gene editing and genetic medicine. Its proprietary NanoGalaxy platform is a library of thousands of non-viral, non-lipid polymer nanoparticles engineered to deliver genetic payloads (mRNA, DNA, and CRISPR ribonucleoprotein) to specific cell types and tissues without triggering an immune response. The company is advancing an internal pipeline of precision genetic medicines focused on autoimmune disease and oncology, led by BRZ-101, a tolerance-inducing candidate for Type 1 diabetes. GenEdit rebranded to BreezeBio in February 2026 alongside a $60M Series B, and has established platform partnerships with Roche's Genentech and Sarepta Therapeutics. This is a therapeutics company with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; the profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Cambrian Bio
providers.description: Cambrian Bio (Cambrian BioPharma, Inc.) is a New York-headquartered clinical-stage drug development company working on the biology of aging. It runs a distributed "PipeCo" model — sourcing promising academic and early-stage science, then capitalizing and staffing each program as a separate subsidiary company under a shared development engine — to advance therapeutics that target the metabolic pathways that decline with age, first as treatments for chronic metabolic disease and ultimately as preventive medicines that extend healthspan. Its lead program, ATX-304, is an AMPK network activator with reported positive human translational data. Cambrian Bio is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes a corporate website, a science and pipeline overview, news and publications, and a blog, but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Carolina BioOncology Institute
providers.description: Carolina BioOncology Institute (CBOI) is a physician-owned Phase I oncology clinical research clinic and translational laboratory in Huntersville, North Carolina, founded by Dr. John Powderly II. It runs first-in-human and early-phase immunotherapy trials for patients with advanced solid tumors, having opened more than 100 oncology trials over fifteen years, and operates the Human Applications Lab — a cGMP-capable cell-processing and biorepository facility developing autologous cellular therapies — alongside research-use-only analytical and clinical lab analysis services for trial sponsors. CBOI is the parent company of BioCytics and an openEHR Industry Partner. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract; the only machine-readable surface on its domain is the stock WordPress REST API its CMS emits, which is not a product API and is deliberately not registered here.

providers.name: Centivax
providers.description: Centivax is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco, California, developing broad-spectrum vaccines to prevent infectious diseases at scale. Its lead program is a universal, broadly protective influenza vaccine in Phase 1 clinical development designed to protect against all strains of the virus. The company's pandemic-prevention work received a Gates Foundation Grand Challenge award and was featured in Netflix's "Pandemic: How to Prevent an Outbreak." Centivax's mission is to accelerate the world's transition to a post-pathogen humanity. This is a life-sciences company profile in the API Evangelist network; Centivax does not currently publish a public developer or API platform.

providers.name: Contraline
providers.description: Contraline is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing non-hormonal, long-acting, reversible contraceptive options for men and couples. Its lead product, ADAM, is an investigational implant designed to provide long-lasting reversible contraception, and NES/T is a daily topical gel intended to pause sperm production. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), Contraline runs clinical trials and participant programs from its Charlottesville, Virginia base. Its products are investigational and have not been approved by the FDA. The company operates a marketing and clinical-trial website with no public developer program or API; this API Evangelist profile captures its web presence, privacy posture, and domain security for the network catalog.

providers.name: Eikon
providers.description: Eikon Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company that integrates Nobel Prize-winning super-resolution single-molecule tracking (SMT) microscopy, advanced engineering, automation, and high-performance computing to visualize and measure the real-time movement of individual proteins in living cells. This proprietary live-cell imaging platform screens protein-ligand interactions across millions of cells per day, generating large, high-dimensional datasets that power the discovery and development of novel small-molecule medicines. Eikon advances a clinical- and preclinical-stage oncology and immunology pipeline, including EIK1001 (a TLR7/8 agonist) and IMP1734 (a selective PARP1 inhibitor). Backed by General Catalyst, the company is headquartered in Millbrae, California with offices in New York and Jersey City.

providers.name: Granata Bio
providers.description: Granata Bio is a reproductive-health biopharmaceutical company founded in 2018 and headquartered in the United States, focused on expanding access to fertility and IVF therapeutics across North America. The company identifies, licenses, and develops biopharmaceuticals spanning the in-vitro fertilization medication lifecycle from ovarian stimulation through luteal phase support, and is advancing a clinical pipeline that includes the Phase III GRACE Study. Granata Bio has raised over $30M, including a $14M Series A led by GV (Google Ventures) and a subsequent $15M Series A+. It operates a corporate and clinical web presence only and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or machine-readable interface; this profile captures its identity and web properties within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Grey Wolf Therapeutics
providers.description: Grey Wolf Therapeutics (Greywolf Therapeutics) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a new therapeutic class of immunotherapies through antigen modulation, aimed at treating people living with cancers and autoimmune disorders. Its approach modulates antigen presentation on cell surfaces so T cells can correctly recognize and target diseased cells, and it is pioneering modulation of Signal 1 in the T cell activation cascade. Lead assets include GRWD5769, a first-in-class oral ERAP1 inhibitor for oncology in Phase 1/2 trials, and GRWD0715, an autoimmunity-focused asset also in Phase 1/2. Backed by Canaan Partners, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company profile. It is a corporate/scientific organization and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Halia Therapeutics
providers.description: Halia Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Lehi, Utah, founded in 2017 and led by CEO Dr. David Bearss. Halia discovers and develops small-molecule therapies that target the immune system's inflammatory response — chiefly allosteric NEK7/NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition and LRRK2 inhibition — to resolve the chronic inflammation that drives hematologic, metabolic and neurodegenerative disease. Its lead clinical program, ofirnoflast (HT-6184), holds FDA Fast Track and Orphan Drug designation for lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes; HT-4253, an LRRK2 inhibitor aimed at neuroinflammation and Alzheimer's prevention in APOE4 carriers, has completed a first-in-human Phase 1 study. The company also markets a "genetic resilience" research platform (GENMOR) built on family-cohort genomics. Halia is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes a Webflow corporate site with pipeline, platform and press pages, and no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: HALO Precision Diagnostics
providers.description: HALO Precision Diagnostics (HALO Dx) is a Menlo Park, California precision-diagnostics company that acquires community imaging centers and rebuilds them as what it calls Imaging Center 2.0 — next-generation diagnostic hubs where advanced imaging, genomics and biomarker testing are all performed under one roof. Its diagnostic ensemble combines whole-body and multiparametric MRI, PSMA-targeted PET (PYLARIFY), digital pathology, polygenic risk scoring, hereditary and proteomic testing, and AI-assisted interpretation, applied first to cancer — the prostate program adds MRI-guided targeted biopsy and MRI-guided TULSA-PRO focal ablation — and expanding into cardiovascular disease and dementia. The company is led by CEO Michael Uhl with co-founder Brian Axe as Chief Product Officer and Dr. John Feller as Chief Medical Officer. Clinical delivery happens in HALO's own centers; referring physicians reach orders, results and images through a vendor-operated provider portal (RoyalMD) and the eUnity enterprise image viewer, and HALO advertises EMR integration for pushing orders and pulling results as a service its vendors deliver rather than as an interface it publishes. HALO operates no public developer program, publishes no API documentation, ships no SDK, and serves no machine-readable API contract; the only JSON on halodx.com is the marketing site's stock WordPress core REST API.

providers.name: Infinimmune
providers.description: Infinimmune is a biotechnology company that discovers and engineers human-derived antibody therapeutics. Its Complete Human Sequencing and Anthrobody library-on-B-cell platform surface rare antibodies that evolution has already proven in people, and its GLIMPSE antibody language model characterizes and optimizes candidates in silico for clinical development. Its lead program, IFX-101, is an IL-22 inhibitor for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, with additional pipeline programs targeting IL-13, APRIL, and IL-17F. Backed by Playground Global. Infinimmune publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; this API Evangelist profile captures the company identity and its public web, security, and legal surface.

providers.name: Kanvas Biosciences
providers.description: Kanvas Biosciences is a spatial biology company building a microbiome drug screening, discovery, and manufacturing platform to accelerate development of next-generation live biotherapeutics. Its proprietary High-Phylogenetic-Resolution Spatial Mapping (HiPR-Map) platform uses oligonucleotide probes targeting ribosomal and messenger RNA to visualize microbial identity and cellular function within tissue across all kingdoms of life, illuminating host-microbiome interactions. The company advances a microbiome-based immuno-oncology pipeline (lead candidate KAN-001) and operates GMP manufacturing. Backed by DCVC. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile; the enrichment pass found no public developer API, SDK, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Levicept
providers.description: Levicept Ltd is a UK-based clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at Innovation House, Discovery Park in Sandwich, Kent, developing LEVI-04, a fully human chimeric fusion protein combining the Fc fragment of human immunoglobulin G1 with the p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR) for the treatment of chronic pain. LEVI-04 is a first-in-class neurotrophin-3 (NT-3) inhibitor designed to restore neurotrophin homeostasis and deliver analgesia without the use-limiting side effects — notably rapidly progressive osteoarthritis — seen with anti-NGF antibodies. The company completed a 510+ participant Phase II study in osteoarthritis of the knee (NCT05618782) that met all primary and secondary endpoints, published the results in The Lancet in March 2026, and had its IND accepted by the US FDA in January 2026. Levicept is backed by Medicxi, Pfizer Ventures, Gilde Healthcare, Advent Life Sciences and Innovate UK. Levicept is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it operates a WordPress corporate website and publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Loyal
providers.description: Loyal (Cellular Longevity, Inc.) is a clinical-stage veterinary biotechnology company developing drugs intended to extend the healthy lifespan of dogs. Its lead programs — including LOY-002 for metabolic dysfunction in senior dogs and LOY-001/LOY-003 for large- and giant-breed dogs — are advancing through the FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine approval process, with more than 1,300 dogs enrolled across clinical studies. Loyal also runs a veterinary Learning Hub for practitioner education. The company is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and First Round Capital. As of this enrichment pass Loyal publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its public web identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Matwings Technology
providers.description: Matwings Technology (天鹜科技) is a global, AI-driven full-stack protein research and development platform. Centered on its self-developed MatwingsVenus general large model for protein design, the company integrates an in-house AI biological design agent (MatwingsVenus Agent), a ten-billion-scale protein sequence dataset (MatwingsVenus Pod), and an automated experimental platform (MatwingsVenus Auto) to deliver an end-to-end paradigm that spans AI design through AI validation. Capabilities include AI-directed evolution, AI enzyme mining, and de novo protein design, applied across affinity fillers and consumables, holistic health, and innovative drug discovery. Matwings is a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company headquartered in Shanghai, with peer-reviewed work at ICLR, NeurIPS, and PNAS. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK is currently published.

providers.name: Mestag Therapeutics
providers.description: Mestag Therapeutics is a clinical-stage immunotherapy company based in Cambridge, UK, developing new treatments for cancer and inflammatory diseases by targeting the understudied role of activated fibroblasts in immune responses. Its lead cancer program, MST-0312, is a targeted LTBR-agonist bispecific antibody designed to drive tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) formation in solid tumors and is now in the Phase I STARLYS trial. Its inflammatory-disease program, M402, uses agonist antibodies against stromal inhibitory receptors for conditions including rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, and lupus. Backed by GV, Mestag is a privately held biotech and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Moonwalk Biosciences
providers.description: Moonwalk Biosciences is a biotechnology company pioneering therapeutics in adipose (fat) biology, driven by deep genetic and epigenetic insights. Co-founded by Alex Aravanis (CEO), Arash Jamshidi (President & CTO), Justin Valley (Chief Platform Officer), and CRISPR pioneer Feng Zhang, the company develops epigenetic and siRNA-based programs — including obesity therapies — and is backed by Khosla Ventures, ARCH Venture Partners, Google Ventures, Future Ventures, Alpha Wave Global, and YK Bioventures. Moonwalk does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or API documentation; this profile captures its corporate identity and web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Mosa Meat
providers.description: Mosa Meat is a European food technology company headquartered in Maastricht, the Netherlands, founded in 2016 as a spin-off of Maastricht University by Mark Post and Peter Verstrate. The company develops cultivated (cell-cultured) beef using cellular agriculture: a small cell sample taken from a cow is nurtured through natural processes into muscle and fat tissue, which the company states can yield up to 80,000 burgers from a single sample. Mosa Meat produced the world's first cultured beef hamburger in 2013 and now operates the Mosa C.A.M.P.U.S. (Center for Advanced Meat Production, Upscaling, and Sustainability) in Maastricht, reported as the largest cultivated meat campus in the world. It is a B Corp certified organization pursuing regulatory approval and market entry for cultivated beef burgers. Mosa Meat is a laboratory and food production business; it publishes no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Nchroma Bio
providers.description: nChroma Bio is a genetic medicines company developing durable in vivo therapies by pairing best-in-class genetic cargoes, including epigenetic editing approaches, with targeted delivery technologies for diseases of significant unmet need. Headquartered at 201 Brookline Avenue in Boston, Massachusetts, the company is backed by DCVC and GV. This is a corporate research and therapeutics organization; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Octant Bio
providers.description: Octant (Octant Bio) is a precision-medicine and therapeutics company based in Emeryville, California, founded by Sri Kosuri and Ramsey Homsany. Octant engineers small-molecule drugs that modulate cellular mechanisms behind serious disease, with a focus on protein misfolding and mistrafficking disorders. Its Navigator platform merges synthetic biology, massively parallel experimentation in human cells, high-throughput chemistry, and AI/ML to understand and modulate how target proteins actually behave inside cells. Programs span rare genetic diseases (including autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa and Fabry disease), oncology, metabolism, and immunology. Octant is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Catalio Capital Management. As of this profile Octant publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this record captures the company's public web identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PhaseV
providers.description: PhaseV is a biopharma software company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts that builds AI and machine-learning solutions for clinical-trial optimization. Its platform helps pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs improve trial design, reduce enrollment and cost, shorten timelines, and increase probability of success through simulation and Bayesian adaptive design (Trial Optimizer), biomarker and patient-subgroup identification (Response Optimizer), disease-progression causal analysis (Portfolio Optimizer), site selection and operational analytics (ClinOps Optimizer), and ML-based early-derived endpoint identification. PhaseV publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture. Backed by Accel and Insight Partners.

providers.name: Preveta
providers.description: Preveta is a healthcare software company that builds an AI-driven care navigation platform and "command center" for specialty clinics. Built on clinical pathways, its software transforms EMR data into actionable insights, giving oncology, urology and gastroenterology practices an entirely new way to view, navigate and manage their patient populations across the cancer care continuum. Preveta is backed by Bullpen Capital and Techstars. As of this profile the company markets a closed clinical SaaS product and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Quris
providers.description: Quris-AI is a Bio-AI company building what it describes as pharma's first AI safety-prediction platform, aiming to predict which drug candidates will be safe in humans before they reach clinical trials. Its approach couples machine learning with "Patients-on-a-Chip" technology — miniaturized, organ-representative human tissue models that generate automatically-tagged biological data used to train classification algorithms for drug-safety prediction. The company targets the roughly 89% of drugs that fail in clinical trials, seeking to de-risk and accelerate pharmaceutical development. Based in Boston and Tel Aviv, Quris was co-founded with pioneers including Moderna co-founder Robert Langer and Nobel Laureate Aaron Ciechanover. Quris is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund and is profiled in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Rakuten Medical
providers.description: Rakuten Medical, Inc. is a global biotechnology company headquartered in San Diego, California, developing precision, cell-targeting investigational cancer therapies on its proprietary Alluminox platform — a drug-device combination pairing an IRDye 700DX light-activated dye conjugated to a cell-targeting antibody with local illumination by 690nm red light. Founded in 2010 as Aspyrian Therapeutics and renamed following investment from Rakuten Group, the company operates in the United States, Japan, Taiwan, Switzerland and India. Its lead asset ASP-1929, an EGFR-targeting antibody-dye conjugate, received marketing approval in Japan in 2021 as Akalux for unresectable locally advanced or recurrent head and neck cancer and is in global Phase 3 development alone and in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy; RM-1995 and RM-0256 follow in earlier-stage programs. As a clinical-stage therapeutics and drug-device company, Rakuten Medical publishes no public developer API, SDK, webhook, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures its corporate identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Reify Health
providers.description: Reify Health is a clinical research technology company whose mission is to remove clinical trial operations as the bottleneck to delivering new therapies to patients. It is the parent organization behind OneStudyTeam, whose StudyTeam platform is a cloud-based patient enrollment and recruitment management system connecting research sites, sponsors, patients, and vendors on a unified workspace, and Care Access, a business unit expanding trial access to underserved communities. StudyTeam is used by roughly 70% of the sponsors running the most clinical trials (including Amgen, AstraZeneca, and Eli Lilly), across 10,000+ research sites in 100+ countries. Reify Health is backed by Altimeter Capital, Battery Ventures, ICONIQ Capital, and Sierra Ventures. No public developer API, developer portal, or API specification was found during enrichment; this profile captures company identity, links, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: sanegenebio
providers.description: SanegeneBio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing RNAi (RNA interference) genetic medicines for metabolic, cardiovascular, and complement-mediated autoimmune diseases, including obesity. Its proprietary LEAD (Ligand and Enhancer Assisted Delivery) platform enables receptor-mediated, targeted delivery of siRNA therapeutics to adipocytes, skeletal myocytes, and other tissues beyond the liver. The company operates as a fully integrated global biotech and has raised over $150 million to advance its pipeline. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a corporate website (about, technology, pipeline, news, contact) but no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Scribe Therapeutics
providers.description: Scribe Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Alameda, California, engineering CRISPR-based genetic medicines through its proprietary "CRISPR by Design" platform. Co-founded by molecular engineers Benjamin Oakes, Brett Staahl, and David Savage alongside CRISPR co-inventor Jennifer Doudna, the company builds highly engineered CasX-derived enzymes — including its X-Editing (XE) molecules for precise gene editing and ELXR epigenetic long-term X-repressor technology for durable gene silencing without altering the underlying DNA sequence. Scribe focuses initially on cardiometabolic disease, the leading cause of death globally, and expands into areas such as sickle cell disease and neurological conditions through strategic pharmaceutical partnerships.
