The company pairs an AI platform with wet-lab biology to mine more than a million natural proteins, identify candidates predicted to hit clinically validated human immune-disease targets, and transform them into therapeutic candidates. Ditto is an early-stage, three-person team led by founders Dennis Sun (CEO), Adair Borges (CSO), and Emily Weiss (CTO). This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Ditto Bio currently publishes a marketing and science website only and exposes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable developer surface.

providers.name: Inceptive
providers.description: Inceptive is an AI biotechnology company founded in 2021 by transformer co-author Jakob Uszkoreit and Stanford biochemist Rhiju Das, building foundation models of life to rationally design sequence-based medicines such as mRNA, siRNA, ASOs, and peptides. The company pairs large-scale deep learning with high-throughput in-house wet-lab experiments in a tight design-build-test loop, then licenses successful molecules to pharmaceutical partners. Inceptive is headquartered in Palo Alto with offices in Berlin and Zurich, is backed by a16z Bio + Health, Obvious Ventures, NVentures (NVIDIA), and S32, and has announced strategic collaborations including a multi-year agreement with Alnylam Pharmaceuticals. Inceptive is a research-partner biotech and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Joes Future Food (Zhouzi Future)
providers.description: Joes Future Food (周子未来 / Nanjing Zhouzi Future Food Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Nanjing-based cellular agriculture and food-technology company pioneering cultivated (cell-cultured) meat in China. The founding team produced what it describes as China's first piece of cultivated meat, and the company develops cell-cultured pork products (pork belly, fatback, skin, meatballs, and a mixed family pack) alongside serum-free culture media and a catalog of primary and gene-edited animal cell lines (porcine adipose and muscle stem cells, bovine muscle and adipose cells, chicken embryo fibroblasts, and more) used across cultivated-meat research and biomanufacturing. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners. The company runs a corporate marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Synonym
providers.description: Synonym (rebranding to Roebling) is a biomanufacturing infrastructure and finance company founded in 2022 by Edward Shenderovich and Joshua Lachter and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It develops, finances, and builds commercial-scale bio-manufacturing facilities to give synthetic biology producers flexible fermentation capacity, and it operates bioproduction tools including a techno-economic modeling suite (TEA/FEL-1/FEL-2 engines) and the Capacitor-powered Match platform that connects clients with production capacity. As of this profile Synonym publishes only a marketing website and private product surfaces; it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, documentation portal, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Cyrus Biotechnology
providers.description: Cyrus Biotechnology is a Seattle-based protein-design and drug-discovery company building novel biologics for serious unmet medical needs by re-engineering existing proteins with a tight loop between computational modeling and lab testing. Its flagship product, Cyrus Bench, is a cloud-based protein modeling and structure-prediction platform that packages the Rosetta software suite (alongside deep-learning tools such as AlphaFold, OpenFold, RoseTTAFold and ProteinMPNN) behind a browser-based interface for homology modeling, protein/protein and enzyme/ligand interface design, protein stabilization, protein/ligand and protein/protein docking, and X-ray molecular replacement. Cyrus Bench is delivered as a hosted web application with user documentation rather than a public developer REST API; the company is backed by Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: Prokarium
providers.description: Prokarium is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in London, UK, developing bacterial immunotherapies for solid tumors. Its foundational technology uses a proprietary attenuated strain of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi (ZH9) as a microbial immunotherapy platform that is naturally tumor-targeting and oncolytic, designed to overcome the suppressive tumor microenvironment and generate anti-tumor immune responses while enabling diverse cargo delivery. The lead program, ZH9 for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer, is in the Phase 1/1b PARADIGM-1 trial, with a muscle-invasive bladder cancer combination arm alongside checkpoint inhibitors, an oral immune fitness agent (IO Prime), and a discovery-stage Living Cures cargo-delivery platform. Prokarium is a therapeutics developer, not a software or data company, and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable interface of any kind.

providers.name: Abpro
providers.description: Abpro Holdings, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in the Boston area (Woburn / Burlington, Massachusetts) that develops next-generation multispecific antibody therapeutics for oncology and ophthalmology. Its DiversImmune antibody-discovery platform and MultiMab multispecific-engineering platform are used to build bispecific and tetravalent T-cell-engager constructs, led by ABP-102/CT-P72, a tetravalent bispecific HER2 x CD3 T-cell engager partnered with Celltrion, alongside the ABP-110, ABP-150 and ABP-201 programs. Abpro is a drug developer rather than a software company: its public web surface is a corporate and investor-relations site, and it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Adcendo
providers.description: Adcendo ApS is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with US operations in Boston, Massachusetts, developing a new generation of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for cancers with high unmet medical need. Founded in 2017 out of research by Lars Henning Engelholm and Niels Behrendt, the company advances a clinical and pre-clinical pipeline that includes ADCE-T02 (targeting Tissue Factor, in the Phase 1b Tiffany-01 study across advanced solid tumors), ADCE-D01 (targeting uPARAP, granted FDA Fast Track designation for soft tissue sarcoma), and the pre-clinical ADCE-B05. Adcendo is a privately held, venture-backed therapeutics developer; it publishes a corporate website, pipeline and publications pages, and investor press releases, but it operates no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: AI Medical Service
providers.description: AI Medical Service Inc. (AIM) is a Tokyo-based med-tech company founded in September 2017 with the mission to save lives worldwide by eliminating gastrointestinal cancers through earlier detection. AIM develops endoscopic AI (artificial intelligence) that assists physicians in real-time diagnostic imaging of the digestive tract, drawing on joint research with more than 100 medical institutions. Its flagship gastroAI family of endoscopic image diagnosis support software has secured regulatory approval in Japan, Singapore, and Thailand, and an earlier FDA approval in the United States. The company distributes its AI on-premise today and is building an in-house cloud platform to broaden access; it currently publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a health-tech lead backed by SoftBank Vision Fund.

providers.name: Alumis
providers.description: Alumis Inc. (NASDAQ: ALMS) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered at 280 East Grand Avenue, South San Francisco, California, developing oral therapies for immune-mediated diseases. Incorporated in 2021 as Esker Therapeutics and renamed Alumis in January 2022, its pipeline is led by envudeucitinib, an oral allosteric TYK2 inhibitor in Phase 3 for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and systemic lupus erythematosus; A-005, a CNS-penetrant TYK2 inhibitor for neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative disease; and lonigutamab, a subcutaneously delivered anti-IGF-1R antibody for thyroid eye disease. Alumis describes a proprietary precision data-analytics platform that integrates genetic, genomic, proteomic, biological and clinical insight, but it is an internal therapeutic-development capability and is not exposed publicly. The company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Ancora Heart
providers.description: Ancora Heart, Inc. is a privately held medical device company headquartered at 4001 Burton Drive, Santa Clara, California, developing transcatheter therapies for people living with heart failure. Its lead product is the AccuCinch Ventricular Restoration System, a completely transcatheter implant designed to reduce the size of an enlarged left ventricle and restore cardiac structure and function in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) who remain symptomatic on guideline-directed medical therapy. The device is investigational and is being evaluated in the CORCINCH-HF study (NCT04331769), a prospective randomized international trial enrolling up to 400 patients across as many as 80 centers, alongside the CORCINCH-EU program in Europe. Ancora Heart is a medical device manufacturer rather than a software company: it publishes a marketing and clinical-information website for patients and physicians, and operates no public developer program, API, or SDK.

providers.name: Apreohealth
providers.description: Apreo Health is a clinical-stage medical device company based in Menlo Park, California, developing a novel, tissue-sparing bronchoscopic treatment for severe emphysema. Its investigational Apreo BREATHE Airway Scaffold uses a self-expanding nitinol scaffold to tent open targeted airways, releasing trapped air and reducing lung hyperinflation without removing healthy tissue. The device received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation in 2024 and is being evaluated in the BREATHE clinical trial program. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, F-Prime Capital, and OSF Ventures, Apreo Health is a physical medical device company with no public developer API, SDK, or software platform; this profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bota Biosciences
providers.description: Bota Biosciences (Bota Bio, 恩和科技) is an industrial and synthetic biology company that applies AI-driven computation and laboratory automation to bio-manufacturing. Its in-house Bota Biofoundry and Cell2Cloud platforms combine computational algorithms, non-model industrial strain engineering, rapid iterative enzyme engineering and performance protein design to shorten design-build-test-learn cycles, and in March 2026 it launched SAION AI, a three-layer "Physical AI" platform (cognition, orchestration, execution) that drives laboratory hardware through a proprietary Biological Protocol Language. Bota commercializes this work as physical ingredients rather than software: Purtect bio-preservatives (nisin, natamycin, ε-poly-lysine, lysozyme), Prorylia biomimetic proteins and Re² Coffea Arabica peptides, sold through its HeliaGenesis food and nutrition brand and its YuccaElements personal care brand, with partnerships including BASF, Proya, Syensqo and Puratos. Founded in 2019 with operations in Hangzhou, China and the San Francisco Bay Area, Bota publishes no developer portal, no public API documentation, no SDKs and no machine-readable specification; its computational software is internal laboratory tooling and its SAION AI application is reachable only through a login with an administrator-managed account whitelist.

providers.name: Braveheart Bio
providers.description: Braveheart Bio is a late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and related cardiac conditions. Its lead candidate, BHB-1893, is a selective cardiac myosin inhibitor (licensed as HRS-1893 from Hengrui Pharma) designed to reduce excessive heart-muscle contraction and improve cardiac performance in patients with obstructive and non-obstructive HCM. The San Francisco-based company launched in November 2025 with a $185M Series A led by a16z alongside Forbion, OrbiMed, Enavate Sciences, and Frazier Life Sciences, and filed for a Nasdaq IPO in July 2026. Braveheart Bio is a corporate/scientific organization and does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or SDKs.

providers.name: Cartography Biosciences
providers.description: Cartography Biosciences is a South San Francisco biotechnology company developing precision cancer immunotherapies designed around tumor-selective antigens. Using single-cell genomics, proteomics, and novel binder-discovery methods, the company profiles antigen expression across thousands of patient samples and millions of cells to build a comprehensive antigen atlas, classifying cancers by antigen expression rather than histology or genetic mutation. Its goal is to direct immunotherapies toward the safest and most effective targets. Backed by a16z, Cartography was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a corporate and careers website but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Cellinobio
providers.description: Cellino Bio develops AI-driven optical bioprocessing technology for personalized regenerative medicine. Its proprietary Nebula platform combines deep learning, laser-based cell management, and closed-loop optical bioprocesses to manufacture patient-specific, induced-pluripotent-stem-cell-derived cell and tissue replacements at scale. The company targets degenerative and chronic conditions including kidney disease, lung disease, spinal cord injury, Alzheimer's, and diabetes. Cellino is a life-sciences/biotech company with no public developer API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company intelligence and is backed by Felicis and Khosla Ventures.

providers.name: Color Health
providers.description: Color Health (founded as Color Genomics in 2015) is a population health technology company that operates a nationwide, oncologist-led Virtual Cancer Clinic and delivers population-scale precision health programs - hereditary cancer and cardiovascular genetic testing, pharmacogenomics, cancer early detection and screening, and clinical care management - for employers, unions, health plans, governments, and public health institutions. Color does NOT publish a public, self-service developer API. Access to its platform is enterprise/partner-gated and contracted directly with organizations; data exchange with health systems and EHRs is handled through interoperability partners (e.g. Redox) using FHIR/HL7 rather than an open developer portal. The APIs listed here are logical, honestly-modeled surfaces (endpointsModeled) that describe how such a program is typically integrated - they are not confirmed public endpoints.

providers.name: Complete Omics
providers.description: Complete Omics is a Baltimore, Maryland based, CLIA- and CAP-accredited molecular diagnostics company building ultra-deep, clinically reproducible proteomics and multi-omics testing. Its Complete360 liquid- and tissue-biopsy platform and Valid-NEO companion-diagnostics platform apply AI-assisted analysis of high-dimensional biological data across oncology, neurology, cardiovascular, and immunology testing. The company holds 40+ global patents and 20+ top-tier journal publications. Complete Omics is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface exists at this time; this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Eikon Therapeutics
providers.description: Eikon Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company (Nasdaq: EIKN) founded in 2019 and headquartered in Millbrae, California, with additional offices in New York and Jersey City. Eikon built a proprietary drug-discovery platform around single-molecule live-cell imaging, applying super-resolution fluorescence microscopy and high-throughput single-molecule tracking to observe how proteins and drug targets move and interact inside living cells in real time. The technology descends from co-founder Eric Betzig's Nobel Prize-winning work in super-resolution microscopy, and the company is led by former Merck R&D chief Roger Perlmutter. Eikon uses these measurements to discover and develop novel therapeutics across oncology and other disease areas. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Eikon publishes a corporate and investor web presence but no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: ILiAD Biotechnologies
providers.description: ILiAD Biotechnologies, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Weston, Florida, developing BPZE1 — a live attenuated intranasal vaccine candidate designed to prevent Bordetella pertussis (whooping cough) colonization and transmission — alongside its B-Tech vector platform, which the company is exploring for infectious, allergic, autoimmune and neurodegenerative disease. The BPZE1 technology originated at Institut Pasteur de Lille and is exclusively licensed to ILiAD, which announced a $115M Series B in February 2026 and received a UK MHRA Innovation Passport designation in December 2024. ILiAD publishes a static corporate and scientific website only: as of 2026-08-22 it operates no public API, developer portal, SDK, machine-readable specification, or any other programmable surface.

providers.name: Luminate
providers.description: Luminate Medical is a healthcare company delivering cancer care at home. Its Lotus Home Infusion platform enables nurse-led, at-home chemotherapy infusion, partnering with oncology clinics, health plans, and patients while keeping drug dispensing oversight with the originating cancer center. Luminate is a portfolio company of 8vc and GV. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer, API, documentation, or integration surface.

providers.name: Mana.bio
providers.description: Mana.bio is an AI-driven drug-delivery biotechnology company specializing in programmable lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) for nucleic-acid therapeutics and vaccines, including mRNA, DNA, and CRISPR-based gene therapy. The company runs a closed-loop design-build-test-learn platform that uses machine-learning models to design novel LNP candidates, synthesizes dozens of formulations weekly via high-throughput automation, screens them with comprehensive assays, and feeds results back to continuously improve its models — targeting precise, optimized extrahepatic delivery. Mana.bio also operates Mina (ChatLNP), an AI agent that helps scientists explore curated literature, predict LNP properties, and optimize formulations, plus an LNP patents / freedom-to-operate map. The company is backed by a16z. Mana.bio publishes no first-party developer or product API; its only public agent surface is a Wix Site MCP endpoint and an llms.txt on its site.

providers.name: Model Medicines
providers.description: Model Medicines is an AI-first biotechnology company based in San Diego, California, discovering and developing first-in-class small-molecule drugs by targeting fundamental disease mechanisms it calls biological choke points. Its end-to-end GALILEO AI engine spans drug design, target discovery, and preclinical development, supported by specialized models including AmesNet for regulatory-grade toxicology prediction and ChemPrint for chemical property prediction. Lead programs target RdRp Thumb-1 (a conserved allosteric pocket on viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) and BRD4, with lead assets MDL-001, a broad-spectrum oral antiviral candidate, and MDL-4102. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Model Medicines publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface; its AI platform is used internally for drug discovery.

providers.name: Nirmidas Biotech
providers.description: Nirmidas Biotech, Inc. is a Mountain View, California life-science company founded in September 2013 that develops and manufactures diagnostics and imaging products built on near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence enhancement. Its patented plasmonic gold (pGOLD) assay platform boosts biological detection signals on gold-coated microarray slides and 96-well microplates, and is paired with the MidaScan and MidaScan-IR confocal scanners, MidaSpot rapid antibody test kits, and the DeepVision, KingsVision, SockEye and AlbertSurgical in vivo NIR-I / NIR-II / SWIR imaging systems, plus a catalog of NIR-II dyes and probes. The company is a member of Janssen Labs (JLABS), QB3, Stanford StartX Med and the MIT Industrial Liaison Program, manufactures under ISO 13485:2016, and received FDA Emergency Use Authorization for its MidaSpot COVID-19 antibody fingerstick test. Products are sold as physical instruments, kits and reagents through an inquiry-based storefront; Nirmidas publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Rani Therapeutics
providers.description: Rani Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing the RaniPill, an ingestible robotic capsule engineered to deliver biologic drugs orally in place of subcutaneous or intravenous injections. The platform aims to preserve injection-comparable bioavailability while removing the pain and adherence barriers of needle-based therapies across chronic and metabolic disease areas. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network; the company is a publicly traded life-sciences firm and does not currently publish a developer API, developer portal, or programmatic data surface.

providers.name: Rejoni
providers.description: Rejoni, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage women's health medical device company founded in June 2020 by serial entrepreneur Amar Sawhney, PhD and Pramand LLC, and headquartered at 201 Burlington Road in Bedford, Massachusetts. It develops proprietary hydrogel-based biomaterial therapies for gynecological surgery, with a stated mission of protecting, preserving and healing the uterus. Its lead product, the Juveena Hydrogel System, is designed to prevent the formation and reformation of intrauterine adhesions (IUAs) — the scar tissue that forms after transcervical procedures such as dilation and curettage, myomectomy or treatment of heavy bleeding, and a leading cause of infertility and abnormal uterine bleeding. The system pairs a low-profile proprietary transcervical catheter with two liquid precursors that cross-link on delivery into a soft, temporary hydrogel implant that mechanically separates the uterine walls during healing and then resorbs on its own in roughly two to three weeks, about one menstrual cycle, so no removal procedure is required. Juveena is investigational only and pending FDA approval; the FDA filed Rejoni's premarket approval (PMA) application in January 2026, and the company completed patient enrollment in its US IDE pivotal study. Rejoni closed a $25 million financing in June 2026 with ClavystBio, Amed Ventures, Ascension Ventures, Catalyst Health Ventures, Delos Capital, FemHealth Ventures, Iyengar Capital and Sparta Group, and appointed women's health MedTech leader John Nealon as chief executive officer in May 2026. Rejoni runs no developer program and publishes no public API: its entire web presence is a small Webflow marketing site, and probes for OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, MCP, llms.txt and every /.well-known/ discovery path returned HTTP 404 against a verified real-404 origin, while api./developer./docs./app./portal.rejoni.com resolve only to a wildcard A record with no listener answering on either port 80 or 443.

providers.name: Revolution Medicines
providers.description: Revolution Medicines is a clinical-stage precision oncology company headquartered in Redwood City, California, developing targeted therapies for RAS-addicted cancers. Its pipeline centers on RAS(ON) inhibitors — including daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), zoldonrasib (RMC-9805), and elironrasib (RMC-6291) — designed to directly target the active, GTP-bound (ON) state of oncogenic RAS proteins across mutations such as KRAS G12X. The company pairs structure-based drug discovery with clinical development to pursue treatments for pancreatic, lung, colorectal, and other RAS-driven tumors. Revolution Medicines is a publicly traded corporate entity (Nasdaq: RVMD) and does not currently expose a public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Topos Bio
providers.description: Topos Bio is an AI-native drug discovery company building all-atom foundation models for intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) — dynamic, flexible proteins implicated in diseases such as Alzheimer's and prostate cancer. Its Topos-1 foundation model generates physically realistic conformational ensembles for flexible proteins, aiming to make previously undruggable targets therapeutically viable. The company is backed by Threshold Ventures. No public API or developer platform is currently published.

providers.name: Vial
providers.description: Vial is a next-generation biotech company advancing first and best-in-class biologics to treat unmet need in Immunology and Inflammation. The company pairs AI-driven drug discovery with automated, technology-enabled clinical trials, working across target discovery (identifying high-value therapeutic targets), molecule design (generating and optimizing molecular candidates), and experimental validation (high-throughput approaches to accelerate development). Its lead pipeline program is an IL-13 x TSLP bi-specific antibody in Phase 1. Vial was originally built as a tech-enabled contract research organization (CRO) focused on reimagining clinical trials, and was backed by General Catalyst. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Vial publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Vitara
providers.description: Vitara (Vitara Biomedical) is a Philadelphia-based medical technology company developing EXTEND, an investigational neonatal support platform that surrounds extremely premature newborns in a fluid-filled, fetal-physiology-modeled environment for their first 28 days, delaying the stress of early air exposure so vital organs can continue to develop. The company aims to improve survival and reduce long-term complications for infants born as early as 22 weeks gestation. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Khosla Ventures portfolio company; Vitara publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation, and its technology has not received U.S. FDA market clearance.

providers.name: CatalYm
providers.description: CatalYm GmbH is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Planegg-Martinsried near Munich, Germany, developing next-generation cancer immunotherapies. Its lead approach neutralizes GDF-15 (Growth Differentiation Factor 15) to reverse a key immune-resistance mechanism in solid tumors, aiming to reinstate anti-tumor immune activity and overcome resistance to checkpoint-inhibitor and other cancer therapies. The company is a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. This is a biotech/pharmaceutical organization with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Clinflash
providers.description: Clinflash (易迪希医药科技 / Clinflash Healthcare Technology) is a Chinese clinical-research technology company founded in 2014 that provides a cloud-based clinical trial information platform for pharmaceutical sponsors, CROs, and research sites. Its self-developed suite spans more than ten systems, including Clinflash EDC (electronic data capture), IRT/IWRS (randomization and trial supply management), eCOA/ePRO (electronic clinical outcome and patient-reported outcomes), Safety/PV (pharmacovigilance and drug-safety alerting), CTMS (clinical trial management), eTMF (electronic trial master file), eCTD, eConsent, eSign, Coder (medical coding), and ePAY (subject payment). Clinflash has supported thousands of clinical trial projects for over a thousand pharmaceutical, generic, medical-device, and IVD organizations, including pivotal Phase III and international multi-center studies. The platform is delivered as a login-gated SaaS at cloud.clinflash.com and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer/API program, OpenAPI, SDKs, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Orchestra Bio
providers.description: Orchestra (orchestra.bio) is an agentic operations platform for drug development and life sciences R&D organizations, helping teams unify planning across leadership, programs, and scientific groups, automate R&D workflows, and reduce the operational risks that derail breakthrough science. The San Francisco company pairs unified program roadmaps with intelligent operations and decision support, and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), 8VC, Haystack, and other investors. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Orchestra publishes a product marketing site, a company blog, and a hosted web application, but no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Tierra Biosciences
providers.description: Tierra Biosciences is a San Leandro, California synthetic biology company using AI-guided, cell-free protein production to synthesize custom proteins on demand for pharmaceutical, industrial, and agricultural research. Its customer-facing Tierra Protein Platform is a web-based eCommerce ordering portal where researchers enter protein sequences and get custom proteins synthesized, validated, and shipped. The company (rebranding toward Revr Bio) is backed by prosus-ventures and Material Impact. No public developer API, SDK, or programmatic-access surface is currently published; this profile was enriched and confirmed as a web-platform-only provider.

providers.name: 10x Science
providers.description: 10x Science is an AI-native software company building the first AI-native protein characterization platform for the life sciences, starting with drug development. A Y Combinator W26 company founded out of Nobel laureate Carolyn Bertozzi's laboratory at Stanford University, it automates peptide mapping for protein therapeutics, delivering explainable molecular insights in minutes where legacy tools and manual workflows take months. The company raised a $4.8M seed round led by Initialized Capital and is headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; it does not yet publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Abogen
providers.description: Abogen Biosciences (Suzhou Abogen Biosciences Co., Ltd. / 苏州艾博生物科技有限公司) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in January 2019 and headquartered in Suzhou, China, dedicated to developing transformative medicines through messenger RNA (mRNA) innovation. The company has built full-scale in-house capabilities spanning the entire mRNA drug development cycle - protein engineering, mRNA sequence design and synthesis, proprietary lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery, formulation, and commercial-scale manufacturing. Its product pipeline covers infectious disease prevention and cancer immunotherapy, and it has advanced an EUA mRNA product along with additional clinical-stage candidates. Abogen is a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund. Abogen is a pharmaceutical / biotechnology company and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile captures its corporate identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Flowneuroscience
providers.description: Flow Neuroscience is a Malmo, Sweden medtech company founded in 2016 by clinical psychologist Daniel Mansson and neuroscientist Erik Rehn. It develops a medically approved, at-home transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) headset paired with a behavioral-therapy smartphone app to treat major depressive disorder without medication. Its Flow FL-100 device is CE-marked in the EU and UK and received FDA approval (PMA P230024) as the first at-home tDCS treatment for depression, with a US launch planned for September 2026. Flow is backed by Khosla Ventures and other global investors. This is a consumer and clinical medical-device company; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Kuehnle AgroSystems
providers.description: Kuehnle AgroSystems, Inc. (KAS) is a Honolulu, Hawaii microalgae biotechnology company founded in 2007 by Dr. Adelheid "Heidi" Kuehnle, with a second site in Cork, Ireland. KAS produces high-value natural products from microalgae for the food, feed and health markets using a patented heterotrophic "dark fermentation" process and proprietary non-GMO Hawaiian algal strains that run in standard fermentation equipment rather than open ponds or photobioreactors, compressing production from weeks to days with substantially lower cost, land, water and energy use. Its lead products are natural astaxanthin and algal protein, sold into nutraceuticals, cosmetics and skincare, functional foods and beverages, and aquaculture and animal feed; in August 2025 KAS entered a development and commercialization partnership with Corbion for an esterified natural astaxanthin. KAS sells ingredients, strains and fermentation process technology rather than software: it publishes no API, developer program, SDK, or machine-readable contract, and kuehnleagro.com is a six-page Squarespace marketing site.

providers.name: Resolyst
providers.description: Resolyst is a specialty-care platform that positions itself as the intelligence layer for AI-enabled specialty care, extending the reach of the world's leading clinicians with continuous, research-first expertise. Rather than episodic consultations, Resolyst provides ongoing multidisciplinary medical oversight for patients with chronic conditions through specialist nurses, pharmacists, dieticians, physiotherapists and psychologists, connecting patients with local and international experts, embedding clinical research into care pathways, and convening condition-specific international expert panels for second opinions and clinical pathway oversight. Backed by Seedcamp, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Arc Institute
providers.description: Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit biomedical research organization headquartered in Palo Alto, California, co-founded in 2021 by Silvana Konermann (Executive Director), Patrick Hsu (Core Investigator), and Stripe co-founder Patrick Collison. With 300+ staff ("Arconauts") across 9 core laboratories and 5 technology centers, Arc develops AI foundation models for biology that span DNA, RNA, proteins, and single cells. Its flagship releases include Evo (Science, 2024) and Evo 2 (Nature, 2026) — DNA foundation models trained on trillions of nucleotides at single-nucleotide resolution with up to a 1-megabase context; STATE and Stack single-cell foundation models for cellular perturbation and in-context learning; the Arc Virtual Cell Atlas; the SRAgent LLM agents for bioinformatics; and the BINSEQ binary sequencing format. Models are released under Apache 2.0 on GitHub and Hugging Face, with hosted inference for Evo 2 available through NVIDIA BioNeMo and the NVIDIA build.nvidia.com API. Arc is funded by philanthropic donations from Patrick and John Collison, Vitalik Buterin, the Ron Conway family, Dustin Moskovitz, Daniel Gross, Elad Gil, and other technology benefactors; it does not sell APIs, SaaS, or models commercially.

providers.name: CAMP4 Therapeutics
providers.description: CAMP4 Therapeutics is a clinical-stage RNA-medicines biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, pioneering a new class of antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapeutics designed to increase targeted gene expression. Built on the company's RAP Platform (Regulatory RNA Activating Platform), which combines epigenomics, computational biology, and machine learning to map the regulatory RNA and signaling circuits controlling gene expression, CAMP4 develops first-in-class medicines for diseases caused by insufficient protein expression, with an initial focus on central nervous system and metabolic disorders such as urea cycle disorders and SYNGAP1. Founded by CEO Josh Mandel-Brehm with scientific co-founders Rick Young (Whitehead Institute/MIT) and Len Zon (Boston Children's Hospital/Harvard), CAMP4 is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). This is a corporate/therapeutics company profile in the API Evangelist network; CAMP4 publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal, so no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: Gilgamesh Pharma
providers.description: Gilgamesh Pharma (Gilgamesh Pharmaceuticals, Inc.) is a New York based clinical-stage neuroscience company founded in 2019 that develops rapid-acting, next-generation therapeutics for psychiatric and substance use disorders. Its discovery and translational platform combines medicinal chemistry, neurocircuitry science, electrophysiology and machine learning to identify new chemical entities, and its pipeline spans short-acting 5-HT2A receptor agonists, NMDA receptor antagonists, non-hallucinogenic neuroplastogens, cardiac-safe ibogaine analogs and M1/M4 muscarinic programs. Lead assets include bretisilocin (GM-2505), acquired by AbbVie in August 2025, and blixeprodil (GM-1020), an orally bioavailable NMDAR antagonist in Phase 2 for major depressive disorder. Gilgamesh is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Helix
providers.description: Helix is a population genomics company operating an end-to-end precision health platform - a proprietary Exome+ next-generation sequencing assay, a CLIA/CAP-certified clinical lab, and bioinformatics tooling - that enables health systems, life sciences companies, and payers to integrate genomic data into clinical care and research at population scale. Through its DNA Product Studio, Helix exposes a partner-gated developer surface - a Genomics API (direct programmatic access to 100M+ base pairs including SNPs, indels, and copy number variants with panel-grade coverage of actionable genes), an Ancestry API (continental ancestry for 6 global populations or regional ancestry for 26+ populations), and an Insight API (user-specific results for hundreds of traits and conditions, from single-marker traits to machine-learning polygenic risk scores) - alongside Embedded Apps and an App Acceleration Framework for building white-label DNA products. API access is enterprise/partner-gated and provisioned through Helix partnerships; there is no public self-serve developer portal or openly published API specification, so the API surface below is modeled from Helix's public product documentation.

providers.name: Kytopen
providers.description: Kytopen Corp. is a Cambridge, Massachusetts life-sciences instrument company, spun out of MIT, that builds non-viral, continuous-flow cellular engineering hardware for cell and gene therapy discovery and manufacturing. Its Flowfect technology combines continuous fluid flow with electric fields to deliver mRNA, DNA and CRISPR payloads into cells, and is sold as two benchtop platforms: Flowfect Discover, an automated small-volume system that runs up to 96 high-throughput transfections in about ten minutes, and Flowfect TX, a closed-system instrument that processes 10-50 million cells per mL at 25-50 mL per minute for GMP-scale manufacturing. The company sells laboratory instruments and consumables to biopharma and CDMO customers through a quote and technology-access motion; it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Instrument data integration for Flowfect customers is delivered by a third party, Ganymede Bio, under its own platform and its own contract - that surface belongs to Ganymede, not to Kytopen.

providers.name: Medeor Therapeutics
providers.description: Medeor Therapeutics is a clinical-stage cellular immunotherapy company in San Mateo, California, developing MDR-101, a one-time cell therapy manufactured from a living kidney donor's blood that induces mixed chimerism so HLA-matched transplant recipients can withdraw from lifelong immunosuppression while preserving graft function. The platform originated in roughly two decades of research at Stanford University led by Dr. Samuel Strober. The company completed a Phase 3 registration trial that exceeded its target success rate, and has since suspended operations and is seeking an acquirer to complete the BLA filing. Medeor is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it publishes no developer portal, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Neuralink
providers.description: Neuralink is a neurotechnology company pioneering implantable brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) intended to restore autonomy to people with unmet medical needs and, longer term, to expand human capability. Its flagship device, the N1 Implant, is a surgically embedded array of thin, flexible threads placed by a purpose-built surgical robot to record and stimulate neural activity, paired with an app that lets users control external devices. Neuralink is a frontier-tech company backed by Craft Ventures, Founders Fund, GV and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its only public machine-readable surfaces are a security.txt vulnerability-disclosure record and standard web/DNS security posture. This profile was surfaced from VC portfolio data and enriched with real probed security artifacts.

providers.name: Ohalo Genetics
providers.description: Ohalo Genetics is an American agricultural biotechnology company founded in 2019 and led by CEO David Friedberg, developing plant-breeding platforms and proprietary crop varieties. Its flagship Boosted Breeding technology — marketed as "2x + 2x = 4x" — alters the reproductive circuitry of parent plants so each parent passes its entire genome to the next generation rather than a random half, producing polyploid offspring that carry the full genetic contribution of both parents and, in early field trials, substantially higher yields. Ohalo pairs this with an Agile Breeding service and a True Seed program that ships uniform, disease-free seedlings directly to growers, with active programs in potato, almond (the FruitionOne self-fertile Nonpareil variety), strawberry and corn, delivered through partnerships such as the Allied Potato partnership and a strawberry consortium. The company sells plant genetics and breeding services to agricultural partners; it is not a software vendor and publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Ratio Therapeutics
providers.description: Ratio Therapeutics Inc. is a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company headquartered at One Design Center Place in Boston, Massachusetts, developing next-generation precision radiopharmaceuticals for solid tumors. Founded in 2022 by Jack Hoppin, Ph.D. and John Babich, Ph.D., the company pairs two proprietary R&D platforms — Trillium, a tunable albumin-binding targeting scaffold that modulates pharmacokinetics, and Macropa, a bifunctional chelator built for the alpha emitter actinium-225 — to improve drug availability, tumor delivery and tumor loading. Its lead program, [Ac-225]RTX-2358, is a FAP-targeted radiotherapeutic in the ATLAS Phase 1/2 trial, alongside a next-generation GRPR program, mono- and bispecific radioligand therapies, and PET imaging assets. Ratio has licensing and collaboration agreements with Novartis, Merck, Bayer and Lantheus, isotope supply agreements with Nusano, TerraPower Isotopes and PanTera, and manufacturing partnerships with PharmaLogic and Eckert & Ziegler. It closed a $70 million Series C in July 2026, bringing total capital raised past $240 million. Ratio is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Sanofi
providers.description: Sanofi is a French multinational pharmaceutical and healthcare company focused on immunology, oncology, rare diseases, and vaccines, and a leading vaccines manufacturer. Sanofi does not publish a public developer API. Its GitHub organization exists but has no public repositories. The company operates patient assistance and HCP portals as well as clinical trial information services that require authenticated access.

providers.name: Satellite Bio
providers.description: Satellite Bio is a biotechnology company developing off-the-shelf liver cell therapies to treat severe and life-threatening liver diseases. Its tissue therapeutics platform engineers functional hepatocytes designed to engraft and restore liver function, combining the biological power of liver cells with scalable manufacturing and distribution. The company is headquartered in Newton, Massachusetts and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Satellite Bio is a life-sciences company and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Again
providers.description: Again is a Copenhagen-based carbon-utilization biotech spun out of research from the Danish Technical University, Stanford, and MIT. Rather than storing captured carbon, Again feeds industrial CO2 waste and hydrogen into bioreactors where AI-designed biocatalysts ferment the gas — much like brewing — into commercial-grade acetate and other green chemicals used in adhesives, solvents, plastics, textiles, cosmetics, aromas and flavors, industrial enzymes, proteins, and fertilizers. The company runs carbon-utilization facilities in Copenhagen (CPH-1), Texas City (TXS-1, with Dow and HELM AG), and Porsgrunn, Norway (NOR-1). Again raised a $43M Series A co-led by GV (Google Ventures) and HV Capital in 2024. No public developer API surface was found during API Evangelist enrichment.

providers.name: Bio-Rad Laboratories
providers.description: Bio-Rad Laboratories is a global leader in developing and manufacturing a wide range of products for the life science research and clinical diagnostic markets, including instruments, reagents, consumables, software, and services. Founded in 1952, Bio-Rad serves scientists in genomics, proteomics, cell biology, quality control, and clinical diagnostics with products like real-time PCR systems, western blotting instruments, flow cytometers, and digital PCR.

providers.name: AMPLY Discovery
providers.description: AMPLY Discovery is a UK (Belfast, Northern Ireland) biotechnology company turning the roughly 98% of the genome largely ignored by drug developers — the "dark genome" — into a pipeline of first-in-class therapeutics. The company pairs six AI/computational discovery engines with two wet labs in a closed loop between silicon and bench to find novel antimicrobial and therapeutic candidates targeting drug-resistant pathogens and complex diseases. AMPLY is a Techstars portfolio company and has been backed by Innovate UK, Invest NI, QUBIS and other UK/NI innovation programmes. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; AMPLY Discovery publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Georgiamune
providers.description: Georgiamune Inc. is a Gaithersburg, Maryland based biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class immunotherapies that reprogram immune signaling pathways to rebalance the immune system and restore health across cancer and autoimmune diseases. Built on a target-discovery platform, its pipeline of immunomodulators spans clinical, preclinical, and discovery stages, including the clinical-stage dual-functioning antibody GIM-122, the regulatory T-cell (Treg) inhibitor GIM-531, and the Treg activator GIM-407, alongside additional antibody and small-molecule programs. The company was surfaced as a venture-backed portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or programmatic interface.

providers.name: GigaCrop
providers.description: GigaCrop is an agricultural biotechnology company engineering the photosynthesis pathway to dramatically increase crop productivity. Founded by Chris Eiben, PhD, the company combines enzyme engineering and machine learning to optimize the RuBisCo enzyme, aiming to roughly double yields in staple crops such as corn and soy and to break past the limits that have held annual yield gains near one percent for a century. Backed by Playground Global, GigaCrop is working to make agriculture both more sustainable and more abundant.

providers.name: Humane Genomics
providers.description: Humane Genomics Inc is a New York City biotechnology company engineering oncolytic RNA viruses to selectively target and destroy cancer cells. Using a first-principle, computer-aided design approach built on Vesicular Stomatitis Virus (VSV) with aptazyme-controlled selective replication, the company develops precision viral therapies; its lead candidate targets pediatric liver cancer (hepatoblastoma). Backed by Union Square Ventures, Humane Genomics operates from Alexandria LaunchLabs and partners with Genezen for cGMP manufacturing. The company publishes no public API or developer surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a portfolio-company lead.

providers.name: Industrial Microbes
providers.description: Industrial Microbes (iMicrobes) is a synthetic-biology company in Alameda, California that engineers microorganisms to convert renewable, low-carbon feedstocks such as ethanol and methane into commercial-grade industrial chemicals and bio-based materials. Founded in 2014 (Y Combinator W15) by Liz Clarke, Derek Greenfield, and Noah Helman, the company has produced 100% bio-based acrylic acid and targets net-zero or negative-emission building-block chemicals for coatings, paints, carbon-fiber precursors, biopolymers, and biodegradable plastics. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Industrial Microbes publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal, so the enrichment pipeline captured only verified company identity and website link properties.

providers.name: Neoplants
providers.description: Neoplants is a French climate-biotechnology company building genetically and microbially engineered houseplants that capture and metabolize indoor air pollutants. Its consumer product line pairs bioengineered pothos plants with an enhanced root microbiome ("Power Drops") to remove volatile organic compounds such as formaldehyde, benzene, toluene and xylene from indoor air. Backed by Partech and other climate investors, Neoplants operates as a direct-to-consumer brand rather than an API provider. This API Evangelist profile was created from a venture-portfolio lead; an enrichment pass confirmed the company publishes no developer API, OpenAPI, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Pheon Therapeutics
providers.description: Pheon Therapeutics is a preclinical-stage oncology biotechnology company developing next-generation antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for a wide range of hard-to-treat solid tumors. Leveraging two decades of ADC experience, Pheon arms monoclonal antibodies against both novel and clinically validated targets with warheads from its proprietary payload platform, which offers a novel mechanism of action, or with off-the-shelf linker-payload combinations, balancing safety and efficacy for each target. The company is privately held and backed by specialist healthcare investors. Pheon publishes a corporate and scientific web presence only; it exposes no public developer API, SDKs, documentation, or well-known API discovery surface.

providers.name: Proxima
providers.description: Proxima (Proxima Bio) is a preclinical biotechnology company making protein interactions programmable through an integrated discovery platform that combines artificial intelligence, machine learning, and structural proteomics. Building on a proprietary atlas of protein cross-linking data, Proxima trains models that design proximity modulators - Inducers, Modulators, and Blockers - small-molecule therapeutics that induce or block protein-protein complexes to address cancer, autoimmune disorders, and other hard-to-treat diseases. The company is backed by DCVC and collaborates with major pharmaceutical firms. It is listed in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; as of this pass Proxima publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Regeneron
providers.description: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals is a leading biotechnology company that invents, develops, and commercializes life-transforming medicines, including EYLEA and EYLEA HD for ophthalmology, Dupixent in immunology (co-developed with Sanofi), Libtayo and Lynozyfic in oncology and hematology, and Praluent for cardiovascular disease. Regeneron does not publish a public developer API; its Regeneron Genetics Center collaborates on large-scale genomic research via the UK Biobank, DiscovEHR, and partner platforms rather than a self-hosted API.

providers.name: Revagenix
providers.description: Revagenix, Inc. is a private clinical-stage precision-therapeutics company headquartered in San Francisco, California, founded in 2019 by antibacterial-discovery veterans from Achaogen. The company takes a first-principles approach to drug design for serious chronic disease, engineering each candidate around target biology, route of delivery and tolerability. Its lead program, Rev-56, is a first-in-class inhaled precision therapy with a novel mechanism of action targeting chronic Pseudomonas infection in non-cystic-fibrosis bronchiectasis (NCFB), a progressive respiratory disease affecting an estimated 350,000 to 500,000 adults in the United States; Rev-56 is entering Phase 1 clinical development in 2026, with a dry-powder formulation approaching candidate selection. Revagenix is backed by Novo Holdings, Tenmile, the REPAIR Impact Fund and the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID contract 75N93022C00061). Revagenix is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Reven Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Reven Pharmaceuticals is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 1999 and headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado. Reven develops medicines from its proprietary RJX Technology platform - a patented, first-in-class intravenous composition of anti-oxidant and anti-inflammatory ingredients - and is advancing candidates for sepsis, multi-system inflammation, cytokine release syndrome, ARDS and vascular, oncology, CNS and ocular indications. Its lead candidate, Rejuveinix (RJX), completed a double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 dose-escalation study in healthy volunteers and received FDA clearance of an Investigational New Drug application for the treatment of COVID-19. Reven publishes a corporate and investor website at reven.com covering its pipeline, modalities, clinical trials, expanded-access program and news, but operates no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable interface of any kind.

providers.name: Ten63 Therapeutics
providers.description: Ten63 Therapeutics is an AI-driven drug-discovery company spun out of Duke University in 2019 and operating from San Francisco, Durham and Boston. It builds BEYOND, which the company describes as the world's first Large Quantum Chemistry Model — pairing generative chemistry at scale (Move37) with a quantum-accurate forcefield and molecular-dynamics engine (Astrolabe) in an approach it calls Superlearning. BEYOND is used to design therapeutics for previously undruggable and under-drugged targets, with an internal pipeline focused on oncology and platform partnerships such as the multi-target collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim. Ten63 is a therapeutics company, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract. It does publish an llms.txt describing the company and platform for AI agents.

providers.name: Tidal Vision
providers.description: Tidal Vision Products, Inc. is a Bellingham, Washington biotechnology and specialty-chemicals manufacturer, and the only commercial-scale US producer of chitosan — a non-toxic, non-hazmat, biodegradable industrial biopolymer upcycled from crab and shrimp shell waste. Its zero-waste Chitofining process extracts, modifies and formulates chitosan chemistries that displace PFAS, halogenated chemicals, toxic antimicrobials and persistent plastics across three business lines: Tidal Clear water and wastewater treatment, Tidal Grow AgriScience crop and soil inputs, and Tidal-Tec Biomaterial Science performance materials. The company closed an oversubscribed $140M+ Series B in 2025 and acquired Clear Water Services. It is a materials-science manufacturer and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: AbCellera
providers.description: AbCellera (NASDAQ: ABCL) is a Vancouver-based antibody discovery and development company that integrates biology, computation, and engineering to develop antibody-based medicines. Its technology platform combines high-throughput single-cell antibody screening, GPCR and ion-channel capabilities, bispecifics, antibody-drug conjugates, structure-based design, and AI for sequence and structure analysis. The company operates a hybrid business model with a co-development partner network (40+ partners and 100+ antibody drug programs since 2015) alongside a growing wholly-owned pipeline that includes ABCL635 (non-hormonal vasomotor symptoms), ABCL575 (atopic dermatitis), ABCL688 (autoimmunity), and ABCL386 (oncology), plus 20+ discovery programs. AbCellera does not publish a public API or developer portal; capabilities are delivered through partner collaborations and contract terms.

providers.name: Atomwise
providers.description: Atomwise pioneered the use of deep convolutional neural networks for structure-based drug discovery, with its AtomNet platform applying AI to virtual screening of small molecules against protein targets. The company ran the Artificial Intelligence Molecular Screen (AIMS) academic collaboration program, partnered with biotech and pharma companies on discovery contracts, and built an internal pipeline of small-molecule programs. As of 2026, atomwise.com redirects to Numerion Labs (numerionlabs.ai), reflecting an apparent rebrand or successor entity that positions itself as an AI superplatform exploring drug-like chemical space with programs in immune and inflammatory diseases. Atomwise never exposed a public commercial API; AtomNet screening was delivered to partners as a service. The legacy GitHub organization (github.com/atomwise) hosts no public repositories.

providers.name: Monsanto
providers.description: Monsanto was a global agricultural products company that produced seeds, biotechnology trait products, and herbicides before being acquired by Bayer AG in 2018. Operations and brands have since been integrated into the Bayer Crop Science division.

providers.name: Transition Bio
providers.description: Transition Bio is a preclinical drug discovery company built on biomolecular condensate science, operating as a joint spin-out of the University of Cambridge and Harvard University with sites in Cambridge, Massachusetts and Cambridge, United Kingdom. The company combines droplet-microfluidics high-throughput molecular screening with a machine learning engine to identify and optimize small molecules that modulate intrinsically disordered proteins and the condensates they form, an approach the company has described as its Condensomics platform. It was seeded in November 2020 and closed a $50 million Series A in June 2022 led by Northpond Ventures with Taiho Ventures, Bristol Myers Squibb and Magnetic Ventures participating, and in November 2025 announced a collaboration with Voyager Therapeutics on small molecules targeting TDP-43 in ALS and frontotemporal dementia. Transition Bio is a therapeutics developer rather than a software or data vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Abinitio Bio
providers.description: Abinitio Bio builds AI foundation models for biopharmaceutical manufacturing, positioning itself as the intelligence layer for drug manufacturing. Its first model, Echo, predicts manufacturing outcomes to assess manufacturability from day one through process scale-up — evaluating molecules early to reduce aggregation and regulatory liabilities, recommending optimal cell lines, media formulations, and bioprocess parameters, predicting process behavior across scales and operating conditions, and delivering lab-validated candidate molecules, processes, and characterization data ready for commercial scale-up. Founded in 2026 in Boston and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), MIT's Researcher-to-Entrepreneur Accelerator, and Fifty Years' 5050 Program. The company operates a B2B model with pharmaceutical companies and CDMOs and does not currently publish a public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Absci
providers.description: Absci is a Vancouver, Washington-based generative AI drug creation company (NASDAQ: ABSI) using AI and synthetic biology to design de novo antibodies in silico against specified epitopes. Its Integrated Drug Creation platform couples generative AI models — including the Origin-1 antibody foundation model — with a 77,000+ sq ft wet lab running proprietary SoluPro and ACE Assay technologies, screening millions of antibody sequence variants per cycle. The data flywheel between in silico design and high-throughput wet lab validation completes in as little as six weeks and can advance from target identification to development candidate in roughly 14 months. Absci's internal pipeline includes ABS-101, an anti-TL1A antibody for inflammatory bowel disease now in Phase 1; ABS-201, a novel anti-PRLR antibody for androgenetic alopecia in the Phase 1/2a HEADLINE trial; and ABS-301, a first-in-class AI-discovered oncology antibody. Strategic partnerships span AstraZeneca, Merck, Almirall, Twist Bioscience, NVIDIA, Owkin, Caltech, and the Gates Foundation. Absci's commercial model is therapeutic development (internal pipeline plus partnered programs and royalties); there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of the Origin-1 model or its drug creation platform.

providers.name: AgroSpheres
providers.description: AgroSpheres is an agricultural biotechnology company based in Charlottesville, Virginia, founded by University of Virginia researchers, that develops bio-based crop protection products built on its AgriCell bioparticle platform. The company uses a single-step fermentation process that produces and biodegradably encapsulates biological actives all at once, giving added stability and a tunable release profile for targeted, non-toxic pest and disease control intended to be safe for pollinators, people and soil. Its first commercial product, the broad-spectrum biofungicide FUN-THYME, is marketed through an exclusive partnership with Wilbur-Ellis and was approved in California in 2026. AgroSpheres manufactures at a biomanufacturing facility in Charlottesville. It is a physical agricultural-inputs business and publishes no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Amber Bio
providers.description: Amber Bio is a San Francisco biotechnology company developing an RNA-based gene-editing platform capable of making multi-kilobase edits — rewriting thousands of bases on a single RNA strand in one step — to reach previously undruggable patient populations. Because edited RNA eventually degrades in the body, the approach is designed to be safer and reversible compared with permanent DNA editing. The platform pairs multi-kilobase RNA writing with AI foundation models to target diverse pathogenic variants across patients with a single product, initially focused on ophthalmology and central nervous system diseases. Founded by CRISPR-field researchers from the Broad Institute and UC Berkeley (co-founder and CTO Basem Al-Shayeb, advised by Nobel Laureate Jennifer Doudna), Amber Bio launched in 2023 with a $26M seed round co-led by Playground Global and Andreessen Horowitz. It has no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Astraea
providers.description: Astraea is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) clinical trial automation platform that gives pharmaceutical sponsors, biotechs, and CROs an AI operating system for clinical development. Founded by Joshua Wang and Sanmay Sarada, the platform orchestrates specialized AI agents across the full biometrics lifecycle - standards mapping, data normalization, CDISC mapping, SDTM and ADaM dataset generation, TFLs/TLFs, SAP, eCRFs, Define-XML, QC, and submission documents - turning a protocol and raw study data into FDA-submission-ready output. Astraea is positioned as sponsor-run software rather than a CRO: it runs inside the customer's own secure environment so clinical data never reaches Astraea's servers, with 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and audit-ready, standards-native traceability. The company reports serving 10+ global pharma and biotech sponsors with 30-50% faster reporting cycles.

providers.name: Aurora Therapeutics
providers.description: Aurora Therapeutics is a CRISPR gene-editing biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing scalable, personalized genetic medicines for rare diseases. Founded by gene-editing pioneers including Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and Fyodor Urnov and led by CEO Edward M. Kaye, the company uses an "umbrella" approach that bundles multiple rare disease-causing mutations under a single regulatory pathway, combining guide RNA design, AI-engineered editors, and delivery systems to correct mutations at scale. Backed by Menlo Ventures, Aurora is profiled in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass it publishes a corporate website and news surface but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or other technical/developer surface.

providers.name: Avistone
providers.description: Beijing Avistone Biotechnology Co., Ltd. is a commercial-stage innovative biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Beijing, China, focused on the research, development, and commercialization of first-in-class and best-in-class oncology therapies. Founded in 2012 (originally Beijing Pearl Biotechnology) and renamed Avistone in 2018, the company has two approved cancer drugs on the market: Vebreltinib (万比锐®), a MET inhibitor approved for non-small cell lung cancer and glioma indications and included in China's National Reimbursement Drug List, and Andamertinib (安比锐®), an EGFR exon 20 insertion inhibitor approved in 2026 for advanced NSCLC. Avistone maintains a pipeline of additional candidates (ANS01 through ANS09) across solid-tumor indications and is backed by IDG Capital. The company publishes no public developer API or programmatic surface; this profile captures its corporate and investor identity.

providers.name: Bolt Threads
providers.description: Bolt Threads, Inc. was a San Francisco Bay Area biomaterials company founded in 2009 to engineer protein- and mycelium-based materials. It is best known for Microsilk, a bioengineered spider-silk fiber; Mylo, a mycelium-derived leather alternative developed with partners including adidas, Kering, Lululemon, Patagonia and Stella McCartney; and b-silk protein, a silk-protein ingredient for beauty and personal care. The company went public on Nasdaq in August 2024 via a SPAC business combination under the ticker BSLK, halted Mylo production, was suspended from Nasdaq in January 2026, and now trades OTC Pink while deregistering with the SEC. Its website serves only a notice that the company is no longer operating. Bolt Threads was a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor, and never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Brilliant Planet
providers.description: Brilliant Planet is a carbon-removal company that grows microalgae in open-air ponds on otherwise-unproductive coastal desert land, using seawater rather than fresh water, to sequester atmospheric carbon dioxide at scale. Harvested algal biomass is dried and stored to lock the captured carbon away durably, while the process also deacidifies the seawater it returns. The company operates research and demonstration facilities in coastal Morocco and is developing measurement, reporting, and verification approaches for its nature-based carbon capture. It is backed by Union Square Ventures and other climate-focused investors. This API Evangelist profile is a company/provider record; Brilliant Planet publishes no public developer API or documentation surface at this time (its primary web presence is access-restricted).

providers.name: C16 Biosciences
providers.description: C16 Biosciences is a New York City based synthetic biology company producing high-performance, sustainable ingredients for consumer goods manufacturers through its proprietary Palmless platform. Using microbial fermentation and biotechnology, C16 designs plant-free, deforestation-free alternatives to palm oil and petroleum-derived commodity ingredients for beauty and personal care, food, and home and personal care markets. Its flagship Palmless Torula Oil is a bioactive super-emollient with antioxidant properties for skincare formulations, alongside designer fats, oils, fatty acids, triglycerides, and alcohols. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of DCVC; it is an ingredients and biomanufacturing business and does not currently publish a public developer platform or API.

providers.name: Capacity Bio
providers.description: Capacity Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing mitophagy therapeutics to restore mitochondrial quality control in age- and disease-related conditions. Its platform advances small molecules, peptides, and nanoparticles that enhance identification and clearance of dysfunctional mitochondria. With operations in Los Angeles and Tokyo, the company closed a $35M financing round in 2023 and is backed by Insight Partners. As a drug-development firm, Capacity Bio publishes no public API, developer platform, or SDK surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Chroma Medicine
providers.description: Chroma Medicine was a Boston-based, clinical-stage biotechnology company developing epigenetic editors — CRISPR-derived medicines that silence or activate genes by writing epigenetic marks rather than cutting DNA — with CRMA-1001, a liver-targeted epigenetic editing therapy for chronic hepatitis B and hepatitis D, as its lead program. In December 2024 it merged with Nvelop Therapeutics, pairing Chroma's epigenetic editors with Nvelop's non-viral in vivo delivery vehicles, to form nChroma Bio with $75 million in new financing. chromamedicine.com now redirects to nchromabio.com. As a therapeutics developer it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: DermBiont
providers.description: DermBiont, Inc. is a Boston, Massachusetts clinical-stage dermatology therapeutics company founded in 2017 that develops targeted topical treatments addressing the root cause of skin disease rather than its symptoms. Its lead program SM-030 is a first-in-class topical PKC-beta inhibitor in development for melasma and other hyperpigmentation disorders of the skin, targeting excess melanin production; earlier programs included SM-020 for seborrheic keratosis and the live-bacterial DBI-001 and DBI-002 candidates for atopic dermatitis, tinea pedis and onychomycosis. The company describes an in-house discovery platform for microbiome-based therapeutics built on terabytes of DNA sequencing data from human skin samples across healthy individuals and patients, paired with a proprietary computational biology platform that identifies functions gained and lost by the skin microbiome. That computational platform is internal research tooling, not a product: DermBiont sells drug candidates and partnering opportunities, publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind, and its website is a Squarespace-hosted corporate site.

providers.name: Elevation Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Elevation Pharmaceuticals was a San Diego specialty pharmaceutical company founded in 2008 by Cam Garner, Bill Gerhart, and Ahmet Tutuncu to develop next-generation aerosol/inhalation therapies for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It raised a $30 million Series A in 2010 backed by Canaan Partners, TPG Growth, Care Capital, and Mesa Verde Venture Partners, and was acquired by Sunovion Pharmaceuticals in August 2012. The company is no longer independently operating; its domain now resolves to Sunovion nameservers and it publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Canaan Partners portfolio record.

providers.name: Fable Therapeutics
providers.description: Fable Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company developing protein-engineered biologics for obesity and metabolic disease. Its lead candidate, FBL-140, is an infrequently dosed monoclonal antibody antagonizing the activin receptor type II (ActR2) pathway to reduce body weight and fat while preserving lean muscle mass and improving cardiometabolic health, with clinical trials expected to begin in early 2027. The company is also advancing a combination therapy pairing ActR2 antagonism with an incretin mimetic. Fable Therapeutics is a deep-tech portfolio company backed by DCVC. It operates as a traditional drug-development company and does not currently publish any public API, developer documentation, or technical platform.

providers.name: Faircraft
providers.description: Faircraft is a biotechnology company creating a new class of cultivated materials, starting with real leather grown in the lab from animal cells rather than raised on farms. Using cell biology and protein engineering, it produces genuine leather (product lines FCL_001 through FCL_006) with the look, feel, and performance of traditional hides but with a lower environmental footprint and no animal farming, and customizable properties for fashion, automotive, and luxury brands. Backed by Kindred Ventures, Faircraft is a materials-science company with no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Formo
providers.description: Formo (Formo Foods GmbH) is a Berlin-based food-technology company producing animal-free dairy through precision fermentation and microbial fermentation of koji (Aspergillus oryzae). Instead of cows, Formo engineers microorganisms to make milk proteins such as casein, which it turns into real cheese and cream cheese products now sold across Germany and Austria. Founded by Raffael Wohlgensinger and backed by EQT Ventures, the company has received a US FDA "no questions" GRAS letter for its fermentation-derived casein. Formo is a consumer food producer and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Genvec
providers.description: GenVec was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 1992 and headquartered in Gaithersburg, Maryland, that pioneered adenovector (AdenoVerse) gene-delivery technology to develop gene-based therapeutics and vaccines, including programs for hearing loss and balance disorders. Backed by Canaan Partners, ARCH Venture Partners, EDF Ventures and HealthCare Ventures, GenVec was acquired by Precigen (formerly Intrexon) on June 16, 2017 and no longer operates as an independent company. It has no public developer platform, API, or documentation surface; the genvec.com domain no longer resolves.

providers.name: Insamo
providers.description: Insamo is a biotechnology company building membrane-permeable, orally available cyclic peptides that combine the binding affinity of antibodies with the pharmacology of small molecules for drug discovery. Its platform automates the design, synthesis, and testing of peptides at large scale and applies machine learning across vast chemical spaces to identify therapeutic candidates. Founded in February 2024 with $12M from Playground Global, venBio, and MRL Ventures Fund, the company operates from Berkeley, California and Chippendale, New South Wales, Australia. Insamo currently publishes no public developer or API surface; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Intrepida Bio
providers.description: Intrepida Bio, Inc. is a preclinical biotechnology company (founded 2019, headquartered in Encinitas / San Diego, CA) developing medicines that modulate the innate immune system to fight cancer and other diseases. Working with Biouniversa s.r.l., the company holds worldwide rights to develop proprietary monoclonal antibodies against the novel targets BAG3 and its receptor IFITM-2 — a signaling axis tumors hijack to build a growth-promoting, immune-evasive microenvironment (notably in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, PDAC). Intrepida raised roughly $9.5M from Canaan, Sofinnova, Indaco Venture Partners and Vertis to fund IND-enabling studies of its lead oncology program. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. NOTE: this is a therapeutics/drug-discovery company with no public API, developer portal, or software product surface; its website (intrepidabio.com) no longer resolves and the entity appears dormant/defunct, so no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: Mammoth Biosciences
providers.description: Mammoth Biosciences is a genetic medicines company co-founded by CRISPR co-inventor Jennifer Doudna, developing in vivo gene-editing therapeutics and CRISPR-based diagnostics. The company discovers and engineers novel CRISPR systems and proteins to overcome delivery challenges in genetic medicine, with the goal of creating permanent cures. It is a therapeutics- and diagnostics-focused biotechnology company rather than an API/platform provider; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or programmatic access. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc, Mayfield and SV Angel and added to the API Evangelist network.
